Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读

In 1924 America's National Research Council sent two engineers to supervise a series of experiments at a telephone-parts factory called the Hawthorne Plant near Chicago. It hoped they would learn how shop-floor lighting 1 workers' productivity. Instead, the studies ended 2 giving their name to the "Hawthorne effect," the extremely influential idea that the very 3 of being experimented upon changed subjects' behavior.

1924年，美国国家研究委员会派两名工程师到芝加哥附近一家名为霍桑工厂的电话配件厂去监督一系列实验。委员会本希望他们能弄清车间照明是如何影响工人生产率的。然而，这些研究最终却得出了一个以"霍桑效应"命名的结论——这一极具影响力的观点认为，仅仅是成为实验对象这一行为本身就会改变受试者的行为。

The idea arose because of the 4 behavior of the women in the plant. According to 5 of the experiments, their hourly output rose when lighting was increased, but also when it was dimmed. It did not 6 what was done in the experiment; 7 something was changed, productivity rose. A(n) 8 that they were being experimented upon seemed to be 9 to alter workers' behavior 10 itself.

这一观点的产生源于工厂里女工们令人困惑的行为。根据实验记录，照明增强时她们每小时的产量会提高，照明减弱时产量同样提高。实验中做了什么似乎并不重要；只要有所改变，生产率就会提高。女工们意识到自己正在接受实验，这一意识本身似乎就足以改变她们的行为。

After several decades, the same data were 11 to econometric analysis. The Hawthorne experiments had another surprise in store. 12 the descriptions on record, no systematic 13 was found that levels of productivity were related to changes in lighting.

几十年后，同样的数据被用于计量经济学分析。霍桑实验还藏着另一个意外。与之前记录的描述相反，人们没有发现系统的证据表明生产率水平与照明变化有关。

It turns out that the peculiar way of conducting the experiments may have led to 14 interpretations of what happened. 15, lighting was always changed on a Sunday. When work started again on Monday, output 16 rose compared with the previous Saturday and 17 to rise for the next couple of days. 18, a comparison with data for weeks when there was no experimentation showed that output always went up on Mondays. Workers 19 to be diligent for the first few days of the week in any case, before 20 a plateau and then slackening off. This suggests that the alleged "Hawthorne effect" is hard to pin down.

结果表明，当时开展实验的奇特方式可能导致了对所发生事情的误导性解读。例如，照明总是在周日改变。周一重新开工时，与上周六相比产量如期上升，并在接下来几天持续增长。然而，与没有进行实验的几周数据对比后发现，产量在周一总是会上升。无论如何，工人们在一周的头几天总是很卖力，达到平台期后才松懈下来。这表明所谓的"霍桑效应"难以确凿证实。

⚠️ 完形总结本文是2010年最难的一篇完形，讲霍桑效应被推翻。关键考点：逻辑关系（7/12/15/18）+ 固定搭配（end up/by itself/be subjected to/hit a plateau）。
Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

Of all the changes that have taken place in English-language newspapers during the past quarter-century, perhaps the most far-reaching has been the inexorable decline in the scope and seriousness of their arts coverage.

在过去四分之一个世纪里，英文报纸所发生的所有变化中，影响最为深远的或许是其艺术报道的范围在不断缩小、严肃性在不断减弱，且这一趋势不可阻挡。

It is difficult to the point of impossibility for the average reader under the age of forty to imagine a time when high-quality arts criticism could be found in most big-city newspapers. Yet a considerable number of the most significant collections of criticism published in the 20th century consisted in large part of newspaper reviews. To read such books today is to marvel at the fact that their learned contents were once deemed suitable for publication in general-circulation dailies.

对于40岁以下的普通读者来说，他们几乎无法想象曾经有一段时期，在大多数大城市的报纸上都能读到高质量的艺术评论。然而，在20世纪出版的最重要的批评文集中，有相当大一部分是由报纸评论组成的。今天再读这类文集，人们会惊叹于这样一个事实：那些广博深奥的内容竟然曾被认为适合登在面向大众的日报上。

We are even farther removed from the unfocused newspaper reviews published in England between the turn of the 20th century and the eve of World War II, at a time when newsprint was dirt-cheap and stylish arts criticism was considered an ornament to the publications in which it appeared. In those far-off days, it was taken for granted that the critics of major papers would write in detail and at length about the events they covered. Theirs was a serious business, and even those reviewers who wore their learning lightly, like George Bernard Shaw and Ernest Newman, could be trusted to know what they were about. These men believed in journalism as a calling, and were proud to be published in the daily press. "So few authors have brains enough or literary gift enough to keep their own end up in journalism," Newman wrote, "that I am tempted to define 'journalism' as 'a term of contempt applied by writers who are not read to writers who are'."

我们离20世纪初至二战前夕英国报纸上那种主题自由的评论甚至更远了——当时新闻纸极其便宜，时尚的艺术评论被视为报刊的装饰。在那些遥远的日子里，人们理所当然地认为，大报的评论家会对自己报道的事件进行详尽而充分的论述。评论在当时是一件严肃的事，即使是像萧伯纳和欧内斯特·纽曼那样不炫耀学问的评论家，人们也相信他们清楚自己在做什么。这些人把新闻业视为一种使命，并为自己的文章能登在日报上而自豪。纽曼写道："有足够头脑或文学天赋把新闻业坚持到底的作家是如此之少，以至于我忍不住想把'新闻业'定义为一个'没人读的作家用来骂有人读的作家的蔑称'。"

Unfortunately, these critics are virtually forgotten. Neville Cardus, who wrote for the Manchester Guardian from 1917 until shortly before his death in 1975, is now known solely as a writer of essays on the game of cricket. During his lifetime, though, he was also one of England's foremost classical-music critics, and a stylist so widely admired that his Autobiography (1947) became a best-seller. He was knighted in 1967, the first music critic to be so honored. Yet only one of his books is now in print, and his vast body of writings on music is unknown save to specialists.

遗憾的是，这些评论家几乎已被遗忘。内维尔·卡德斯从1917年到1975年去世前不久一直为《曼彻斯特卫报》撰稿，如今他仅仅以板球随笔作家的身份为人所知。然而在他生前，他还是英国最重要的古典音乐评论家之一，也是广受推崇的文体家，其《自传》（1947年）曾成为畅销书。他于1967年被封为爵士，是第一位获此殊荣的音乐评论家。然而如今他的著作中只有一本仍在印行，他那大量关于音乐的著述除专业人士外已无人知晓。

Is there any chance that Cardus's criticism will enjoy a revival? The prospect seems remote. Journalistic tastes had changed long before his death, and postmodern readers have little use for the richly upholstered Vicwardian prose in which he specialized. Moreover, the amateur tradition in music criticism has been in headlong retreat.

卡德斯的评论还有复兴的可能吗？前景似乎渺茫。早在他去世之前，新闻业的品味就已改变，后现代读者对他所擅长的那种辞藻华丽的维多利亚—爱德华时代散文几乎不感兴趣。此外，音乐评论中的业余传统也一直在迅速衰落。

细节推断题
答案 B
It is indicated in Paragraphs 1 and 2 that ___.第 1 段和第 2 段表明___。
[A] arts criticism has disappeared from big-city newspapers艺术评论已从大都市报纸上消失
[B] English-language newspapers used to carry more arts reviews
[C] high-quality newspapers retain a large body of readers高质量报纸保有一大批读者
[D] young readers doubt the suitability of criticism on dailies年轻读者怀疑日报评论的恰当性
💡 考场思路首段说 arts coverage 的 scope 和 seriousness 在 inexorable decline（不可阻挡地衰落），第二段说过去大城市报上能读到高质量评论——反推：过去报纸有更多艺术评论。
逐项分析 [A] 艺术评论已从大报消失 → 偷换，原文是 decline 不是 disappeared；
[B] 英文报过去有更多艺术评论 → 正确，decline 反推过去更多；
[C] 高质量报纸仍有大量读者 → 无中生有；
[D] 年轻读者怀疑评论适合登日报 → 无中生有，原文是今天的人 marvel at。

Text 2   商业方法专利面临威胁（26–30）

Over the past decade, thousands of patents have been granted for what are called business methods. Amazon.com received one for its "one-click" online payment system. Merrill Lynch got legal protection for an asset allocation strategy. One inventor patented a technique for lifting a box.

在过去十年里，数千项所谓的商业方法被授予了专利。亚马逊公司因其"一键式"在线支付系统获得了一项专利。美林证券公司的一项资产配置策略获得了法律保护。还有一位发明家为一项提箱子的技术申请了专利。

Now the nation's top patent court appears completely ready to scale back on business-method patents, which have been controversial ever since they were first authorized 10 years ago. In a move that has intellectual-property lawyers abuzz, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit said it would use a particular case to conduct a broad review of business-method patents. In re Bilski, as the case is known, is "a very big deal," says Dennis D. Crouch of the University of Missouri School of Law. It "has the potential to eliminate an entire class of patents."

如今，美国最高专利法院似乎已准备好全面缩减商业方法专利的规模——这类专利自10年前首次获批以来就一直备受争议。美国联邦巡回上诉法院表示将利用某个特定案件对商业方法专利展开广泛复审，这一举动让知识产权律师们议论纷纷。密苏里大学法学院的丹尼斯·克劳奇说，这起被称为"比尔斯基案"的官司"事关重大"，它"有可能导致一整类专利被撤销"。

Curbs on business-method claims would be a dramatic about-face, because it was the Federal Circuit itself that introduced such patents with its 1998 decision in the so-called State Street Bank case, approving a patent on a way of pooling mutual-fund assets. That ruling produced an explosion in business-method patent filings, initially by emerging Internet companies trying to stake out exclusive rights to specific types of online transactions. Later, more established companies raced to add such patents to their files, if only as a defensive move against rivals that might beat them to the punch. In 2005, IBM noted in a court filing that it had been issued more than 300 business-method patents, despite the fact that it questioned the legal basis for granting them. Similarly, some Wall Street investment firms armed themselves with patents for financial products, even as they took positions in court cases opposing the practice.

对商业方法专利申请的限制将是一次戏剧性的大转弯，因为正是联邦巡回法院自己在1998年所谓的美国道富银行案中引入了这类专利，批准了一项汇集共同基金资产方法的专利。那项裁决引发了商业方法专利申请的激增，起初是新兴的互联网公司试图为特定类型的在线交易抢占独家权利。后来，更老牌的公司也竞相将此类专利收入囊中——哪怕只是作为一种防御性举措，以防竞争对手抢先一步。2005年，IBM在一份法庭文件中称，自己已被授予300多项商业方法专利，尽管它本身就质疑授予这些专利的法律依据。同样，一些华尔街投资公司也用金融产品专利来武装自己，即便它们在法庭案件中反对这种做法。

The Bilski case involves a claimed patent on a method for hedging risk in the energy market. The Federal Circuit issued an unusual order stating that the case would be heard by all 12 of the court's judges, rather than a typical panel of three, and that one issue it wants to evaluate is whether it should "reconsider" its State Street Bank ruling.

比尔斯基案涉及一项能源市场风险对冲方法的专利申请。联邦巡回法院发布了一项不同寻常的命令，要求该案由法院全部12名法官而非典型的三人合议庭审理，并且它要评估的一个问题是：是否应当"重新考虑"其道富银行案的裁决。

The Federal Circuit's action comes in the wake of a series of recent decisions by the Supreme Court that has narrowed the scope of protections for patent holders. Last April, for example, the justices signaled that too many patents were being upheld for "inventions" that are obvious. The judges on the Federal Circuit are "reacting to the anti-patent trend at the Supreme Court," says Harold C. Wegner, a patent attorney and professor at George Washington University Law School.

联邦巡回法院的此举是在最高法院最近一系列缩小专利持有人保护范围的裁决之后做出的。例如，去年4月，法官们发出信号：太多显而易见的"发明"被授予了专利。乔治华盛顿大学法学院专利律师哈罗德·韦格纳教授说，联邦巡回法院的法官们正在"对最高法院的反专利趋势做出回应"。

Text 3   社会潮流传播与有影响力者（31–35）

In his book The Tipping Point, Malcolm Gladwell argues that "social epidemics" are driven in large part by the actions of a tiny minority of special individuals, often called influentials, who are unusually informed, persuasive, or well connected. The idea is intuitively compelling, but it doesn't explain how ideas actually spread.

马尔科姆·格拉德威尔在其《引爆点》一书中认为，"社会潮流"在很大程度上由极少数特殊人物的行为所推动，这些人通常被称为有影响力者，他们见多识广、能言善辩或人脉广阔。这一观点在直觉上很有说服力，但它并没有解释观念实际上是如何传播的。

The supposed importance of influentials derives from a plausible-sounding but largely untested theory called the "two-step flow of communication": Information flows from the media to the influentials and from them to everyone else. Marketers have embraced the two-step flow because it suggests that if they can just find and influence the influentials, those select people will do most of the work for them. The theory also seems to explain the sudden and unexpected popularity of certain looks, brands, or neighborhoods. In many such cases, a cursory search finds that some small group of people was wearing, promoting, or developing whatever it is before anyone else paid attention. Anecdotal evidence of this kind fits nicely with the idea that only certain special people can drive trends.

有影响力者的所谓重要性源自一个听起来合理但基本未经验证的理论——"两级传播论"：信息从媒体流向有影响力者，再从他们流向其他人。营销人员欣然接受这一理论，因为它表明，只要能找到有影响力者并影响他们，这些精选出来的人就会替他们完成大部分工作。这一理论似乎也能解释某些打扮、品牌或街区为何突然出乎意料地流行。在许多此类案例中，粗略调查就会发现，某一小群人总是在别人注意到之前就已经在穿戴、推广或开发某种东西了。这种传闻证据恰好契合了"只有某些特殊人物才能推动潮流"的观点。

In their recent work, however, some researchers have come up with the finding that influentials have far less impact on social epidemics than is generally supposed. In fact, they don't seem to be required at all.

然而，一些研究人员在最近的研究中发现，有影响力者对社会潮流的影响远没有人们普遍认为的那么大。事实上，社会潮流似乎根本不需要他们。

The researchers' argument stems from a simple observation about social influence: With the exception of a few celebrities like Oprah Winfrey—whose outsize presence is primarily a function of media, not interpersonal, influence—even the most influential members of a population simply don't interact with that many others. Yet it is precisely these non-celebrity influentials who, according to the two-step-flow theory, are supposed to drive social epidemics by influencing their friends and colleagues directly. For a social epidemic to occur, however, each person so affected must then influence his or her own acquaintances, who must in turn influence theirs, and so on; and just how many others pay attention to each of these people has little to do with the initial influential. If people in the network just two degrees removed from the initial influential prove resistant, for example, the cascade of change won't propagate very far or affect many people.

研究人员的论点源于对社会影响的一个简单观察：除了像奥普拉·温弗瑞这样少数名人之外——她的巨大影响力主要来自媒体而非人际影响——即使是人群中最有影响力的人，其交往对象也并没有那么多。然而，根据两级传播论，恰恰是这些非名人有影响力者，本应通过直接影响朋友和同事来推动社会潮流。然而，要形成社会潮流，每一个受到影响的人都必须再去影响自己的熟人，这些熟人又必须去影响他们的熟人，如此层层传递；而究竟有多少人会关注这些人中的每一个，与最初那个有影响力者几乎毫无关系。例如，如果传播网络中与最初有影响力者相隔两个层级的人表现出抵制，那么变化的连锁反应就不会传播很远，也不会影响很多人。

Building on the basic truth about interpersonal influence, the researchers studied the dynamics of social influence by conducting thousands of computer simulations of populations, manipulating a number of variables relating to people's ability to influence others and their tendency to be influenced. They found that the principal requirement for what is called "global cascades"—the widespread propagation of influence through networks—is the presence not of a few influentials but, rather, of a critical mass of easily influenced people.

基于人际影响这一基本事实，研究人员对人群进行了数千次计算机模拟，操纵了与人们影响他人的能力以及受他人影响的倾向相关的若干变量，由此研究社会影响的动态。他们发现，所谓"全球连锁反应"（即影响通过网络广泛传播）的主要前提，不是少数有影响力者的存在，而是一大群容易受影响的人的存在。

Text 4   银行与会计准则制定者的冲突（36–40）

Bankers have been blaming themselves for their troubles in public. Behind the scenes, they have been taking aim at someone else: the accounting standard-setters. Their rules, moan the banks, have forced them to report enormous losses, and it's just not fair. These rules say they must value some assets at the price a third party would pay, not the price managers and regulators would like them to fetch.

公开场合，银行家们一直把自己的麻烦归咎于自己。但私下里，他们却把矛头对准了别人：会计准则制定者。银行抱怨说，这些准则迫使他们报告巨额损失，而这太不公平了。准则规定，他们必须按第三方愿意支付的价格来评估某些资产，而不是按经理人和监管者希望这些资产能卖得的价格来评估。

Unfortunately, banks' lobbying now seems to be working. The details may be unknowable, but the independence of standard-setters, essential to the proper functioning of capital markets, is being compromised. And, unless banks carry toxic assets at prices that attract buyers, reviving the banking system will be difficult.

不幸的是，银行的游说如今似乎奏效了。具体细节或许无从得知，但对资本市场正常运作至关重要的准则制定者的独立性正在受到损害。而且，除非银行能按吸引买家的价格处置不良资产，否则银行体系的复苏将举步维艰。

After a bruising encounter with Congress, America's Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) rushed through rule changes. These gave banks more freedom to use models to value illiquid assets and more flexibility in recognizing losses on long-term assets in their income statements. Bob Herz, the FASB's chairman, cried out against those who "question our motives." Yet bank shares rose and the changes enhance what one lobby group politely calls "the use of judgment by management."

在与国会发生一场激烈冲突之后，美国财务会计准则委员会（FASB）匆匆通过了准则修改。修改后，银行在使用模型评估非流动资产方面拥有了更大自由，在损益表中确认长期资产损失时也有了更大弹性。FASB主席鲍勃·赫茨强烈斥责那些"质疑我们动机"的人。然而，银行股价上涨了，而这些修改强化了某游说团体委婉称之为"管理层运用自由裁量"的东西。

European ministers instantly demanded that the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) do likewise. The IASB says it does not want to act without overall planning, but the pressure to fold when it completes its reconstruction of rules later this year is strong. Charlie McCreevy, a European commissioner, warned the IASB that it did "not live in a political vacuum" but "in the real world" and that Europe could yet develop different rules.

欧洲各国部长立即要求国际会计准则理事会（IASB）照做。IASB表示，它不想在没有整体规划的情况下贸然行动，但在今年晚些时候完成准则重建时，其面临的屈服压力十分巨大。欧盟委员查理·麦克里夫警告IASB说，它"并非生活在政治真空中"，而是"生活在现实世界里"，欧洲最终可能制定出不同的准则。

It was banks that were on the wrong planet, with accounts that vastly overvalued assets. Today they argue that market prices overstate losses, because they largely reflect the temporary illiquidity of markets, not the likely extent of bad debts. The truth will not be known for years. But banks' shares trade below their book value, suggesting that investors are skeptical. And dead markets partly reflect the paralysis of banks which will not sell assets for fear of booking losses, yet are reluctant to buy all those supposed bargains.

真正站在错误立场上的是银行，它们的账目严重高估了资产。如今它们辩称，市场价格夸大了损失，因为这些价格主要反映的是市场暂时的非流动性，而不是坏账可能达到的程度。真相如何，多年后才能知晓。但银行股价低于其账面价值，表明投资者持怀疑态度。而死寂的市场在一定程度上反映了银行的瘫痪：它们因害怕把损失入账而不愿出售资产，却又不愿买进那些所谓的便宜货。

To get the system working again, losses must be recognized and dealt with. America's new plan to buy up toxic assets will not work unless banks mark assets to levels which buyers find attractive. Successful markets require independent and even combative standard-setters. The FASB and IASB have been exactly that, cleaning up rules on stock options and pensions, for example, against hostility from special interests. But by giving in to critics now they are inviting pressure to make more concessions.

要让系统重新运转，就必须承认损失并加以处理。美国收购不良资产的新计划不会奏效，除非银行把资产价格标到买家觉得有吸引力的水平。成功的市场需要独立、甚至富有斗争精神的准则制定者。FASB和IASB过去一直正是如此——例如，它们不顾特殊利益集团的敌意，清理了股票期权和养老金方面的准则。但如今向批评者让步，它们就是在招致要求做出更多让步的压力。

The author's attitude towards standard-setters is one of ___.作者对标准制定者的态度是___之一。

[C] objectiveness.客观。
[D] sympathy.
💡 考场思路末段说 successful markets require independent and even combative standard-setters，又说它们giving in to critics是在招致压力——作者同情被银行游说施压的准则制定者。
核心词汇
take aim at 瞄准/批评
moan v. 抱怨
compromise v. 损害
toxic assets 不良资产
illiquid adj. 非流动的
book value 账面价值
combative adj. 好斗的
concession n. 让步
Part B · 新题型七选五（41–45）

【题目】阅读关于欧洲食品饮料批发市场的文章，从A–G中选出最合适的段落填入41–45，使文章连贯。E段已就位。

已知首段大意：欧洲食品饮料零售市场已停滞，零售商纷纷尝试电商和海外扩张却收效甚微，几乎都忽略了身后那片大而有利可图的机会——批发业务。

E段（已就位）：尽管细节各异，法、德、意、西等国批发市场由相同构件组成。需求来自两类：独立夫妻店（太小无法直接向生产商采购）和食品服务运营商（自动售货机到大型餐饮）。业内称hoReCa（酒店、餐厅、咖啡馆）。欧洲食品饮料批发整体增速与零售一样缓慢，但加总后掩盖了两种相反趋势。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
The first and more important is the consumer's growing preference for eating out; the consumption of food and drink in places other than homes has risen from about 32 percent of total consumption in 1995 to 35 percent in 2000 and is expected to approach 38 percent by 2005. This development is boosting wholesale demand from the food service segment by 4 to 5 percent a year across Europe, compared with growth in retail demand of 1 to 2 percent. Meanwhile, as the recession is looming large, people are getting anxious. They tend to keep a tighter hold on their purse and consider eating at home a realistic alternative.
首先也是更重要的一点是，消费者越来越倾向于外出就餐；在家庭以外场所的饮食消费占全部消费的比重，已从1995年的约32%升至2000年的35%，并有望在2005年接近38%。这一趋势正使欧洲餐饮服务板块的批发需求每年增长4%到5%，而零售需求仅增长1%到2%。与此同时，随着经济衰退逼近，人们日益焦虑，更倾向于捂紧钱包，把在家吃饭视为现实的选择。
B
Retail sales of food and drink in Europe's largest markets are at a standstill, leaving European grocery retailers hungry for opportunities to grow. Most leading retailers have already tried e-commerce, with limited success, and expansion abroad. But almost all have ignored the big, profitable opportunity in their own backyard: the wholesale food and drink trade, which appears to be just the kind of market retailers need.
欧洲最大市场的食品饮料零售销售陷入停滞，令欧洲食品零售商渴求增长机会。多数领军零售商已试水电商（成效有限）并开拓海外，但几乎都忽视了自己后院里那块巨大且盈利的可乘之机——食品饮料批发业务，而这恰恰是零售商所需要的那种市场。
C
Will such variations bring about a change in the overall structure of the food and drink market? Definitely not. The functioning of the market is based on flexible trends dominated by potential buyers. In other words, it is up to the buyer, rather than the seller, to decide what to buy. At any rate, this change will ultimately be acclaimed by an ever-growing number of both domestic and international consumers, regardless of how long the current consumer pattern will take hold.
这些变化会改变食品饮料市场的整体结构吗？绝对不会。市场的运转建立在由潜在买家主导的灵活趋势之上。换言之，买什么由买家而非卖家决定。无论如何，无论当前的消费模式还会维持多久，这一变化最终都会受到越来越多国内外消费者的欢迎。
D
All in all, this clearly seems to be a market in which big retailers could profitably apply their scale, existing infrastructure and proven skills in the management of product ranges, logistics, and marketing intelligence. Retailers that master the intricacies of wholesaling in Europe may well expect to rake in substantial profits thereby. At least, that is how it looks as a whole. Closer inspection reveals important differences among the biggest national markets, especially in their customer segments and wholesale structures, as well as the competitive dynamics of individual food and drink categories. Big retailers must understand these differences before they can identify the segments of European wholesaling in which their particular abilities might unseat smaller but entrenched competitors. New skills and unfamiliar business models are needed too.
总而言之，这显然看似是一个大型零售商能有利可图地施展其规模、现有基础设施以及在商品组合、物流和营销情报管理方面成熟经验的市场。能掌握欧洲批发业门道的零售商大可期望从中获取丰厚利润。至少整体看来如此。细察之下，各大民族市场之间存在重要差异，尤其体现在客户群与批发结构，以及各食品饮料品类的竞争态势上。大型零售商必须先理解这些差异，才能找准欧洲批发业中那些其独特能力足以撼动规模较小却根基稳固的竞争者的细分领域。同时还需要新技能和不熟悉的商业模式。
E
Despite variations in detail, wholesale markets in the countries that have been closely examined—France, Germany, Italy, and Spain—are made out of the same building blocks. Demand comes mainly from two sources: independent mom-and-pop grocery stores which, unlike large retail chains, are too small to buy straight from producers, and food service operators that cater to consumers when they don't eat at home. Such food service operators range from snack machines to large institutional catering ventures, but most of these businesses are known in the trade as "horeca": hotels, restaurants, and cafes. Overall, Europe's wholesale market for food and drink is growing at the same sluggish pace as the retail market, but the figures, when added together, mask two opposing trends.
尽管细节有别，法国、德国、意大利和西班牙等被仔细研究过的国家，其批发市场由相同的构件组成。需求主要来自两类：一是独立夫妻杂货店（与大型零售连锁不同，它们规模太小，无法直接向生产商采购），二是在人们不在家吃饭时为其提供餐饮服务的运营商。这类餐饮运营商从自动零食机到大型机构餐饮企业不一而足，但业内大多称其为"horeca"：酒店、餐厅和咖啡馆。总体而言，欧洲食品饮料批发市场的增速与零售市场同样迟缓，但把数据加总后，却掩盖了两种相反的趋势。
F
For example, wholesale food and drink sales come to $268 billion in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom in 2000—more than 40 percent of retail sales. Moreover, average overall margins are higher in wholesale than in retail; wholesale demand from the food service sector is growing quickly as more Europeans eat out more often; and changes in the competitive dynamics of this fragmented industry are at last making it feasible for wholesalers to consolidate.
例如，2000年法、德、意、西、英五国的食品饮料批发销售额达2680亿美元——超过零售额的40%。此外，批发的平均整体利润率高于零售；随着更多欧洲人更频繁地外出就餐，餐饮服务板块的批发需求快速增长；而这一零散行业竞争态势的变化，终于使批发商整合成为可能。
G
However, none of these requirements should deter large retailers (and even some large good producers and existing wholesalers) from trying their hand, for those that master the intricacies of wholesaling in Europe stand to reap considerable gains.
然而，这些要求都不应吓退大型零售商（乃至一些大型食品生产商和现有批发商）去一试身手，因为那些掌握欧洲批发业门道者必将获得可观收益。
41
段落匹配题
答案 B
匹配依据[B] 欧洲最大市场食品饮料零售停滞，零售商急于寻找增长机会，几乎都忽略了身后批发这块大蛋糕。→ 承接首段"零售商忽略批发"，引出批发话题。
42
段落匹配题
答案 F
匹配依据[F] 例如，2000年法德意西英五国批发额达2680亿美元，超过零售40%；批发利润率更高；外出就餐使食品服务批发需求快速增长，行业整合成为可能。→ 用数据论证批发市场之大、之有利可图。
43
段落匹配题
答案 D
匹配依据[D] 总之，大零售商可凭规模、基础设施和产品管理专长在批发业获利；但仔细看各大国家市场在客户群、批发结构和品类竞争上存在重要差异，必须先理解这些差异才能找到用武之地，也需要新技能和不熟的商业模式。→ 承上启下，从"批发有利可图"转向"各国市场有差异"，末句"differences"直接引出E段"Despite variations in detail..."。
44
段落匹配题
答案 G
匹配依据[G] 然而，这些要求都不应吓退大型零售商（乃至大型食品生产商和现有批发商），那些掌握欧洲批发门道的人将获得可观收益。→ 回应D段末句"需要新技能和不熟悉的商业模式"，"these requirements"指代D段提到的种种门槛。
45
段落匹配题
答案 A
匹配依据[A] 第一个也是更重要的趋势是消费者越来越偏好外出就餐；家外食品饮料消费占比从1995年32%升至2005年35%，预计2008年达38%。→ E段末句说"两个相反趋势"，A段开头"The first and more important is..."直接承接。
干扰项[C] 问这些变化是否改变整体市场结构——答"不，买家决定一切"（本文未讨论市场结构是否改变，偏离主线）。
Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）
46
翻译
Scientists jumped to the rescue with some distinctly shaky evidence to the effect that insects would eat us up if birds failed to control them.
科学家们急忙介入，但提出的证据显然站不住脚，其大意是：如果鸟类不能控制昆虫数量，昆虫便会吞噬我们人类。
采分点① jump to the rescue 急忙赶来救援（意译）；② distinctly shaky evidence 明显站不住脚的证据；③ to the effect that 大意是/意思是（固定短语，高频考点）。
47
翻译
but we have at least drawn nearer the point of admitting that birds should continue as a matter of intrinsic right, regardless of the presence or absence of economic advantage to us.
但是我们至少已经近乎承认，鸟类无论对我们有无经济价值，都应继续生存下去，这是它们固有的权利。
采分点① draw nearer the point of 近乎/接近……这一步；② intrinsic right 固有权利；③ regardless of 不管；④ the presence or absence of 有无。
48
翻译
Time was when biologists somewhat overworked the evidence that these creatures preserve the health of game by killing the physically weak, or that they prey only on "worthless" species.
曾经有段时间，生物学家有点过重地使用了这样的证据：这些生物通过猎杀体弱的动物来保持猎物种群的健康，或者说它们捕食的只是"没有价值"的物种。
采分点① Time was when… 曾经有段时间（=There was a time when）；② overwork 过度使用；③ game 猎物（熟词僻义）；④ prey on 捕食。
49
翻译
In Europe, where forestry is ecologically more advanced, the noncommercial tree species are recognized as members of the native forest community, to be preserved as such, within reason.
在欧洲，林业在生态上更为先进，那些没有商业价值的树种被视为原始森林群落的成员，因而受到相应的保护，而且是在合理范围之内。
采分点① ecologically more advanced 生态上更先进；② noncommercial 无商业价值的；③ as such 照此/本身；④ within reason 合理地。
50
翻译
It tends to ignore, and thus eventually to eliminate, many elements in the land community that lack commercial value, but that are essential to its healthy functioning.
这一体系往往会忽视并最终消灭陆地群落中许多缺乏商业价值、但对其健康运行却至关重要的物种。
采分点① tend to 往往；② eliminate 消灭；③ 两个that并列定语从句修饰elements，注意but转折；④ healthy functioning 健康运行。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 招募志愿者通知

原题指令 Directions

Suppose you are a member of the Postgraduates' Association. Write a notice to recruit volunteers for an international conference on globalization. The notice should include the basic qualifications of the applicants and other information you think relevant. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the notice. Use "Postgraduates' Association" instead.

【译文】假设你代表研究生会。写一则通知，为一场关于全球化的国际会议招募志愿者。通知应包含申请者的基本条件以及其他你认为相关的信息。字数约100词。通知末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“研究生会”落款。

题目

代表研究生会写一则通知，为一场关于全球化的国际会议招募志愿者。内容应包括申请者的基本资格以及其他你认为相关的信息。约100词，落款用"Postgraduates' Association"。

审题

① 格式：通知（notice），标题居中，落款组织；② 内容：会议时间地点+招募条件（英语好、沟通能力、相关经验、时间充裕）+ 报名方式；③ 语气：正式但友好。

参考范文

Notice

An International Conference on Globalization will be held on our campus from January 15 to 17. To ensure its smooth running, the Postgraduates' Association is now recruiting 30 volunteers.

Ideal candidates should meet the following requirements. First and foremost, a good command of spoken English is essential, since most participants come from overseas. Second, those with previous volunteer experience will be given priority. Third, applicants must be available to work full-time throughout the conference.

Those interested may sign up at the Postgraduates' Association office before January 8. We look forward to your active participation.

Postgraduates' Association

【译文】

通知

一场以全球化为主题的国际研讨会将于1月15日至17日在我校举行。为保障会议顺利进行，研究生会现招募30名志愿者。

理想人选应符合以下条件：首先，英语口语流利至关重要，因为多数与会者来自海外；其次，有志愿服务经历者优先；最后，申请者需在会议期间能够全职到岗。

有意者请于1月8日前到研究生会办公室报名。期待你的积极参与。

研究生会

Part B 大作文（20分）— 文化"火锅"，既美味又营养

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The drawing shows a hotpot in which various ingredients are boiling, with Chinese and foreign cultural symbols written on them, such as "Shenzhou", "Confucius", "Einstein", "Lao She", "Shakespeare", "deconstruction", "enlightenment", "humanism", "Buddhism", "Taoism", etc. The caption reads: Cultural "hotpot" — both delicious and nutritious.

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 图画展示了一口火锅，里面煮着各种“食材”，锅上写着中外文化符号，如“神舟”“孔子”“爱因斯坦”“老舍”“莎士比亚”“解构”“启蒙”“人本”“佛”“道”等。下方文字：文化“火锅”，既美味又营养。

图画描述

图画中一个火锅里煮着许多食材，上面写着"Shenzhou""Confucius""Einstein""解构""天鹅湖""老舍""解构""启蒙""人本""行为""儒""道""佛""莎士比亚""后现代""网络"等中外文化符号。下方文字：文化"火锅"，既美味又营养。

审题框架

三段式：①简要描述图画（火锅里的中外文化元素）；②阐释寓意（文化融合是当今时代趋势，既美味又营养）；③给出评论（我们应欢迎文化交流、取精去糟）。160-200词。

参考范文

The vivid illustration portrays a simmering hotpot brimming with a rich assortment of cultural ingredients, ranging from Confucius and Shakespeare to postmodernism and Beijing Opera. Below the picture sits a line of caption: the cultural "hotpot" is both delicious and nutritious.

What this drawing conveys is truly thought-provoking. As globalization deepens, cultures across the world are mingling and blending at an unprecedented pace. The hotpot serves as a perfect metaphor: just as assorted ingredients combine to make a tasty soup, Eastern and Western cultures, once fused, nourish the spirit of modern people. Cultural integration not only enriches our daily lives but also fosters mutual understanding among nations.

From my perspective, this trend is both inevitable and beneficial. On the one hand, we should take pride in and preserve our own cultural heritage; on the other hand, we should embrace the essence of foreign cultures with an open mind. Only by absorbing the best of both worlds can we truly savor a delicious and nutritious cultural feast.

【译文】

生动的图画描绘了一只沸腾的火锅，里面煮着五花八门的文化"食材"，从孔子、莎士比亚到后现代主义和京剧，应有尽有。图画下方有一行文字：文化"火锅"，既美味又营养。

这幅画所传达的意涵发人深省。随着全球化深入，世界各地的文化正以空前的速度交融汇合。火锅是个绝妙的比喻：正如各种食材融合成一锅好汤，中西文化一旦结合，便滋养着现代人的精神。文化融合不仅丰富我们的日常生活，也促进各国人民之间的相互理解。

在我看来，这一趋势既不可阻挡，也大有裨益。一方面，我们应珍视并守护自身的文化遗产；另一方面，也应以开放的心态吸纳外来文化的精华。唯有兼收并蓄，我们才能真正品尝到一场美味又营养的文化盛宴。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读

Ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle viewed laughter as "a bodily exercise precious to health." But 1 some claims to the contrary, laughing probably has little influence on physical fitness. Laughter does 2 short-term changes in the function of the heart and its blood vessels, 3 heart rate and oxygen consumption. But because hard laughter is difficult to 4, a good laugh is unlikely to have 5 benefits the way, say, walking or jogging does.

可以想象，这种身体反应或许有助于缓解心理压力的影响。无论如何，笑这一行为确实可能产生其他类型的身体反馈，从而改善个人的情绪状态。根据一个经典的情绪理论，我们的情感有一部分源于身体反应。19世纪末有人提出，人类不是因为悲伤才哭泣，而是当眼泪开始流淌时才变得悲伤。

Although sadness also 14 tears, evidence suggests that emotions can flow 15 muscular responses. In an experiment published in 1988, social psychologist Fritz Strack of the University of Würzburg in Germany asked volunteers to 16 a pen either with their teeth—thereby creating an artificial smile—or with their lips, which would produce a(n) 17 expression. Those forced to exercise their smiling muscles 18 more enthusiastically to funny cartoons than did those whose mouths were contracted in a frown, 19 that expressions may influence emotions rather than just the other way around. 20, the physical act of laughter could improve mood.

尽管悲伤也会先于眼泪出现，但证据表明，情感可以从肌肉反应中产生。在1988年发表的一项实验中，德国维尔茨堡大学的社会心理学家弗里茨·斯特拉克让志愿者用牙齿咬住一支笔——从而做出人为的微笑——或者用嘴唇叼住笔，这会做出失望的表情。那些被迫活动笑肌的志愿者，比那些嘴唇皱成皱眉的志愿者对搞笑卡通片反应更热烈，这表明表情可能影响情绪，而不仅仅是情绪影响表情。类似地，笑这一身体行为也可以改善情绪。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009. For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least. "Hooray! At last!" wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided classical-music critic.

纽约爱乐乐团决定聘请艾伦·吉尔伯特作为其下一任音乐总监，自2009年这一任命突然宣布以来，就一直是古典音乐界的热门话题。至少可以说，大多数反应是积极的。一向严谨的古典乐评论家安东尼·托马西尼写道："太好了！终于来了！"

One of the reasons why the appointment came as such a surprise, however, is that Gilbert is comparatively little known. Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert's appointment in the Times, calls him "an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him." As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.

然而，这一任命之所以如此令人意外，原因之一是吉尔伯特相对而言并不出名。就连曾在《纽约时报》上支持任命吉尔伯特的托马西尼，也称他为"一位谦逊的音乐家，身上没有那种令人敬畏的指挥家架子"。对于一个迄今为止一直由古斯塔夫·马勒和皮埃尔·布列兹这样的音乐家执掌的乐团来说，这样描述其下一任音乐总监，至少会让一些《纽约时报》读者觉得是牵强的夸奖。

For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one. To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting orchestral music. All I have to do is to go to my CD shelf, or boot up my computer and download still more recorded music from iTunes.

就我而言，我不知道吉尔伯特是否是一位伟大的指挥家，甚至是否算得上优秀。诚然，他指挥了种类繁多、令人印象深刻的有趣作品，但我不必非要去艾弗里·费舍尔音乐厅或别的地方才能听到有趣的管弦乐。我所要做的只是走到CD架前，或者打开电脑从iTunes下载更多录制好的音乐。

Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point. For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century. These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often much higher in artistic quality than today's live performances; moreover, they can be "consumed" at a time and place of the listener's choosing. The widespread availability of such recordings has thus brought about a crisis in the institution of the traditional classical concert.

那些忠实的音乐会常客回答说唱片无法替代现场演出，他们没有抓住问题的关键。为了赢得热爱艺术的公众的时间、注意力和金钱，古典乐器演奏家不仅必须与歌剧院、舞蹈团、戏剧公司和博物馆竞争，还必须与20世纪伟大古典音乐家的录音演出竞争。这些唱片价格低廉、随处可得，而且艺术品质往往远高于如今的现场演出；此外，听众可以自己选择时间和地点来"消费"它们。这种唱片的广泛可得性因而给传统古典音乐会这一制度带来了危机。

One possible response is for classical performers to program attractive new music that is not yet available on record. Gilbert's own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into "a markedly different, more vibrant organization." But what will be the nature of that difference? Merely expanding the orchestra's repertoire will not be enough. If Gilbert and the Philharmonic are to succeed, they must first change the relationship between America's oldest orchestra and the new audience it hopes to attract.

古典音乐表演者的一个可能应对办法是，编排一些尚未录制成唱片的、有吸引力的新音乐。吉尔伯特本人对新音乐的兴趣已广受关注：古典乐评论家亚历克斯·罗斯形容他是一个能把爱乐乐团变成"一个截然不同、更有活力的组织"的人。但这种不同的本质会是什么呢？仅仅扩大乐团的演出曲目是不够的。如果吉尔伯特和爱乐乐团想要成功，他们必须首先改变这个美国最古老的乐团与它希望吸引的新观众之间的关系。

Text 2   高管裸辞：为追求新目标而跳槽（26–30）

When Liam McGee departed as president of Bank of America in August, his explanation was surprisingly straight up. Rather than cloaking his exit in the usual vague excuses, he came right out and said he was leaving "to pursue my goal of running a company." Broadcasting his ambition was "very much my decision," McGee says. Within two weeks, he was talking for the first time with the board of Hartford Financial Services Group, which named him CEO and chairman on September 29.

8月，当利亚姆·麦吉辞去美国银行总裁一职时，他的解释出人意料地直白。他没有用常见的含糊说辞来掩饰离职，而是直截了当地说，他离开是"为了追求自己管理一家公司的目标"。麦吉说，公开自己的雄心"很大程度上是我自己的决定"。两周之内，他就第一次与哈特福德金融服务集团董事会进行了会谈，该集团于9月29日任命他为CEO兼董事长。

McGee says leaving without a position lined up gave him time to reflect on what kind of company he wanted to run. It also sent a clear message to the outside world about his aspirations. And McGee isn't alone. In recent weeks the No. 2 executives at Avon and American Express quit with the explanation that they were looking for a CEO post. As boards scrutinize succession plans in response to shareholder pressure, executives who don't get the nod also may wish to move on. A turbulent business environment also has senior managers cautious of letting vague pronouncements cloud their reputations.

麦吉说，在没有找到下家的情况下离开，给了他时间去思考自己究竟想经营什么样的公司。这也向外界传达了关于他抱负的明确信息。而且麦吉并非个例。最近几周，雅芳和美国运通的二把手也辞职了，理由是他们正在寻找CEO的职位。随着董事会在股东压力下仔细审查继任计划，那些未被提名的高管也可能希望另谋高就。动荡的商业环境也让高级经理们小心翼翼，不愿让含糊的声明损害自己的声誉。

As the first signs of recovery begin to take hold, deputy chiefs may be more willing to make the jump without a net. In the third quarter, CEO turnover was down 23% from a year ago as nervous boards stuck with the leaders they had, according to Liberum Research. As the economy picks up, opportunities will abound for aspiring leaders.

随着经济复苏的最初迹象开始稳固，二把手们可能更愿意在没有下家的情况下跳槽。据Liberum研究公司的数据，由于紧张的董事会留任现有领导，第三季度CEO的离职率同比下降了23%。随着经济回暖，有抱负的领导者将面临大量机会。

The decision to quit a senior position to look for a better one is unconventional. For years executives and headhunters have adhered to the rule that the most attractive CEO candidates are the ones who must be poached. Says Korn/Ferry senior partner Dennis Carey: "I can't think of a single search I've done where a board has not instructed me to look at sitting CEOs first."

辞去高级职位去寻找更好职位的决定是不合常规的。多年来，高管和猎头公司一直遵循这样一条规则：最具吸引力的CEO候选人必须是那些被挖来的人。光辉国际的高级合伙人丹尼斯·凯里说："在我所做的每一次搜寻中，董事会都会指示我首先从在任的CEO中物色。"

Those who jumped without a job haven't always landed in top positions quickly. Ellen Marram quit as chief of Tropicana a decade ago, saying she wanted to be a CEO. It was a year before she became head of a tiny Internet-based commodities exchange. Robert Willumstad left Citigroup in 2005 with ambitions to be a CEO. He finally took that post at a major financial institution three years later.

那些没有找好下家就跳槽的人，并不总能迅速登上高位。埃伦·马拉姆十年前辞去纯果乐公司负责人一职，说自己想当CEO。过了一年她才成为一家小型互联网商品交易公司的主管。罗伯特·维伦斯塔德2005年带着成为CEO的雄心离开花旗集团。三年后他才在一家大型金融机构就任该职。

Many recruiters say the old disgrace is fading for top performers. The financial crisis has made it more acceptable to be between jobs or to leave a bad one. "The traditional rule was it's safer to stay where you are, but that's been fundamentally inverted," says one headhunter. "The people who've been hurt the worst are those who've stayed too long."

许多招聘人员表示，对优秀高管而言，过去那种不光彩的感觉正在消退。金融危机使待业或辞去糟糕工作变得更易被接受。一位猎头说："传统的规则是待在原地更安全，但这一规则已被彻底颠覆。受伤最重的人，恰恰是那些待得太久的人。"

Text 3   新媒体时代的付费媒体与赢得媒体（31–35）

The rough guide to marketing success used to be that you got what you paid for. No longer. While traditional "paid" media—such as television commercials and print advertisements—still play a major role, companies today can exploit many alternative forms of media. Consumers passionate about a product may create "earned" media by willingly promoting it to friends, and a company may leverage "owned" media by sending e-mail alerts about products and sales to customers registered with its Web site. The way consumers now approach the process of making purchase decisions means that marketing's impact stems from a broad range of factors beyond conventional paid media.

过去，营销成功的粗略指南是：花多少钱办多少事。如今情况不再如此。尽管传统的"付费"媒体——如电视广告和平面广告——仍发挥重要作用，但如今企业还可以利用许多其他形式的媒体。酷爱某一产品的消费者可能会自愿向朋友推销它，从而创造出"赢得"媒体；企业也可以利用"自有"媒体，向在其网站注册的客户发送有关产品和促销的电子邮件提醒。如今消费者做出购买决策的方式意味着，营销的影响力源自传统付费媒体之外的广泛因素。

Paid and owned media are controlled by marketers promoting their own products. For earned media, such marketers act as the initiator for users' responses. But in some cases, one marketer's owned media become another marketer's paid media—for instance, when an e-commerce retailer sells ad space on its Web site. We define such sold media as owned media whose traffic is so strong that other organizations place their content or e-commerce engines within that environment. This trend, which we believe is still in its infancy, effectively began with retailers and travel providers such as airlines and hotels and will no doubt go further. Johnson & Johnson, for example, has created BabyCenter, a stand-alone media property that promotes complementary and even competitive products. Besides generating income, the presence of other marketers makes the site seem objective, gives companies opportunities to learn valuable information about the appeal of other companies' marketing, and may help expand user traffic for all companies concerned.

付费媒体和自有媒体由推销自有产品的营销人员掌控。对于赢得媒体，这些营销人员充当用户反应的发起者。但在某些情况下，一个营销人员的自有媒体会成为另一个营销人员的付费媒体——例如，当一家电子商务零售商在其网站上出售广告空间时。我们把这种售出媒体定义为这样一种自有媒体：其流量如此之大，以至于其他机构把内容或电子商务引擎放到这个环境中。我们认为这一趋势仍处于起步阶段，但它实际上始于零售商和航空公司、酒店等旅游服务商，而且无疑会走得更远。例如，强生公司创建了BabyCenter——这是一个独立媒体资产，用于推广互补甚至竞争性产品。除了产生收入之外，其他营销人员的存在使该网站显得客观，让各公司有机会了解其他公司营销吸引力的宝贵信息，并且可能有助于扩大所有相关公司的用户流量。

The same dramatic technological changes that have provided marketers with more (and more diverse) communications choices have also increased the risk that passionate consumers will voice their opinions in quicker, more visible, and much more damaging ways. Such hijacked media are the opposite of earned media: an asset or campaign becomes hostage to consumers, other stakeholders, or activists who make negative allegations about a brand or product. Members of social networks, for instance, are learning that they can hijack media to apply pressure on the businesses that originally created them.

同样是这些为营销人员提供了更多（也更多样）传播选择的重大技术变革，也增加了风险：情绪激动的消费者会以更快、更显眼、更具破坏性的方式表达意见。这种"被劫持"媒体与赢得媒体正好相反：一项资产或活动沦为消费者、其他利益相关者或活动人士的人质，他们会对某一品牌或产品提出负面指控。例如，社交网络的成员正在认识到，他们可以通过劫持媒体来向最初创建这些媒体的企业施加压力。

If that happens, passionate consumers would try to persuade others to boycott products, putting the reputation of the target company at risk. In such a case, the company's response may not be sufficiently quick or thoughtful, and the learning curve has been steep. Toyota Motor, for example, alleviated some of the damage from its recall crisis earlier this year with a relatively quick and well-orchestrated social-media response campaign, which included efforts to engage with consumers directly on sites such as Twitter and the social-news site Digg.

如果这种情况发生，情绪激动的消费者会试图说服其他人抵制产品，从而危及目标公司的声誉。在这种情况下，公司的反应可能不够迅速或周到，而学习曲线一直很陡峭。例如，丰田汽车在今年早些时候的召回危机中，通过一场相对迅速且精心策划的社交媒体应对活动减轻了部分损失，活动包括在Twitter和社交新闻网站Digg等平台上直接与消费者沟通。

Text 4   养孩子是幸福还是遗憾（36–40）

It's no surprise that Jennifer Senior's insightful, provocative magazine cover story, "I Love My Children, I Hate My Life," is arousing much chatter—nothing gets people talking like the suggestion that child rearing is anything less than a completely fulfilling, life-enriching experience. Rather than concluding that children make parents either happy or miserable, Senior suggests we need to redefine happiness: instead of thinking of it as something that can be measured by moment-to-moment joy, we should consider being happy as a past-tense condition. Even though the day-to-day experience of raising kids can be soul-crushingly hard, Senior writes that "the very things that in the moment dampen our moods can later be sources of intense gratification and delight."

詹妮弗·西尼尔那篇富有洞察力且颇具争议性的杂志封面文章《我爱我的孩子，我恨我的生活》引发了热议，这并不令人意外——没有什么比"养孩子并非一段完全令人满足、丰富人生的经历"这种暗示更能让人讨论了。西尼尔并没有断言孩子让父母幸福或痛苦，而是提出我们需要重新定义幸福：不要把幸福看作可以用瞬间快乐来衡量的东西，而应把它视为一种过去时的状态。尽管日复一日养孩子的经历可能令人崩溃，但西尼尔写道："正是那些当下令我们心情沮丧的事情，日后却可能成为巨大满足和喜悦的源泉。"

The magazine cover showing an attractive mother holding a cute baby is hardly the only Madonna-and-child image on newsstands this week. There are also stories about newly adoptive—and newly single-mom Sandra Bullock, as well as the usual "Jennifer Aniston is pregnant" news. Practically every week features at least one celebrity mom, or mom-to-be, smiling on the newsstands.

杂志封面上一位迷人的母亲抱着一个可爱婴儿的画面，绝非本周报摊上唯一的圣母圣子形象。还有关于刚收养孩子、刚成为单身母亲的桑德拉·布洛克的报道，以及常见的"詹妮弗·安妮斯顿怀孕"新闻。几乎每周都至少有一位明星妈妈或准妈妈在报摊上微笑亮相。

In a society that so persistently celebrates procreation, is it any wonder that admitting you regret having children is equivalent to admitting you support kitten-killing? It doesn't seem quite fair, then, to compare the regrets of parents to the regrets of the childless. Unhappy parents rarely are provoked to wonder if they shouldn't have had kids, but unhappy childless folks are bothered with the message that children are the single most important thing in the world: obviously their misery must be a direct result of the gaping baby-size holes in their lives.

在一个如此执着地歌颂生育的社会里，承认后悔生孩子就等同于承认自己支持杀小猫，这又有什么好奇怪的呢？那么，把父母的后悔与无子女者的后悔相提并论，似乎并不公平。不幸福的父母很少会被激起去想自己是不是不该生孩子，而不幸福的无子女者却被"孩子是世界上最重要的东西"这一讯息所困扰：显然，他们的痛苦一定是生活中那个巨大的婴儿大小的空洞直接造成的。

Of course, the image of parenthood that celebrity magazines like Us Weekly and People present is hugely unrealistic, especially when the parents are single mothers like Bullock. According to several studies concluding that parents are less happy than childless couples, single parents are the least happy of all. No shock there, considering how much work it is to raise a kid without a partner to lean on; yet to hear Sandra and Britney tell it, raising a kid on their "own" (read: with round-the-clock help) is a piece of cake.

当然，《我们周刊》和《人物》等名人杂志所呈现的为人父母的形象极不现实，尤其是当父母是布洛克这样的单身母亲时。几项研究得出结论：有孩子的父母不如无子女的夫妻幸福，而单亲家庭最不幸福。这并不令人意外，想想在没有伴侣可以依靠的情况下养一个孩子有多辛苦；但听听桑德拉和布兰妮的说法吧，"独自"养孩子（实际意思是：有全天候帮手）简直是小菜一碟。

It's hard to imagine that many people are dumb enough to want children just because Reese and Angelina make it look so glamorous: most adults understand that a baby is not a haircut. But it's interesting to wonder if the images we see every week of stress-free, happiness-enhancing parenthood aren't in some small, subconscious way contributing to our own dissatisfactions with the actual experience, in the same way that a small part of us hoped getting "the Rachel" might make us look just a little bit like Jennifer Aniston.

很难想象，会有很多人蠢到仅仅因为瑞茜和安吉丽娜把养孩子这件事显得如此光鲜就想要孩子：大多数成年人都明白，养孩子不是剪个头发。但有趣的是，我们每周看到的那些无忧无虑、幸福感爆棚的为人父母形象，是否正以某种微小的、潜意识的方式加剧着我们对真实育儿经历的不满——就像我们内心一小部分人曾希望剪个"瑞秋头"能让自己看起来有点像詹妮弗·安妮斯顿一样。

Part B · 新题型排序题（41–45）

【题目】关于哈佛教授Louis Menand所著《思想市场：美国大学的改革与阻力》一书的书评。E、G段已就位。排序：G → 41 → 42 → 43 → E → 44 → 45。

G段（已就位首段）：哈佛英语教授Louis Menand写的《思想市场》这本书值得每个想读博的学生读一读——他们读后可能会决定去别处。美国大学里正在发生一些奇怪的事，而Menand巧妙地捕捉到了。

E段（已就位中段）：除了职业的专业化，美国大学还把教授本身专业化了。联邦科研经费在1960-1990年间翻了四倍，但教师教学时间减半……但Menand认为专业化背后的关键思想是：特定专业所需的知识和技能不可传授但可转移……学科不仅垄断知识生产，还垄断知识生产者的生产。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
No disciplines have seized on professionalism with as much enthusiasm the humanities. You can, Mr. Menand points out, became a lawyer in three years and a medical doctor in four. But the regular time it takes to get a doctoral degree in the humanities is nine years. Not surprisingly, up to half of all doctoral students in English drop out before getting their degrees.
没有任何学科像人文学科那样热衷于专业化。梅南德先生指出，你可以三年成为律师、四年成为医生，但人文学科拿博士学位通常要九年。无怪乎多达一半的英语专业博士生在拿到学位前就辍学了。
B
His concern is mainly with the humanities: Literature, languages, philosophy and so on. These are disciplines that are going out of style: 22% of American college graduates now major in business compared with only 2% in history and 4% in English. However, many leading American universities want their undergraduates to have a grounding in the basic canon of ideas that every educated person should possess. But most find it difficult to agree on what a "general education" should look like. At Harvard, Mr. Menand notes, "the great books are read because they have been read", they form a sort of social glue.
他主要关切的是人文学科：文学、语言、哲学等等。这些学科正日渐式微：如今22%的美国大学毕业生主修商科，而主修历史和英语的分别只有2%和4%。然而，许多美国顶尖大学希望本科生掌握每个受过教育的人都应具备的基本思想经典。但大多数学者难以就"通识教育"应有的模样达成一致。梅南德先生指出，在哈佛，"伟大著作之所以被读，是因为它们一直被读"，它们构成了某种社会黏合剂。
C
Equally unsurprisingly, only about half end up with professorships for which they entered graduate school. There are simply too few posts. This is partly because universities continue to produce ever more PhDs. But fewer students want to study humanities subjects: English department awarded more bachelor's degrees in 1970-71 than they did 20 years later. Fewer students requires fewer teachers. So, at the end of a decade of theses-writing, many humanities students leave the profession to do something for which they have not been trained.
同样不意外的是，最终只有约一半人获得了他们读研所瞄准的教授职位。实在是因为岗位太少。这 partly 是因为大学仍在不断培养越来越多的博士。但愿意攻读人文学科的学生变少了：英语系在1970—71年授予的学士学位比20年后还要多。学生少了，教师需求也就少了。于是，在长达十年的论文写作之后，许多人文学生离开了本行，去做一些他们并未受过训练的工作。
D
One reason why it is hard to design and teach courses is that they can cut across the insistence by top American universities that liberal-arts educations and professional education should be kept separate, taught in different schools. Many students experience both varieties. Although more than half of Harvard undergraduates end up in law, medicine or business, future doctors and lawyers must study a non-specialist liberal-art degree before embarking on a professional qualification.
课程难以设计与讲授的一个原因是，它们会与顶尖美国大学所坚持的"文科教育与职业教育应当分离、分属不同学院"相冲突。许多学生两种都经历过。尽管超过半数的哈佛本科生最终进入法律、医学或商界，但未来的医生和律师在攻读职业资格之前，必须先修一个非专业性的文科学位。
E
Besides professionalizing the professions by this separation top American universities have professionalized the professor. The growth on public money for academic research has speeded the process: federal research grants rose fourfold between 1960 and 1990, but faculty teaching hours fell by half as research took its toll. Professionalism has turned the acquisition of a doctoral degree into a prerequisite for a successful academic career: as late as 1969 a third of American professors did not possess one. But the key idea behind professionalization, argues Mr. Menand, is that "the knowledge and skills needed for a particular specialization are transmissible but not transferable." So disciplines acquire a monopoly not just over the production of knowledge, but also over the production of the producers of knowledge.
除了通过这种分离使各职业专业化之外，顶尖美国大学还使教授这一职业本身专业化了。公共科研经费的增长加速了这一进程：1960至1990年间联邦研究资助增至四倍，但随着科研挤占，教师授课时数减半。专业化已把获得博士学位变成了学术生涯成功的前提：迟至1969年，仍有三分之一的美国教授没有博士学位。但梅南德先生认为，专业化背后的核心理念是"某一特定专业所需的知识和技能可以传授却不可转移"。于是学科不仅垄断了知识的生产，也垄断了知识生产者的生产。
F
The key to reforming higher education, concludes Mr. Menand, is to alter the way in which "the producers of knowledge are produced." Otherwise, academics will continue to think dangerously alike, increasingly detached from the societies which they study, investigate and criticize. "Academic inquiry, at least in some fields, may need to become less exclusionary and more holistic." Yet quite how that happens, Mr. Menand does not say.
梅南德先生总结道，改革高等教育的关键在于改变"知识生产者被生产出来的方式"。否则，学者们将继续危险地趋同思维，越来越脱离他们所研究、调查和批评的社会。"学术研究，至少在某些领域，或许需要变得少些排他、多些整体。"然而究竟如何做到，梅南德先生并未言明。
G
The subtle and intelligent little book The Marketplace of Ideas: Reform and Resistance in the American University should be read by every student thinking of applying to take a doctoral degree. They may then decide to go elsewhere. For something curious has been happening in American Universities, and Louis Menand, a professor of English at Harvard University, captured it skillfully.
这本精妙而睿智的小书《思想的市场：美国大学的改革与阻力》应当被每一个考虑申请攻读博士学位的学生阅读。他们读后或许会决定另谋出路。因为美国大学里正发生着某种怪事，而哈佛英语教授路易斯·梅南德巧妙地捕捉到了它。
41
段落排序题
答案 B
匹配依据[B] 他主要关心人文学科：文学、语言、哲学等。这些学科正在过时：22%的美国大学生学商科，而历史只占2%、英语4%。但顶尖大学希望本科生接受"经典著作"基础训练……→ 承接G段"Menand捕捉到美国大学怪事"，先讲他关心的对象是人文学科。
42
段落排序题
答案 D
匹配依据[D] 难设计和教授这些课程的一个原因是，美国顶尖大学坚持把博雅教育与专业教育分开，在不同学院教授。哈佛一半以上本科生最终读法律、医学或商科，但未来的医生律师必须先修非专业博雅学位。→ B段末句提到"general education/经典著作"，D段解释为什么博雅教育难搞（它与专业教育分离）。
43
段落排序题
答案 A
匹配依据[A] 没有哪个学科像人文学科那样狂热地追求专业化。Menand指出，三年能成律师、四年能成医生，但人文学科博士要九年。不足一半的英语博士生在拿到学位前退学。→ D段讲专业教育分离，A段讲人文学科专业化之狂热（读博要九年），并引出E段"通过这种分离，大学把教授也专业化了"。
44
段落排序题
答案 C
匹配依据[C] 同样不出所料，只有约一半人最终拿到他们读研究生时想要的教职。教职岗位太少。部分原因是大学还在制造越来越多的博士……十年写论文结束时，许多人文学科学生进入了一个他们从未受过训练的行业。→ E段讲教授专业化、知识生产垄断，C段顺承讲专业化后果：教职少、博士过剩、学生被迫转行。
45
段落排序题
答案 F
匹配依据[F] Menand总结，改革高等教育的关键在于改变"知识生产者是如何被生产出来的"方式。否则学者们会继续危险地雷同思考，越来越脱离他们所研究、调查和批评的社会……学术研究需要少一些排外、多一些整体观。至于如何做到，Menand没有说。→ 全文结尾段，提出改革方向，与G段首尾呼应。
干扰项本题为排序题，无干扰段落；A-G中除正确顺序外其余即按逻辑自然衔接。
Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）
46
翻译
Allen's contribution was to take an assumption we all share—that because we are not robots we therefore control our thoughts—and reveal its erroneous nature.
艾伦的贡献在于，他拿出"我们并非机器人，因此能掌控自己的思想"这一公认的假设，并揭示了其谬误所在。
采分点① contribution 贡献；② assumption 假设；③ that 同位语从句解释 assumption；④ erroneous nature 错误本质。
47
翻译
while we may be able to sustain the illusion of control through the conscious mind alone, in reality we are continually faced with a question: "Why cannot I make myself do this or achieve that?"
尽管我们或许可以仅凭意识来维系"控制"这种错觉，现实中我们还是不断要面对一个问题："我为什么不能让自己做这个或实现那个？"
采分点① sustain the illusion 维持错觉；② conscious mind 意识；③ be faced with 面对。
48
翻译
This seems a justification for neglect of those in need, and a rationalization of exploitation, of the superiority of those at the top and the inferiority of those at the bottom.
这似乎是在为忽视贫困者的行为作辩护，为剥削、为社会上层人群的优越及社会底层人群的卑微找理由。
采分点① justification 辩护；② those in need 贫困者；③ rationalization 合理化；④ exploitation 剥削；⑤ superiority/inferiority 优越/卑微。
49
翻译
circumstances seem to be designed to bring out the best in us, and if we feel that we have been "wronged" then we are unlikely to begin a conscious effort to escape from our situation.
环境仿佛就是为了激发我们的最大潜能而设，如果我们觉得自己遭受了"不公"，就不太可能有意识地去努力摆脱自己的处境。
采分点① be designed to 旨在；② bring out the best in sb 激发某人最大潜能；③ wrong 冤枉（动词）；④ conscious effort 有意识的努力。
50
翻译
The upside is the possibilities contained in knowing that everything is up to us; where before we were experts in the array of limitations, now we become authorities of what is possible.
其正面意义在于，了解了一切都取决于我们自己，即有了诸多可能；此前我们是谙熟各种局限的专家，现在我们成了驾驭各种可能性的权威。
采分点① upside 正面/积极面；② be up to sb 取决于某人；③ the array of 一系列；④ authorities 权威。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 推荐信

原题指令 Directions

Suppose you are a college student. Write a letter to a friend to recommend your favorite movie and give your reasons for the recommendation. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the letter. Use "Li Ming" instead. Do not write the address.

【译文】假设你是一名大学生。给一位朋友写一封信，推荐你最喜欢的一部电影，并说明推荐理由。字数约100词。信末不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。不要写地址。

题目

给一位朋友写信，1）推荐一部你最喜欢的电影，2）给出推荐理由。约100词，落款Li Ming，不写地址。

审题

① 格式：私人信件；② 语气：亲切热情；③ 内容：电影名+2-3条具体推荐理由（剧情/演员/主题）。

参考范文

Dear Friend,

I was thrilled to learn that you are looking for a good movie to watch, and I would like to recommend Forrest Gump without the slightest hesitation.

My reasons are as follows. To begin with, the story is deeply moving: it follows a simple-minded yet upright man who witnesses half a century of American history with remarkable perseverance. Besides, Tom Hanks' performance is absolutely brilliant, making the character both touching and inspiring. Most importantly, the film conveys a timeless message about fate, love and the power of perseverance that will stay with you long after the credits roll.

I hope you enjoy it. Looking forward to hearing your thoughts!

Yours, Li Ming

【译文】

亲爱的朋友：

得知你正想找一部好电影来看，我毫不犹豫地想向你推荐《阿甘正传》。

我的理由如下。首先，故事感人至深：它讲述了一个憨厚正直的男人，以惊人的毅力见证了美国半个世纪的历史。此外，汤姆·汉克斯的表演堪称精湛，让这个角色既动人又鼓舞人心。最重要的是，影片传递了关于命运、爱与坚持力量的永恒主题，令人久久难忘。

希望你喜欢。期待听到你的想法！

你的，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 旅程之"余"（环境保护）

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The picture shows a tourist boat on a river. While sightseeing, the passengers are throwing rubbish into the water, which is already littered with lunch boxes, bottles and paper. The caption reads: "What is left after the journey".

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 图中一艘游船在河上游览，船上游客观光时往河里乱扔垃圾，水面已漂浮着饭盒、瓶子、纸张等废物。标题：旅程之“余”。

图画描述

图中一艘游船在河上游览，船上游客一边观光一边往河里乱扔垃圾，水面上已经漂浮着饭盒、瓶子、纸张等各种废物，河水一片狼藉。下方标题：旅程之"余"。

审题框架

三段式：①描述图画（游客乱丢垃圾污染景区）；②阐释寓意（旅游中破坏环境的行为，讽刺只顾自己不顾环境的不文明现象）；③评论（应提高环保意识、文明旅游）。160-200词。

参考范文

The thought-provoking picture depicts a boat drifting down a river, where sightseers casually toss litter overboard. The water is already littered with lunch boxes, bottles and waste paper, and the caption reads: the "leftovers" of a journey.

What the drawing exposes is a widespread malaise: while enjoying nature's beauty, many travelers leave behind a trail of damage. The "leftovers" in the caption refer not to food, but to the garbage and pollution thoughtless tourists abandon in their wake. Such behavior not only spoils the charm of scenic spots but also wrecks the ecosystem, turning a pleasant trip into an environmental tragedy.

From my perspective, urgent action is called for. First, tourists should be educated to raise their environmental awareness and behave responsibly. Second, scenic areas ought to tighten supervision and penalize littering. Only when every traveler treats nature with respect can we preserve the planet's beauty for generations to come.

【译文】

这幅发人深省的图画描绘了一艘在河上漂流的游船，游客随手将垃圾抛入水中。水面早已散落着饭盒、瓶子和废纸，图题写道：旅程之"余"。

画面所揭示的是一种普遍弊病：许多游客在享受自然之美的同时，却留下了一路破坏。标题中的"余"指的并非食物，而是无知游客抛在身后的垃圾与污染。这种行为不仅破坏了景区的魅力，更摧毁了生态环境，把一次愉快的旅程变成一场环境悲剧。

在我看来，亟需采取行动。首先，应教育游客增强环保意识、规范自身行为；其次，景区应加强监管并对乱扔垃圾者予以处罚。唯有每位游客都敬畏自然，我们才能为子孙后代留住这片美丽。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读

The ethical judgments of the Supreme Court justices have become an important issue recently. The court cannot 1 its legitimacy as guardian of the rule of law 2 justices behave like politicians. Yet, in several instances, justices acted in ways that 3 the court's reputation for being independent and impartial.

最高法院大法官的伦理判断近来成了一个重要议题。如果大法官表现得像政客一样，法院就无法"维护"其作为法治捍卫者的合法性。然而，在好几起事件中，大法官们的所作所为"削弱"了法院独立、公正的声誉。

Justice Antonin Scalia, for example, appeared at political events. That kind of activity makes it less likely that the court's decisions will be 4 as impartial judgments. Part of the problem is that the justices are not 5 by an ethics code. At the very least, the court should make itself 6 to the code of conduct that 7 to the rest of the federal judiciary.

例如，大法官安东宁·斯卡利亚就曾出席政治活动。这类行为使得法院的判决不太可能被"接受"为公正的裁决。问题的部分原因在于，大法官们并不"受"道德准则的"约束"。至少，法院应当让自己"遵守"那些"适用于"其他联邦司法人员的行为准则。

This and other similar cases 8 the question of whether there is still a 9 between the court and politics.

这一事件以及其他类似案件"提出"了一个问题：法院与政治之间是否还存在"界限"。

The framers of the Constitution envisioned law 10 having authority apart from politics. They gave justices permanent positions 11 they would be free to 12 those in power and have no need to 13 political support. Our legal system was designed to set law apart from politics precisely because they are so closely 14.

宪法制定者们"把"法律设想"为"一种独立于政治之外的权威。他们给予大法官终身职位，"以便"他们能自由地"打压"当权者，而无需"培植"政治支持。我们的法律制度之所以把法律与政治分开来设计，正是因为二者联系如此"紧密"。

Constitutional law is political because it results from choices rooted in fundamental social 15 like liberty and property. When the court deals with social policy decisions, the law it 16 is inescapably political—which is why decisions split along ideological lines are so easily 17 as unjust.

宪法之所以是政治性的，是因为它源于植根于自由、财产等基本社会"概念"的选择。当法院处理社会政策裁决时，它所"形成"的法律不可避免地带有政治性——这就是为什么按意识形态划线的裁决如此容易被"斥为"不公正。

The justices must 18 doubts about the court's legitimacy by making themselves 19 to the code of conduct. That would make rulings more likely to be seen as separate from politics and, 20, convincing as law.

大法官们必须通过让自己"遵守"行为准则来"解决"人们对法院合法性的质疑。那将使裁决更可能被视为独立于政治之外，"从而"作为法律令人信服。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

Come on—Everybody's doing it. That whispered message, half invitation and half forcing, is what most of us think of when we hear the words peer pressure. It usually leads to no good—drinking, drugs and casual sex. But in her new book Join the Club, Tina Rosenberg contends that peer pressure can also be a positive force through what she calls the social cure, in which organizations and officials use the power of group dynamics to help individuals improve their lives and possibly the world.

得了吧——大家都这么做呢。当我们听到"同伴压力"这个词时，大多数人想到的就是这种半是邀请、半是强迫的耳语。它通常不会带来什么好事——酗酒、吸毒、随意的性行为。但在新作《加入俱乐部》中，蒂娜·罗森伯格主张，同伴压力也可以通过她所谓的"社会疗法"成为一种积极力量，在社会疗法中，组织和官员们利用群体动力的力量来帮助个人改善生活，甚至可能改善整个世界。

Rosenberg, the recipient of a Pulitzer Prize, offers a host of examples of the social cure in action: In South Carolina, a state-sponsored antismoking program called Rage Against the Haze sets out to make cigarettes uncool. In South Africa, an HIV-prevention initiative known as LoveLife recruits young people to promote safe sex among their peers.

普利策奖得主罗森伯格给出了大量社会疗法付诸实践的例子：在南卡罗来纳州，一个由州政府资助、名为"向烟雾宣战"的反吸烟项目旨在让吸烟变得不再酷。在南非，一个名为"热爱生命"的艾滋病预防项目招募年轻人，在同伴中推广安全性行为。

The idea seems promising, and Rosenberg is a perceptive observer. Her critique of the lameness of many public-health campaigns is spot-on: they fail to mobilize peer pressure for healthy habits, and they demonstrate a seriously flawed understanding of psychology. "Dare to be different, please don't smoke!" pleads one billboard campaign aimed at reducing smoking among teenagers—teenagers, who desire nothing more than fitting in. Rosenberg argues convincingly that public-health advocates ought to take a page from advertisers, so skilled at applying peer pressure.

这个想法似乎很有前景，而罗森伯格也是一位敏锐的观察家。她对许多公共卫生运动蹩脚之处的批评一针见血：这些运动没能调动同伴压力来促成健康习惯，而且暴露出对心理学严重错误的理解。一个旨在减少青少年吸烟的广告牌活动呼吁道："敢于与众不同，请不要吸烟！"——可青少年最渴望的恰恰是融入群体。罗森伯格令人信服地指出，公共卫生倡导者应该向广告商学习，后者太擅长施加同伴压力了。

But on the general effectiveness of the social cure, Rosenberg is less persuasive. Join the Club is filled with too much irrelevant detail and not enough exploration of the social and biological factors that make peer pressure so powerful. The most glaring flaw of the social cure as it's presented here is that it doesn't work very well for very long. Rage Against the Haze failed once state funding was cut. Evidence that the LoveLife program produces lasting changes is limited and mixed.

但在社会疗法的整体效果上，罗森伯格就不那么有说服力了。《加入俱乐部》充斥着太多无关细节，却没有充分探讨使同伴压力如此强大的社会和生物因素。这里所呈现的社会疗法最明显的缺陷是：它的效果持续不了多久。一旦州政府削减资金，"向烟雾宣战"就失败了。而"热爱生命"项目能否产生持久改变的证据既有限又褒贬不一。

There's no doubt that our peer groups exert enormous influence on our behavior. An emerging body of research shows that positive health habits—as well as negative ones—spread through networks of friends via social communication. This is a subtle form of peer pressure: we unconsciously imitate the behavior we see every day.

毫无疑问，同伴群体对我们的行为施加着巨大影响。大量新兴研究表明，积极的健康习惯——以及消极的习惯——都通过社会交往在朋友网络中传播。这是一种微妙的同伴压力形式：我们无意识地模仿每天看到的行为。

Far less certain, however, is how successfully experts and bureaucrats can select our peer groups and steer their activities in virtuous directions. It's like the teacher who breaks up the troublemakers in the back row by pairing them with better-behaved classmates. The tactic never really works. And that's the problem with a social cure engineered from the outside: in the real world, as in school, we insist on choosing our own friends.

然而，更难确定的是，专家和官僚在多大程度上能成功挑选我们的同伴群体并引导他们的行为走上正道。这就像老师把后排捣蛋鬼拆开、把他们和表现好的同学配在一起。这种策略从来就没真正奏效过。而这正是从外部设计的社会疗法的问题所在：在现实世界里，正如在学校里一样，我们坚持自己选择朋友。

Text 2   Entergy公司与佛蒙特州核电厂争端（26–30）

A deal is a deal—except, apparently, when Entergy is involved. The company, a major energy supplier in New England, provoked justified outrage in Vermont last week when it announced it was reneging on a longstanding commitment to abide by the state's strict nuclear regulations.

交易就是交易——但Entergy公司一掺和进来显然就另当别论了。这家新英格兰地区的主要能源供应商上周宣布，它将背弃遵守该州严格核规章的长期承诺，这在佛蒙特州激起了理所应当的愤怒。

Instead, the company has done precisely what it had long promised it would not: challenge the constitutionality of Vermont's rules in the federal court, as part of a desperate effort to keep its Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant running. It's a stunning move.

相反，该公司恰恰做了它长期以来承诺不做的事：在联邦法院对佛蒙特州的规章是否合宪提出质疑，这是它为维持佛蒙特扬基核电厂运转而拼死一搏的一部分。这一举动令人震惊。

The conflict has been surfacing since 2002, when the corporation bought Vermont's only nuclear power plant, an aging reactor in Vernon. As a condition of receiving state approval for the sale, the company agreed to seek permission from state regulators to operate past 2012. In 2006, the state went a step further, requiring that any extension of the plant's license be subject to the Vermont legislature's approval. Then, too, the company went along.

这场冲突自2002年起就开始浮出水面，当时该公司买下了佛蒙特州唯一的核电站——位于弗农的一座老旧反应堆。作为获得州政府批准这项交易的条件，该公司同意在2012年之后运营须征求州监管机构许可。2006年，州政府更进一步，要求电厂执照的任何延期都必须经过佛蒙特州立法机构批准。而该公司当时也照做了。

Either Entergy never really intended to live by those commitments, or it simply didn't foresee what would happen next. A string of accidents, including the partial collapse of a cooling tower in 2007 and the discovery of an underground pipe system leakage, raised serious questions about both Vermont Yankee's safety and Entergy's management—especially after the company made misleading statements about the pipe. Enraged by Entergy's behavior, the Vermont Senate voted 26 to 4 last year against allowing an extension.

要么Entergy从未真正打算遵守这些承诺，要么它根本没有预料到接下来会发生什么。一连串事故——包括2007年冷却塔部分倒塌以及发现地下管道系统泄漏——使人们对佛蒙特扬基电厂的安全和Entergy的管理都提出了严重质疑，尤其是在该公司就管道问题发表误导性声明之后。被Entergy的行为激怒，佛蒙特州参议院去年以26票对4票反对批准延期。

Now the company is suddenly claiming that the 2002 agreement is invalid because of the 2006 legislation, and that only the federal government has regulatory power over nuclear issues. The legal issues in the case are obscure: whereas the Supreme Court has ruled that states do have some regulatory authority over nuclear power, legal scholars say the Vermont case will offer a precedent-setting test of how far those powers extend. Certainly, there are valid concerns about the patchwork regulations that could result if every state sets its own rules. But had Entergy kept its word, that debate would be beside the point.

如今该公司突然声称，由于2006年的立法，2002年协议无效，而且只有联邦政府对核问题拥有监管权。本案的法律问题模糊不清：尽管最高法院已裁定各州确实对核能拥有一定监管权，但法学家们表示，佛蒙特案将成为一个开创性的判例，检验这些权力究竟能延伸多远。当然，如果每个州都自定规则，由此产生的补丁式规章确实令人担忧。但如果Entergy信守诺言，这场争论就无关紧要了。

The company seems to have concluded that its reputation in Vermont is already so damaged that it has nothing left to lose by going to war with the state. But there should be consequences. Permission to run a nuclear plant is a public trust. Entergy runs 11 other reactors in the United States, including Pilgrim Nuclear station in Plymouth. Pledging to run Pilgrim safely, the company has applied for federal permission to keep it open for another 20 years. But as the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reviews the company's application, it should keep in mind what promises from Entergy are worth.

该公司似乎已断定，它在佛蒙特州的声誉已经受损如此之重，以至于和州政府对着干也没什么可再失去的了。但应该会有后果。运营核电厂的许可是一种公共信任。Entergy在美国还运营着另外11座反应堆，包括普利茅斯的朝圣者核电站。该公司已申请联邦许可，承诺安全运营朝圣者核电站20年。但在核监管委员会审查该公司申请时，它应该牢记Entergy的承诺到底值多少钱。

Text 3   科学发现声明的可信性过程（31–35）

In the idealized version of how science is done, facts about the world are waiting to be observed and collected by objective researchers who use the scientific method to carry out their work. But in the everyday practice of science, discovery frequently follows an ambiguous and complicated route. We aim to be objective, but we cannot escape the context of our unique life experiences. Prior knowledge and interest influence what we experience, what we think our experiences mean, and the subsequent actions we take. Opportunities for misinterpretation, error, and self-deception abound.

在科学研究的理想化版本中，关于世界的事实等待着客观的研究者去观察和收集，这些研究者运用科学方法开展工作。但在日常的科学实践中，发现之路往往模糊而复杂。我们力求客观，却无法逃脱自身独特生活经历的背景。先前的知识和兴趣会影响我们的经历、我们对经历意义的理解以及随后采取的行动。误解、错误和自欺的机会比比皆是。

Consequently, discovery claims should be thought of as protoscience. Similar to newly staked mining claims, they are full of potential. But it takes collective scrutiny and acceptance to transform a discovery claim into a mature discovery. This is the credibility process, through which the individual researcher's me, here, now becomes the community's anyone, anywhere, anytime. Objective knowledge is the goal, not the starting point.

因此，发现声明应被视为原科学。就像新划定的采矿权一样，它们充满潜力。但要把发现声明转变为成熟的发现，需要集体的审视和接受。这就是可信性过程，通过这一过程，个体研究者的"我、此地、此时"变成了整个学界的"任何人、任何地点、任何时间"。客观知识是目标，而非起点。

Once a discovery claim becomes public, the discoverer receives intellectual credit. But, unlike with mining claims, the community takes control of what happens next. Within the complex social structure of the scientific community, researchers make discoveries; editors and reviewers act as gatekeepers by controlling the publication process; other scientists use the new finding to suit their own purposes; and finally, the public (including other scientists) receives the new discovery and possibly accompanying technology. As a discovery claim works its way through the community, the interaction and confrontation between shared and competing beliefs about the science and the technology involved transforms an individual's discovery claim into the community's credible discovery.

一旦发现声明公开，发现者就获得了学术荣誉。但与采矿权不同的是，接下来如何发展由学界掌控。在科学界复杂的社会结构中，研究者做出发现；编辑和审稿人充当守门人，控制发表过程；其他科学家为自己的目的使用新发现；最后，公众（包括其他科学家）接受这项新发现以及可能伴随的技术。当发现声明努力在学界中获得认可时，关于相关科学和技术的共同信念与相互竞争的信念之间的互动和对抗，就把个体的发现声明转变成了学界的可信发现。

Two paradoxes exist throughout this credibility process. First, scientific work tends to focus on some aspect of prevailing knowledge that is viewed as incomplete or incorrect. Little reward accompanies duplication and confirmation of what is already known and believed. The goal is new-search, not re-search. Not surprisingly, newly published discovery claims and credible discoveries that appear to be important and convincing will always be open to challenge and potential modification or refutation by future researchers. Second, novelty itself frequently provokes disbelief. Nobel Laureate and physiologist Albert Szent-Györgyi once described discovery as "seeing what everybody has seen and thinking what nobody has thought." But thinking what nobody else has thought and telling others what they have missed may not change their views. Sometimes years are required for truly novel discovery claims to be accepted and appreciated.

在整个可信性过程中存在着两个悖论。第一，科学工作往往聚焦于现有知识中被视为不完整或不正确的某个方面。重复和证实已知的东西几乎没有回报。目标是新探索，而非再探索。毫不奇怪，新发表的发现声明和看似重要、令人信服的可信发现，总是会面临未来研究者的挑战、修正甚至反驳。第二，新奇本身常常引发怀疑。诺贝尔奖得主、生理学家阿尔伯特·森特-哲尔吉曾把发现描述为"看到每个人都看到的东西，想到没人想到的事"。但想到别人没想到的、告诉他们错过了什么，未必能改变他们的观点。有时，真正新奇的发现声明需要多年才能被接受和赏识。

In the end, credibility "happens" to a discovery claim—a process that corresponds to what philosopher Annette Baier has described as the commons of the mind. "We reason together, challenge, revise, and complete each other's reasoning and each other's conceptions of reason."

最终，可信性"发生"在一项发现声明身上——这一过程正如哲学家安妮特·拜尔所描述的"思想的共同领域"。"我们共同推理、互相挑战、修正并完善彼此的推理和彼此对理性的构想。"

Text 4   公共部门工会的兴盛（36–40）

If the trade unionist Jimmy Hoffa were alive today, he would probably represent civil servants. When Hoffa's Teamsters were in their prime in 1960, only one in ten American government workers belonged to a union; now 36% do. In 2009 the number of unionists in America's public sector passed that of their fellow members in the private sector. In Britain, more than half of public-sector workers but only about 15% of private-sector ones are unionized.

如果工会主义者吉米·霍法今天还活着，他很可能会代表公务员了。1960年霍法的卡车司机工会鼎盛时期，美国政府工作人员中只有十分之一加入工会；如今这一比例已达36%。2009年，美国公共部门工会会员人数超过了私营部门。在英国，超过一半的公共部门工作人员加入了工会，而私营部门只有约15%。

There are three reasons for the public-sector unions' thriving. First, they can shut things down without suffering much in the way of consequences. Second, they are mostly bright and well-educated. A quarter of America's public-sector workers have a university degree. Third, they now dominate left-of-centre politics. Some of their ties go back a long way. Britain's Labor Party, as its name implies, has long been associated with trade unionism. Its current leader, Ed Miliband, owes his position to votes from public-sector unions.

公共部门工会的兴盛有三个原因。第一，他们可以停工而不必承担太多后果。第二，他们大多聪明、受过良好教育。美国公共部门工作人员中有四分之一拥有大学学位。第三，他们如今在中左翼政治中占主导地位。他们的某些联系由来已久。英国工党，顾名思义，长期以来与工会主义联系在一起。其现任领袖埃德·米利班德的地位就归功于公共部门工会的选票。

At the state level their influence can be even more fearsome. Mark Baldassare of the Public Policy Institute of California points out that much of the state's budget is patrolled by unions. The teachers' unions keep an eye on schools, the CCPOA on prisons and a variety of labor groups on health care.

在州一级，他们的影响力甚至更可怕。加州公共政策研究所的马克·巴尔达萨雷指出，加州预算的很大一部分都受到工会的监督。教师工会盯着学校，加州感化官员协会盯着监狱，各种劳工组织盯着医疗保健。

In many rich countries average wages in the state sector are higher than in the private one. But the real gains come in benefits and work practices. Politicians have repeatedly "backloaded" public-sector pay deals, keeping the pay increases modest but adding to holidays and especially pensions that are already generous.

在许多富裕国家，公共部门的平均工资高于私营部门。但真正的好处来自福利和工作惯例。政客们一再"变相拖延"公共部门的薪酬协议，保持工资增长适度，却增加了假期，尤其是本来就很丰厚的养老金。

Reform has been vigorously opposed, perhaps most notoriously in education, where charter schools, academies and merit pay all faced drawn-out battles. Even though there is plenty of evidence that the quality of the teachers is the most important variable, teachers' unions have fought against getting rid of bad ones and promoting good ones.

改革遭到强烈反对，其中在教育领域也许最为臭名昭著：特许学校、专科学校和绩效工资都面临旷日持久的斗争。尽管大量证据表明教师质量是最重要的变量，教师工会还是反对辞退差老师、提拔好老师。

As the cost to everyone else has become clearer, politicians have begun to clamp down. In Wisconsin the unions have rallied thousands of supporters against Scott Walker, the hardline Republican governor. But many within the public sector suffer under the current system, too.

随着这一制度对其他所有人的代价日益清晰，政客们已开始采取强硬措施。在威斯康星州，工会召集了数千名支持者，对抗强硬派共和党州长斯科特·沃克。但在现行制度下，公共部门内部也有很多人受害。

John Donahue at Harvard's Kennedy School points out that the norms of culture in Western civil services suit those who want to stay put but is bad for high achievers. The only American public-sector workers who earn well above $250,000 a year are university sports coaches and the president of the United States. Bankers' fat pay packets have attracted much criticism, but a public-sector system that does not reward high achievers may be a much bigger problem for America.

哈佛大学肯尼迪学院的约翰·多纳休指出，西方公务员制度的文化规范适合那些安于现状的人，但对高成就者不利。美国公共部门中年收入远超25万美元的工作人员，只有大学体育教练和美国总统。银行家的丰厚薪酬引来诸多批评，但一个不奖励高成就者的公共部门制度，对美国来说可能是个大得多的问题。
