[C] governmental ineffectiveness on moral issues.政府在道德议题上的无力。
[D] the wide misuse of integrity among institutions.各机构对诚信的广泛滥用。
💡 考场思路第一段：the only "sorting mechanism" in society should be profit and the market——她不满的是把利润和市场作为唯一分选机制所带来的后果（诚信缺失）。
逐项分析 [A] 当前分选机制的后果 → 正确；
[B] 不道德行为导致的财务损失 → 未提及；
[C] 政府在道德问题上的无能 → 片面；
[D] 机构对诚信的广泛滥用 → 她讲的是 dearth（缺失），不是 misuse（滥用）。
核心词汇
dearth n. 缺乏
integrity n. 诚信

accountable adj. 负责的

Part B · 新题型七选五（41–45）

【题目】关于阅读过程如何进行的议论文。从A-G中选出5句填入空白，2个干扰项。

解题关键：41空前讲"理解生词含义、推断词间关系、运用语法知识"，41空后讲"开始推断文本语境（谁在说话、对谁说、何时何地）"。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
Are we studying that text and trying to respond in a way that fulfils the requirement of a given course? Reading it simply for pleasure? Skimming it for information? Ways of reading on a train or in bed are likely to differ considerably from reading in a seminar room.
我们是在研读那篇文本、并试图以某种满足某门课程要求的方式作出回应吗？还是仅仅为了愉悦而读？或是略读以获取信息？在火车上或床上阅读的方式，很可能与在研讨室里阅读大不相同。
B
Factors such as the place and period in which we are reading, our gender, ethnicity, age and social class will encourage us towards certain interpretation but at the same time obscure or even close off others.
我们阅读的场所与时期、我们的性别、族裔、年龄和社会阶层等因素，会引导我们趋向某些解读，但同时也会遮蔽甚至封闭另一些解读。
C
If you are unfamiliar with words or idioms, you guess at their meaning, using clues presented in the context. On the assumption that they will become relevant later, you make a mental note of discourse entities as well as possible links between them.
如果你不熟悉某些词语或习语，你会借助语境提供的线索去猜测其义。基于它们日后会变得相关的假设，你会在脑中记下话语实体以及它们之间可能的联系。
D
In effect, you try to reconstruct the likely meanings or effects that any given sentence, image or reference might have had: These might be the ones the author intended.
实际上，你试图重构任何一个特定句子、意象或指涉可能具有的含义或效果：这些可能正是作者所意图的。
E
You make further inferences, for instance, about how the text may be significant to you, or about its validity—inferences that form the basis of a personal response for which the author will inevitably be far less responsible.
你会作出进一步的推断，例如关于该文本可能对你有何意义，或关于其有效性——这些推断构成了个人回应的基础，而作者对其所负的责任必然小得多。
F
In plays, novels and narrative poems, characters speak as constructs created by the author, not necessarily as mouthpieces for the author's own thoughts.
在戏剧、小说和叙事诗中，人物是作为作者所创造的建构在说话，而不一定是作者自身思想的传声筒。
G
Rather, we ascribe meanings to text on the basis of interaction between what we might call textual and contextual material: between kinds of organization or patterning we perceive in a text's formal structures (so especially its language structures) and various kinds of background, social knowledge, belief and attitude that we bring to the text.
毋宁说，我们是在所谓文本材料与语境材料的互动基础上赋予文本以意义：即我们在文本形式结构（尤其是其语言结构）中感知到的某种组织方式或模式，与我们带入文本的各类背景、社会知识、信念和态度之间的互动。
41
七选五
答案 C
匹配依据[C] "如果你不熟悉单词或习语，你会根据上下文线索猜测词义……"——紧接前文"identifying meanings for individual words"，且与后文"begin to infer a context"顺承。
42
七选五
答案 E
匹配依据42空前讲"comprehension...active engagement in inference and problem-solving"——理解是主动推断。[E] "你还会进一步推断，比如文本对你有何意义、其有效性如何……"——further inferences 承接 active engagement。
43
七选五
答案 G
匹配依据43空前讲"不是检索绝对固定的含义"。[G] "相反，我们是在文本材料与背景材料的相互作用基础上赋予文本意义……"——Rather 转折，对应 not retrieval of absolute meaning。
44
七选五
答案 B
匹配依据44空前讲"这种背景材料不可避免地反映了我们是谁"。[B] "诸如阅读地点和时期、性别、种族、年龄、社会阶层等因素会促使我们做出某些解读……"——factors such as... 具体展开"反映我们是谁"。
45
七选五
答案 A
匹配依据45空前讲"我们阅读特定文本还取决于我们对阅读它的特定兴趣"。[A] "我们是在学习那门课程要求的文本？还是为了消遣？还是为了获取信息而略读？"——连续问句对应"particular interest"。
干扰项[D] "你试图重建可能的含义"（重复前文）；[F] 戏剧小说中人物不是作者传声筒（与阅读过程无关）。
Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）
46
翻译
This movement, driven by powerful and diverse motivations, built a nation out of a wilderness and, by its nature, shaped the character and destiny of an uncharted continent.
在各种强大动机的推动下，这场迁移从荒野中造就了一个民族，并循其本质塑造了一片全新大陆的特点，决定了它的命运。
采分点① driven by... 由……推动；② built a nation out of a wilderness 从荒野中造就民族；③ uncharted continent 未知大陆。
47
翻译
The United States is the product of two principal forces—the immigration of European peoples with their varied ideas, customs, and national characteristics and the impact of a new country which modified these traits.
合众国是两股主要力量作用的产物：一是具有不同思想、风俗和民族特点的欧洲各民族的迁入；二是一个新国家因改变了这些特征而产生的影响。
采分点① principal forces 主要力量；② varied ideas, customs 不同思想风俗；③ modified these traits 改变了这些特征。
48
翻译
But the force of geographic conditions peculiar to America, the interplay of the varied national groups upon one another, and the sheer difficulty of maintaining old-world ways in a raw, new continent caused significant changes.
但美洲特有地理条件的作用，不同族裔间的相互影响，加上在一片蛮荒新大陆上维持旧大陆方式的巨大困难，所有这一切引起了意义深远的变化。
采分点① peculiar to 特有的；② interplay 相互作用；③ sheer difficulty 巨大困难；④ raw, new continent 蛮荒新大陆。
49
翻译
The first shiploads of immigrants bound for the territory which is now the United States crossed the Atlantic more than a hundred years after the 15th-and-16th-century explorations of North America.
在15、16世纪的北美大陆探险过去一百多年后，首批满载移民驶向今天合众国这片疆土的船只横穿过了大西洋。
采分点① shiploads of 满载……的船；② bound for 驶向；③ territory 领土。
50
翻译
The virgin forest with its richness and variety of trees was a real treasure-house which extended from Maine all the way down to Georgia.
郁郁葱葱、树种繁多的原始森林是一座从缅因一直向南绵延到佐治亚的天然宝库。
采分点① virgin forest 原始森林；② richness and variety 丰富多样；③ treasure-house 宝库；④ all the way down to 一直绵延到。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 推荐信

原题指令 Directions

Suppose you are the host of a club reading session. Write an email of about 100 words to the club members to recommend a book and explain your reasons. Do not sign your own name at the end of the email. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】假设你是读书会的主持人。写一封约100词的电子邮件，向俱乐部成员推荐一本书并说明原因。邮件末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

你将主持一次俱乐部读书会。写一封约100词的邮件，向俱乐部成员推荐一本书。说明推荐理由。落款 Li Ming。

审题

① 格式：邮件；② 语气：热情友好；③ 内容：书名+2-3条推荐理由。

参考范文

Dear Club Members,

I am writing to recommend a book for our next reading session: The Old Man and the Sea by Ernest Hemingway.

I recommend it for three reasons. First, it is a concise yet profound novella that can be finished within a few hours. Second, Hemingway's distinctive "iceberg" style leaves much to discuss in terms of language and symbolism. Finally, the story of the old fisherman's struggle against a giant marlin conveys a timeless spirit of perseverance that inspires every reader. I hope you will enjoy reading it.

Yours sincerely, Li Ming

【译文】

各位书友：

我写信是想为咱们下期的读书会推荐一本书：欧内斯特·海明威的《老人与海》。

推荐它有三点理由。首先，这是一部凝练而深刻的中篇，几小时便可读完。其次，海明威独特的"冰山"风格在语言与象征上极富讨论空间。最后，老渔夫与巨鱼搏斗的故事传递出永恒的不屈精神，激励着每一位读者。希望你们读得开心。

谨上，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文《手机时代的聚会》

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The picture shows four people sitting around a dinner table full of dishes, but each is bowing over his or her mobile phone, with no communication at all. The caption reads: "A gathering in the mobile-phone era".

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 四个人围坐在餐桌旁，面前摆满菜肴，但每个人都低头盯着自己的手机，彼此毫无交流。图题：手机时代的聚会。

图画描述

四个人围坐在餐桌旁，面前摆满菜肴，但每个人都低头盯着自己的手机，彼此毫无交流。图题：手机时代的聚会。

审题框架

三段式：①简要描述图画；②阐释含义（手机削弱了面对面交流、人情冷漠）；③给出评论（合理使用手机、重视面对面沟通）。160-200词。

参考范文

The cartoon depicts four people seated around a dinner table laden with food, yet each is bowing their head over a smartphone, exchanging no words with one another. The caption reads: a party in the age of mobile phones.

The drawing reveals a common malady of modern life: while mobile phones bring us unprecedented convenience, they are quietly alienating us from those around us. Many young people stare at screens even during family dinners or gatherings with friends, treating physical companionship as mere background noise. Left unchecked, this habit will erode genuine human bonds and leave our relationships hollow.

From my perspective, phones are tools, not masters. We should learn to put them aside when we are with family and friends. Only by treasuring face-to-face communication can we maintain authentic emotional ties and build a warmer society.

【译文】

漫画描绘了四人围坐在一桌佳肴旁，却各自低头盯着手机，彼此一言不发。图题为：手机时代的聚会。

这幅画揭示了现代生活的一种通病：手机带来空前便利的同时，也在悄悄疏离我们与身边人的距离。许多年轻人即便在家庭聚餐或朋友聚会时也紧盯屏幕，把现实陪伴当作背景噪音。若任其发展，这种习惯将侵蚀真挚的人际纽带，使关系变得空洞。

在我看来，手机是工具，而非主人。与亲友相处时，我们应学会放下手机。唯有珍视面对面交流，才能维系真诚的情感联结，构建更有温度的社会。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读

In Cambodia, the choice of a spouse is a complex one for the young male. It may involve not only his parents and his friends, 1 those of the young woman, but also a matchmaker. A young man can 2 a likely spouse on his own and then ask his parents to 3 the marriage negotiations, or the young man's parents may make the choice of a spouse, giving the child little to say in the selection. 4, a girl may veto the spouse her parents have chosen. 5 a spouse has been selected, each family investigates the other to make sure its child is marrying 6 a good family.

在柬埔寨，选择配偶对年轻男性来说是一件复杂的事。这不仅涉及他的父母和朋友，也涉及女方的父母和朋友，还可能涉及媒人。年轻男子可以自己选定一个合适的配偶，然后请父母安排婚姻谈判；或者年轻男子的父母可以替他选择配偶，孩子在选择过程中几乎没有发言权。从理论上讲，女孩可以否决父母为她选择的配偶。配偶选定之后，双方家庭都会调查对方，以确保自己的孩子嫁入/娶进一个好家庭。

The traditional wedding is a long and colorful affair. Formerly it lasted three days, 7 by the 1980s it more commonly lasted a day and a half. Buddhist priests offer a short sermon and 8 prayers of blessing. Parts of the ceremony involve ritual hair cutting, 9 cotton threads soaked in holy water around the bride's and groom's wrists, and 10 a candle around a circle of happily married and respected couples to bless the 11. Newlyweds traditionally move in with the wife's parents and may 12 with them up to a year, 13 they can build a new house nearby.

传统婚礼是一件漫长而丰富多彩的事。过去婚礼持续三天，但到了20世纪80年代，通常只持续一天半。佛教僧侣会做简短布道并念诵祈福祷文。仪式内容包括象征性的剪发、把浸过圣水的棉线系在新娘和新郎的手腕上，以及让一对婚姻幸福、受人尊敬的夫妇围成一圈，新人手捧蜡烛环绕他们行走，以祝福这桩婚姻。按传统，新婚夫妇会搬到妻子父母家住，可能和他们住上一年，直到能在附近盖起新房。

Divorce is legal and easy to 14, but not common. Divorced persons are 15 with some disapproval. Each spouse retains 16 property he or she 17 into the marriage, and jointly-acquired property is 18 equally. Divorced persons may remarry, but a gender prejudice 19 up: The divorced male doesn't have a waiting period before he can remarry 20 the woman must wait ten months.

离婚是合法的，也容易办理，但并不常见。离婚者会受到一些非议。配偶各方保留他/她带入婚姻的任何财产，共同获得的财产则平均分配。离婚者可以再婚，但性别偏见会显现出来：离婚男性再婚没有等待期，而女性必须等十个月。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

France, which prides itself as the global innovator of fashion, has decided its fashion industry has lost an absolute right to define physical beauty for women. Its lawmakers gave preliminary approval last week to a law that would make it a crime to employ ultra-thin models on runways. The parliament also agreed to ban websites that "incite excessive thinness" by promoting extreme dieting.

以全球时尚创新者自居的法国，已认定其时尚业已丧失了为女性定义形体美的绝对权利。其立法者上周初步批准了一项法律，将在T台上雇用超瘦模特定为犯罪。议会还同意取缔那些通过推广极端节食来"煽动过度消瘦"的网站。

Such measures have a couple of uplifting motives. They suggest beauty should not be defined by looks that end up impinging on health. That's a start. And the ban on ultra-thin models seems to go beyond protecting models from starving themselves to death—as some have done. It tells the fashion industry that it must take responsibility for the signal it sends women, especially teenage girls, about the social tape-measure they must use to determine their individual worth.

这些措施有几个令人振奋的动机。它们表明，美不应以最终损害健康的外表来定义。这仅仅是个开始。禁止超瘦模特似乎不仅是在保护模特免于饿死——确实有人这样做过。它还告诉时尚业，必须为其传递给女性、尤其是少女的信号负责，这个信号关乎她们用什么社会标尺来衡量自己的个人价值。

The bans, if fully enforced, would suggest to women (and many men) that they should not let others be arbiters of their beauty. And perhaps faintly, they hint that people should look to intangible qualities like character and intellect rather than dieting their way to size zero or wasp-waist physiques.

这些禁令若得到全面实施，将向女性（以及许多男性）表明：她们不应让别人来评判自己的美。或许还隐约暗示，人们应看重品格、才智等无形品质，而不是靠节食达到零码或蜂腰身材。

The French measures, however, rely too much on severe punishment to change a culture that still regards beauty as skin-deep—and bone-showing. Under the law, using a fashion model that does not meet a government-defined index of body mass could result in a $85,000 fine and six months in prison.

然而，法国的措施过于依赖严厉惩罚来改变一种仍然把美视为"肤浅——而且要露出骨头"的文化。根据该法律，雇用不符合政府规定体重指数的时装模特，可能面临8.5万美元罚款和六个月监禁。

The fashion industry knows it has an inherent problem in focusing on material adornment and idealized body types. In Denmark, the United States, and a few other countries, it is trying to set voluntary standards for models and fashion images that rely more on peer pressure for enforcement.

时尚业知道，它在注重物质装饰和理想化体型方面存在固有问题。在丹麦、美国和其他一些国家，时尚业正试图为模特和时尚形象制定自愿标准，更多依靠同侪压力来执行。

In contrast to France's actions, Denmark's fashion industry agreed last month on rules and sanctions regarding the age, health, and other characteristics of models. The newly revised Danish Fashion Ethical Charter clearly states: "We are aware of and take responsibility for the impact the fashion industry has on body ideals, especially on young people." The charter's main tool of enforcement is to deny access for designers and modeling agencies to Copenhagen Fashion Week (CFW), which is run by the Danish Fashion Institute. But in general it relies on a name-and-shame method of compliance.

与法国的行动形成对比，丹麦时尚业上月就模特年龄、健康及其他特征的规定和制裁达成一致。新修订的《丹麦时尚道德宪章》明确写道："我们意识到时尚业对身材理想的影响，尤其是对年轻人的影响，并为此负责。"宪章的主要执行工具是拒绝设计师和模特经纪机构参加由丹麦时装协会主办的哥本哈根时装周（CFW）。但总体上它依靠的是"点名羞辱"的合规方式。

Relying on ethical persuasion rather than law to address the misuse of body ideals may be the best step. Even better would be to help elevate notions of beauty beyond the material standards of a particular industry.

依靠道德劝导而非法律来解决对身材理想的滥用，或许是最好的一步。更好的做法是帮助将美的观念提升到超越某一行业物质标准的层次。

Text 2   英国乡村保护与城市开发之争（26–30）

For the first time in history more people live in towns than in the country. In Britain this has had a curious result. While polls show Britons rate "the countryside" alongside the royal family, Shakespeare and the National Health Service (NHS) as what makes them proudest of their country, this has limited political support.

人类历史上第一次，居住在城镇的人口超过了乡村。在英国，这产生了一个奇怪的结果。民意调查显示，英国人把"乡村"与王室、莎士比亚和国民医疗服务体系（NHS）并列为最让他们为国家自豪的事物，但这种情感在政治上获得的支持却有限。

A century ago Octavia Hill launched the National Trust not to rescue stylish houses but to save "the beauty of natural places for everyone forever." It was specifically to provide city dwellers with spaces for leisure where they could experience "a refreshing air." Hill's pressure later led to the creation of national parks and green belts. They don't make countryside any more, and every year concrete consumes more of it. It needs constant guardianship.

一个世纪前，奥克塔薇娅·希尔创立了国民信托，不是为了拯救时尚的建筑，而是为了"为所有人永远保住自然之地的美"。它专门为城市居民提供休闲空间，让他们能体验"清新的空气"。希尔的压力后来促成了国家公园和绿化带的建立。但这些不会再造就乡村，混凝土每年都在吞噬更多乡村。乡村需要持续的守护。

At the next election none of the big parties seem likely to endorse this sentiment. The Conservatives' planning reform explicitly gives rural development priority over conservation, even authorising "off-plan" building where local people might object. The concept of sustainable development has been defined as profitable. Labour likewise wants to discontinue local planning where councils oppose development. The Liberal Democrats are silent. Only Ukip, sensing its chance, has sided with those pleading for a more considered approach to using green land. Its Campaign to Protect Rural England struck terror into many local Conservative parties.

在下届大选中，似乎没有哪个大党会支持这种情感。保守党的规划改革明确把乡村开发置于保护之上，甚至在当地人可能反对的地方批准"期房"建设。可持续发展的概念已被定义为有利可图。工党同样想取消地方议会反对开发的规划。自由民主党保持沉默。只有独立党嗅到了机会，站到了那些呼吁更审慎使用绿地的人一边。它的"保护英格兰乡村运动"令许多地方保守党胆战心惊。

The sensible place to build new houses, factories and offices is where people are, in cities and towns where infrastructure is in place. The London agents Stirling Ackroyd recently identified enough sites for half a million houses in the London area alone, with no intrusion on green belt. What is true of London is even truer of the provinces.

建造新住宅、工厂和办公楼的合理地点是有人的地方，在基础设施已经完备的城镇。伦敦中介Stirling Ackroyd最近仅在伦敦地区就找到了足够建造50万套住宅的地块，且不侵占绿化带。伦敦如此，各郡更是如此。

The idea that "housing crisis" equals "concreted meadows" is pure lobby talk. The issue is not the need for more houses but, as always, where to put them. Under lobby pressure, George Osborne favours rural new-build against urban renovation and renewal. He favours out-of-town shopping sites against high streets. This is not a free market but a biased one. Rural towns and villages have grown and will always grow. They do so best where building sticks to their edges and respects their character. We do not ruin urban conservation areas. Why ruin rural ones?

"住房危机"就等于"把草地浇上混凝土"的说法纯粹是游说集团的说辞。问题不在于需要更多房子，而一如既往地在于把它们建在哪里。在游说压力下，乔治·奥斯本偏好乡村新建而非城市改造和更新。他偏好城外购物中心而非商业街。这不是自由市场，而是有偏向的市场。乡村城镇一直在发展，也将永远发展。它们在建筑紧贴边缘、尊重其特色的情况下发展得最好。我们不破坏城市保护区，为什么要破坏乡村保护区？

Development should be planned, not let rip. After the Netherlands, Britain is Europe's most crowded country. Half a century of town and country planning has enabled it to retain an enviable rural coherence, while still permitting low-density urban living. There is no doubt of the alternative—the corrupted landscapes of southern Portugal, Spain or Ireland. Avoiding this rather than promoting it should unite the left and right of the political spectrum.

发展应该被规划，而非放任自流。英国是继荷兰之后欧洲最拥挤的国家。半个世纪的城乡规划使其得以保留令人羡慕的乡村连贯性，同时仍允许低密度的城市生活。另一种选择毫无疑问——葡萄牙南部、西班牙或爱尔兰那些被破坏的景观。避免这种局面而非促成它，应该能团结政治光谱上的左右两派。

Text 3   企业社会责任（CSR）的经济价值（31–35）

"There is one and only one social responsibility of business," wrote Milton Friedman, a Nobel prize-winning economist, "That is, to use its resources and engage in activities designed to increase its profits." But even if you accept Friedman's premise and regard corporate social responsibility (CSR) policies as a waste of shareholders' money, things may not be absolutely clear-cut. New research suggests that CSR may create monetary value for companies—at least when they are prosecuted for corruption.

诺贝尔奖得主、经济学家米尔顿·弗里德曼写道："企业有且只有一种社会责任，那就是利用其资源、从事旨在增加利润的活动。"但即使你接受弗里德曼的前提，把企业社会责任（CSR）政策视为浪费股东的钱，事情也未必完全绝对。新研究表明，CSR可能为企业创造货币价值——至少当企业因腐败被起诉时是这样。

The largest firms in America and Britain together spend more than $15 billion a year on CSR, according to an estimate by EPG, a consulting firm. This could add value to their businesses in three ways. First, consumers may take CSR spending as a "signal" that a company's products are of high quality. Second, customers may be willing to buy a company's products as an indirect way to donate to the good causes it helps. And third, through a more diffuse "halo effect," whereby its good deeds earn it greater consideration from consumers and others.

据咨询公司EPG估计，美国和英国最大的公司每年在CSR上的总投入超过150亿美元。这可能通过三种方式为企业增值。第一，消费者可能把CSR支出视为公司产品质量高的"信号"。第二，顾客可能愿意购买某公司产品，作为间接为其公益事业捐款的方式。第三，通过更广泛的"光环效应"——其善行赢得消费者和其他人更多的好感。

Previous studies on CSR have had trouble differentiating these effects because consumers can be affected by all three. A recent study attempts to separate them by looking at bribery prosecutions under America's Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA). It argues that since prosecutors do not consume a company's products as part of their investigations, they could be influenced only by the halo effect.

以往关于CSR的研究难以区分这三种效应，因为消费者可能同时受到三者影响。最近一项研究试图通过考察美国《反海外腐败法》（FCPA）下的贿赂起诉来区分它们。研究认为，由于检察官在调查中不消费公司产品，他们只能受光环效应影响。

The study found that, among prosecuted firms, those with the most comprehensive CSR programmes tended to get more lenient penalties. Their analysis ruled out the possibility that it was firms' political influence, rather than their CSR stand, that accounted for the leniency: Companies that contributed more to political campaigns did not receive lower fines.

研究发现，在被起诉的企业中，CSR项目最全面的企业往往获得更宽大的处罚。他们的分析排除了这种可能性：是企业的政治影响力而非其CSR立场导致了宽大处理——向政治竞选捐款更多的企业并未获得更低罚款。

In all, the study concludes that whereas prosecutors should only evaluate a case based on its merits, they do seem to be influenced by a company's record in CSR. "We estimate that either eliminating a substantial labour-rights concern, such as child labour, or increasing corporate giving by about 20% results in fines that generally are 40% lower than the typical punishment for bribing foreign officials," says one researcher.

总之，研究得出结论：尽管检察官理应只根据案情本身来评估，但他们似乎确实受到公司CSR记录的影响。一位研究者说："我们估计，消除一个重大劳工权益问题（如童工），或把企业捐赠增加约20%，可使罚款比贿赂外国官员的典型处罚低约40%。"

Researchers admit that their study does not answer the question of how much businesses ought to spend on CSR. Nor does it reveal how much companies are banking on the halo effect, rather than the other possible benefits, when they decide their do-gooding policies. But at least they have demonstrated that when companies get into trouble with the law, evidence of good character can win them a less costly punishment.

研究者承认，他们的研究没有回答企业应该在CSR上花多少钱的问题。也没有揭示企业在决定行善政策时，有多大程度指望光环效应而非其他可能的好处。但至少他们证明了：当企业陷入法律麻烦时，良好品格的证据能为它们赢得成本更低的处罚。

Text 4   纽约时报纸质版的未来（36–40）

There will eventually come a day when The New York Times ceases to publish stories on newsprint. Exactly when that day will be is a matter of debate. "Sometime in the future," the paper's publisher said back in 2010.

总有一天，《纽约时报》将不再在新闻纸上刊登报道。这一天究竟何时到来，是个有争议的问题。"未来的某个时候，"该报出版人早在2010年就说过。

Nostalgia for ink on paper and the rustle of pages aside, there's plenty of incentive to ditch print. The infrastructure required to make a physical newspaper—printing presses, delivery trucks—isn't just expensive; it's excessive at a time when online-only competitors don't have the same set of financial constraints. Readers are migrating away from print anyway. And though print ad sales still dwarf their online and mobile counterparts, revenue from print is still declining.

撇开对纸上油墨和翻页沙沙声的怀旧不谈，放弃纸质版的理由也十分充分。制造实体报纸所需的基础设施——印刷机、送报卡车——不仅昂贵；在纯线上竞争对手没有同样财务约束的时代，这种开销更是过度。读者本来也在从纸质版迁走。尽管纸质广告收入仍远超线上和移动端，但纸质收入仍在下降。

Overhead may be high and circulation lower, but rushing to eliminate its print edition would be a mistake, says BuzzFeed CEO Jonah Peretti.

BuzzFeed首席执行官乔纳·佩雷蒂表示，尽管运营成本高、发行量下降，但急于砍掉纸质版将是一个错误。

Peretti says the Times shouldn't waste time getting out of the print business, but only if they go about doing it the right way. "Figuring out a way to accelerate that transition would make sense for them," he said, "but if you discontinue it, you're going to have your most loyal customers really upset with you."

佩雷蒂说，《纽约时报》不该浪费时间退出纸质业务，但前提是要以正确方式去做。"找到加速这一转型的方法对他们来说是有意义的，"他说，"但如果你停掉它，你会让最忠实的顾客非常不满。"

Sometimes that's worth making a change anyway. Peretti gives the example of Netflix discontinuing its DVD-mailing service to focus on streaming. "It was seen as a blunder," he said. The move turned out to be foresighted. And if Peretti were in charge at the Times? "I wouldn't pick a year to end print," he said. "I would raise prices and make it into more of a legacy product."

有时候这种改变终究是值得的。佩雷蒂举了Netflix停掉DVD邮寄服务、专注流媒体的例子。"这在当时被视为一个错误，"他说。结果这一步被证明是有远见的。如果佩雷蒂掌管《纽约时报》呢？"我不会选定一个年份停掉纸质版，"他说。"我会提高价格，把它做成一种更像'传承产品'的东西。"

The most loyal customers would still get the product they favor, the idea goes, and they'd feel like they were helping sustain the quality of something they believe in. "So if you're overpaying for print, you could feel like you were helping," Peretti said. "Then increase it at a higher rate each year and essentially try to generate additional revenue." In other words, if you're going to make a print product, make it for the people who are already obsessed with it. Which may be what the Times is doing already. Getting the print edition seven days a week costs nearly $500 a year—more than twice as much as a digital-only subscription.

其思路是，最忠实的顾客仍会得到他们喜欢的产品，而且会觉得自己在帮助维持他们所信仰之物的品质。"所以如果你为纸质版多付了钱，你会觉得自己在帮忙，"佩雷蒂说。"然后每年以更高的幅度提价，本质上就是努力创造额外收入。"换言之，如果你要做纸质产品，就为那些已经痴迷于它的人做。而这可能正是《纽约时报》已经在做的。一周七天拿到纸质版一年要花近500美元——是纯数字订阅的两倍多。

"It's a really hard thing to do and it's a tremendous luxury that BuzzFeed doesn't have a legacy business," Peretti remarked. "But we're going to have questions like that where we have things we're doing that don't make sense when the market changes and the world changes. In those situations, it's better to be more aggressive than less aggressive."

"这是一件非常难做到的事，而BuzzFeed没有传统业务是一种巨大的奢侈，"佩雷蒂说。"但我们也会遇到类似问题：当市场和世界变化时，我们所做的一些事就不再合理。在那种情况下，更激进一些总比不够激进修好。"

匹配依据本段讲"Enlist the support of professionals...Hire a personal stylist...Work with a professional photographer"——找专业人士帮忙。对应 E. Work with professionals。
45
小标题匹配
答案 F
匹配依据本段讲"形象升级不是为了臭美，而是减少决策疲劳、买标准工作服、一次买齐"——让它高效。对应 F. Make it efficient。

Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）
46
翻译
We don't have to learn how to be mentally healthy; it is built into us in the same way that our bodies know how to heal a cut or mend a broken bone.
我们的心理健康不是学来的；它是我们生来就有的，正如同我们的身体知道如何愈合伤口或修复断骨一样。
采分点① be built into us 内置于我们/天生具有；② heal a cut 愈合伤口；③ mend a broken bone 修复断骨。
47
翻译
Our mental health doesn't really go anywhere; like the sun behind a cloud, it can be temporarily hidden from view, but it is fully capable of being restored in an instant.
心理健康并没有真的离开；宛如云朵后面的太阳，它虽然可能暂离我们的视线，但完全能在转瞬之间重现。
采分点① temporarily hidden 暂时被遮蔽；② be capable of 能够；③ in an instant 瞬间。
48
翻译
Mental health allows us to view others with sympathy if they are having troubles, with kindness if they are in pain, and with unconditional love no matter who they are.
健康的心理让我们在他人遇到困难时心怀同情，遭受苦痛时心怀善意，不论他们是谁都心怀无条件的爱。
采分点① view others with sympathy 以同情看待他人；② unconditional love 无条件的爱。
49
翻译
Although mental health is the cure-all for living our lives, it is perfectly ordinary as you will see that it has been there to direct you through all your difficult decisions.
尽管心理健康是我们生活的万能良药，但它又再寻常不过，因为你会发现，它一直在那里引领你完成所有艰难的抉择。
采分点① cure-all 万灵药；② perfectly ordinary 再寻常不过；③ direct you through 引领你度过。
50
翻译
As you will come to see, knowing that mental health is always available and knowing to trust it allow us to slow down to the moment and live life happily.
你终会明白，懂得心理健康无时不在并懂得信赖它，这能让我们慢下来活在每一刻，快乐地生活着。
采分点① available 可获得的/存在的；② slow down to the moment 慢下来活在当下；③ live life happily 快乐地生活。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 通知

原题指令 Directions

Suppose you are a librarian at a university. Write a notice of about 100 words to new international students, providing information about the library. Do not sign your own name at the end of the notice. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】假设你是大学图书馆员。写一则约100词的通知，向新入学的留学生提供图书馆相关信息。通知末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

假设你是大学图书馆员。写一则约100词的通知，向新入学的国际学生提供图书馆相关信息。落款 Li Ming。

审题

① 格式：通知（NOTICE）；② 内容：开放时间、借阅规则、资源服务、培训等。

参考范文

NOTICE

Welcome to our university! To help you make the most of the library, here is some essential information for new international students.

The library is open from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. on weekdays and from 9:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. on weekends. Each student may borrow up to five books for 30 days. With your student ID, you can also access our online databases and e-journals 24 hours a day. A free orientation session will be held in the main hall next Monday at 2:00 p.m.

We look forward to seeing you in the library!

Li Ming
The Library

【译文】

通知

欢迎来到我们大学！为帮助新入学的国际学生充分利用图书馆，以下提供若干重要信息。

图书馆工作日开放时间为早8:00至晚10:00，周末为早9:00至晚9:00。每位学生最多可借5本书，借期30天。凭学生证可全天候访问我们的在线数据库与电子期刊。下周一14:00将在主厅举办免费的导览培训。

期待在图书馆见到你！

李明
图书馆

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文《与其只提要求，不如做个榜样》

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The left picture shows a father sitting on the sofa watching TV and shouting at his son, "Study hard!" while the son sits at his desk looking upset. The right picture shows the father and son both studying at their desks. The title is "Setting an example works better than mere demands".

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 左图：父亲坐在沙发上看电视，对儿子喊“儿子，你给我好好学习！”，儿子坐在书桌前愁眉苦脸。右图：父子俩各自坐在书桌前认真学习。图题：与其只提要求，不如做个榜样。

图画描述

左图：父亲坐在沙发上看电视，对儿子喊"儿子，你给我好好学习！"，儿子坐在书桌前愁眉苦脸。右图：父子俩各自坐在书桌前认真学习。图题：与其只提要求，不如做个榜样。

审题框架

三段式：①简要描述图画（两种教育方式对比）；②阐释含义（身教重于言传、父母榜样的力量）；③给出评论。160-200词。

参考范文

The cartoon presents a thought-provoking contrast. In the left picture, a father lounges comfortably before the TV, shouting at his son to "study hard," while the boy looks worried; in the right picture, both father and son are reading diligently at their desks. The caption reads: "Rather than merely making demands, it is better to set an example."

The drawing conveys a universal principle in education: parents should lead by example rather than by words. All too often, adults themselves indulge in television or smartphones while scolding children for being lazy. Such double standards rarely work, because children naturally imitate what they see. A parent who reads, thinks and works hard will inspire a child far more effectively than any endless lecture. After all, actions speak louder than words.

From my perspective, this principle applies not only to family education but also to teachers, leaders and anyone in a position of influence. True education lies not in what we say, but in what we do. Only when we become the people we want our children to be can we expect them to follow.

【译文】

漫画呈现了一组发人深省的对比。左图中，父亲悠闲地坐在电视前，对儿子喊"你给我好好学习！"，男孩则愁眉苦脸；右图中，父子二人都在书桌前认真学习。图题写道："与其只提要求，不如做个榜样。"

这幅画传达了教育中一条普适原则：父母应以身作则，而非仅以言教。太多成年人自己沉迷电视或手机，却责怪孩子懒惰。这种双重标准很少奏效，因为孩子天然会模仿所见。一个爱读书、勤思考、肯努力的父母，远比任何喋喋不休的说教更能激励孩子。毕竟，身教重于言教。

在我看来，这一原则不仅适用于家庭教育，也适用于教师、领导者以及任何具有影响力的人。真正的教育不在于我们说了什么，而在于我们做了什么。唯有当我们自己成为希望孩子成为的人，才能期待他们追随。

Could a hug a day keep the doctor away? The answer may be a resounding "yes!" 1 helping you feel close and 2 to people you care about, it turns out that hugs can bring a 3 of health benefits to your body and mind. Believe it or not, a warm embrace might even help you 4 getting sick this winter.

每天一个拥抱能让医生远离吗？答案可能是一声响亮的"能！"。除了帮助你与关心的人感到亲密和相连之外，事实证明，拥抱还能给你的身心带来大量健康益处。信不信由你，一个温暖的拥抱甚至可能帮你在这个冬天避免生病。

In a recent study 5 over 400 healthy adults, researchers from Carnegie Mellon University in Pennsylvania examined the effects of perceived social support and the receipt of hugs 6 the participants' susceptibility to developing the common cold after being 7 to the virus. People who perceived greater social support were less likely to come 8 with a cold, and the researchers 9 that the stress-reducing effects of hugging 10 about 32 percent of that beneficial effect. 11 among those who got a cold, the ones who felt greater social support and received more frequent hugs had less severe 12.

在最近一项涉及400多名健康成年人的研究中，宾夕法尼亚州卡内基梅隆大学的研究人员考察了感知到的社会支持和获得拥抱对参与者在接触病毒后患普通感冒易感性的影响。感知到更多社会支持的人更不容易感冒，研究人员计算出，拥抱的减压作用解释了该有益效果中约32%的部分。即使在那些已经感冒的人中，感受到更多社会支持、获得更频繁拥抱的人症状也更轻。

"Hugging protects people who are under stress from the 13 risk for colds that's usually 14 with stress," notes Sheldon Cohen, a professor of psychology at Carnegie. Hugging "is a marker of intimacy and helps 15 the feeling that others are there to help 16 difficulty."

卡内基梅隆大学心理学教授谢尔登·科恩指出："拥抱能保护处于压力下的人，使他们免受通常与压力相关的更高感冒风险的影响。"拥抱"是亲密的标志，有助于产生一种感觉——在面对困难时，有人会伸出援手。"

Some experts 17 the stress-reducing, health-related benefits of hugging to the release of oxytocin, often called "the bonding hormone" 18 it promotes attachment in relationships, including that between mothers and their newborn babies. Oxytocin is made primarily in the central lower part of the brain, and some of it is released into the bloodstream. But some of it 19 in the brain, where it 20 mood, behavior and physiology.

一些专家把拥抱的减压及健康相关益处归因于催产素的释放——催产素通常被称为"亲密激素"，因为它能促进关系中的依恋，包括母亲与新生婴儿之间的依恋。催产素主要在大脑中下部产生，一部分释放到血液中。但有一部分留在大脑中，在那里它影响情绪、行为和生理。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

First two hours, now three hours—this is how far in advance authorities are recommending people show up to catch a domestic flight, at least at some major U.S. airports with increasingly massive security lines.

先是两小时，现在是三小时——当局建议人们提前这么久到机场搭乘国内航班，至少在一些安检队伍越来越长的美国主要机场是这样。

Americans are willing to tolerate time-consuming security procedures in return for increased safety. The crash of EgyptAir Flight 804, which terrorists may have downed over the Mediterranean Sea, provides another tragic reminder of why. But demanding too much of air travelers or providing too little security in return undermines public support for the process. And it should: Wasted time is a drag on Americans' economic and private lives, not to mention infuriating.

美国人愿意忍受耗时的安检程序，以换取更高的安全。埃及航空804航班可能被恐怖分子在地中海上空击落，这一事件再次悲剧性地提醒人们为何要如此。但对航空旅客要求过多、或回报给他们的安全太少，会削弱公众对这一程序的支持。而且确实应该如此：浪费的时间拖累美国人的经济和私人生活，更不必说令人愤怒。

Last year, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) found in a secret check that undercover investigators were able to sneak weapons—both fake and real—past airport security nearly every time they tried. Enhanced security measures since then, combined with a rise in airline travel due to the improving economy and low oil prices, have resulted in long waits at major airports such as Chicago's O'Hare International. It is not yet clear how much more effective airline security has become—but the lines are obvious.

去年，运输安全管理局（TSA）在一次秘密检查中发现，卧底调查人员几乎每次都能把武器——假的和真的——偷偷带过机场安检。此后加强的安检措施，加上经济好转和低油价带来的航空出行增加，导致芝加哥奥黑尔国际机场等主要机场排队时间漫长。航空安检到底有效了多少尚不清楚——但队伍是显而易见的。

Part of the issue is that the government did not anticipate the steep increase in airline travel, so the TSA is now rushing to get new screeners on the line. Part of the issue is that airports have only so much room for screening lanes. Another factor may be that more people are trying to overpack their carry-on bags to avoid checked-baggage fees, though the airlines strongly dispute this.

部分问题在于政府没有预料到航空出行的急剧增长，所以TSA现在正急着让新安检员上岗。部分问题在于机场只有有限的空间设置安检通道。另一个因素可能是，越来越多的人试图把手提包塞得满满当当，以避免托运行李费，尽管航空公司强烈反对这一说法。

There is one step the TSA could take that would not require remodeling airports or rushing to hire: Enroll more people in the PreCheck program. PreCheck is supposed to be a win-win for travelers and the TSA. Passengers who pass a background check are eligible to use expedited screening lanes. This allows the TSA to focus on travelers who are higher risk, saving time for everyone involved. The TSA wants to enroll 25 million people in PreCheck.

TSA可以采取一个不需要改造机场或急着招人 的措施：让更多人加入PreCheck计划。PreCheck本应是旅客和TSA双赢的安排。通过背景调查的乘客有资格使用快速安检通道。这使TSA能把注意力集中在高风险旅客身上，为所有相关人员节省时间。TSA计划让2500万人加入PreCheck。

It has not gotten anywhere close to that, and one big reason is sticker shock: Passengers must pay $85 every five years to process their background checks. Since the beginning, this price tag has been PreCheck's fatal flaw. Upcoming reforms might bring the price to a more reasonable level. But Congress should look into doing so directly, by helping to finance PreCheck enrollment or to cut costs in other ways.

它远未达到这一目标，一个重要原因是价格冲击：乘客每五年必须支付85美元来处理背景调查。从一开始，这个价格标签就是PreCheck的致命缺陷。即将到来的改革可能把价格降到更合理的水平。但国会应该直接介入，通过资助PreCheck注册或以其他方式降低成本。

The TSA cannot continue diverting resources into underused PreCheck lanes while most of the traveling public suffers in unnecessary lines. It is long past time to make the program work.

TSA不能继续把资源投入使用不足的PreCheck通道，而让大多数出行公众在不必要的队伍中受苦。让这个计划真正发挥作用早就该提上日程了。

21

Text 2   夏威夷莫纳克亚山天文台争议（26–30）

"The ancient Hawaiians were astronomers," wrote Queen Liliuokalani, Hawaii's last reigning monarch, in 1897. Star watchers were among the most esteemed members of Hawaiian society. Sadly, all is not well with astronomy in Hawaii today. Protests have erupted over construction of the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT), a giant observatory that promises to revolutionize humanity's view of the cosmos.

"古代夏威夷人是天文学家，"夏威夷最后一位在位君主利留卡拉尼女王在1897年写道。观星者曾是夏威夷社会最受尊敬的成员之一。可悲的是，今天夏威夷的天文学并不顺利。三十米望远镜（TMT）的建设引发了抗议，这是一座有望彻底改变人类宇宙观的巨型观测站。

At issue is the TMT's planned location on Mauna Kea, a dormant volcano worshiped by some Hawaiians as the piko, that connects the Hawaiian Islands to the heavens. But Mauna Kea is also home to some of the world's most powerful telescopes. Rested in the Pacific Ocean, Mauna Kea's peak rises above the bulk of our planet's dense atmosphere, where conditions allow telescopes to obtain images of unsurpassed clarity.

争议的焦点是TMT计划建于莫纳克亚山——这座休眠火山被一些夏威夷人尊为"脐部"，是连接夏威夷群岛与天堂的地方。但莫纳克亚山也是世界上一些最强大望远镜的所在地。莫纳克亚山坐落于太平洋中，其峰顶高出地球大部分稠密大气层，那里的条件使望远镜能获得无比清晰的图像。

Opposition to telescopes on Mauna Kea is nothing new. A small but vocal group of Hawaiians and environmentalists have long viewed their presence as disrespect for sacred land and a painful reminder of the occupation of what was once a sovereign nation.

反对在莫纳克亚山建望远镜并非新鲜事。一小群声音响亮的夏威夷人和环保主义者长期以来一直认为，望远镜的存在是对圣地的不敬，也是对这个曾经主权国家被占领的痛苦提醒。

Some blame for the current controversy belongs to astronomers. In their eagerness to build bigger telescopes, they forgot that science is not the only way of understanding the world. They did not always prioritize the protection of Mauna Kea's fragile ecosystems or its holiness to the islands' inhabitants. Hawaiian culture is not a relic of the past; it is a living culture undergoing a renaissance today.

当前这场争议的部分责任在天文学家。他们急于建造更大的望远镜，却忘了科学不是理解世界的唯一方式。他们并不总是优先考虑保护莫纳克亚山脆弱的生态系统，或其对岛上居民的神圣意义。夏威夷文化不是过去的遗迹；它是今天正在复兴的活的文化。

Yet science has a cultural history, too, with roots going back to the dawn of civilization. The same curiosity to find what lies beyond the horizon that first brought early Polynesians to Hawaii's shores inspires astronomers today to explore the heavens. Calls to disassemble all telescopes on Mauna Kea or to ban future development there ignore the reality that astronomy and Hawaiian culture both seek to answer big questions about who we are, where we come from and where we are going. Perhaps that is why we explore the starry skies, as if answering a primal calling to know ourselves and our true ancestral homes.

然而，科学也有文化历史，其根源可以追溯到文明之初。最初把早期波利尼西亚人带到夏威夷海岸的那种寻找地平线之外事物的好奇心，如今正激励着天文学家探索天空。要求拆除莫纳克亚山上所有望远镜、或禁止未来在那里开发的呼声，忽视了这样一个现实：天文学和夏威夷文化都在寻求关于我们是谁、从何而来、向何而去的重大问题的答案。也许这就是我们探索星空的原因，仿佛在回应一种原始召唤——去了解我们自己和我们真正的祖居之地。

The astronomy community is making compromises to change its use of Mauna Kea. The TMT site was chosen to minimize the telescope's visibility around the island and to avoid archaeological and environmental impact. To limit the number of telescopes on Mauna Kea, old ones will be removed at the end of their lifetimes and their sites returned to a natural state. There is no reason why everyone cannot be welcomed on Mauna Kea to embrace their cultural heritage and to study the stars.

天文学界正在做出妥协，改变其对莫纳克亚山的使用。TMT选址旨在尽量减少望远镜在岛上的可见度，并避免对考古和环境的影响。为限制莫纳克亚山上望远镜的数量，旧望远镜将在使用寿命结束时被移除，其旧址恢复自然状态。没有理由不让所有人都被欢迎到莫纳克亚山来拥抱他们的文化遗产、研究星空。

Text 3   GDP与幸福感：英国脱欧启示（31–35）

Robert F. Kennedy once said that a country's GDP measures "everything except that which makes life worthwhile." With Britain voting to leave the European Union, and GDP already predicted to slow as a result, it is now a timely moment to assess what he was referring to.

罗伯特·F·肯尼迪曾说，一个国家的GDP衡量的是"除了让生活有意义之物以外的一切"。随着英国投票脱离欧盟，且GDP已预计因此放缓，现在正是评估他所指为何的恰当时刻。

The question of GDP and its usefulness has annoyed policymakers for over half a century. Many argue that it is a flawed concept. It measures things that do not matter and misses things that do. By most recent measures, the UK's GDP has been the envy of the Western world, with record low unemployment and high growth figures. If everything was going so well, then why did over 17 million people vote for Brexit, despite the warnings about what it could do to their country's economic prospects?

GDP及其有用性的问题已困扰政策制定者半个多世纪。许多人认为它是一个有缺陷的概念。它衡量无关紧要的东西，却漏掉真正重要的东西。按最新衡量标准，英国的GDP一直是西方世界羡慕的对象——失业率创纪录新低、增长数据强劲。如果一切如此美好，那么为什么超过1700万人不顾脱欧对国家经济前景可能造成的警告，仍投票支持脱欧？

A recent annual study of countries and their ability to convert growth into well-being sheds some light on that question. Across the 163 countries measured, the UK is one of the poorest performers in ensuring that economic growth is translated into meaningful improvements for its citizens. Rather than just focusing on GDP, over 40 different sets of criteria from health, education and civil society engagement have been measured to get a more rounded assessment of how countries are performing.

最近一项关于各国将增长转化为幸福感能力的年度研究为这个问题提供了一些启示。在被测的163个国家中，英国在确保经济增长转化为公民有意义改善方面表现最差之一。该研究不仅仅关注GDP，还衡量了来自健康、教育和公民社会参与等方面的40多套不同标准，以更全面地评估各国表现。

While all of these countries face their own challenges, there are a number of consistent themes. Yes, there has been a budding economic recovery since the 2008 global crash, but in key indicators in areas such as health and education, major economies have continued to decline. Yet this isn't the case with all countries. Some relatively poor European countries have seen huge improvements across measures including civil society, income equality and the environment.

尽管所有这些国家都面临各自的挑战，但存在一些一致的主题。诚然，自2008年全球危机以来出现了初步经济复苏，但在健康、教育等关键领域的重要指标上，主要经济体持续下滑。然而并非所有国家都是如此。一些相对贫穷的欧洲国家在公民社会、收入平等和环境等指标上都取得了巨大进步。

This is a lesson that rich countries can learn: When GDP is no longer regarded as the sole measure of a country's success, the world looks very different.

这是富裕国家可以吸取的教训：当GDP不再被视为衡量国家成功的唯一标准时，世界看起来就大不相同了。

So, what Kennedy was referring to was that while GDP has been the most common method for measuring the economic activity of nations, as a measure, it is no longer enough. It does not include important factors such as environmental quality or education outcomes—all things that contribute to a person's sense of well-being.

那么，肯尼迪所指的是，虽然GDP一直是衡量国家经济活动最常用的方法，但作为一种衡量标准，它已经不够了。它不包括环境质量或教育成果等重要因素——所有那些有助于一个人幸福感的东西。

The sharp hit to growth predicted around the world and in the UK could lead to a decline in the everyday services we depend on for our well-being and for growth. But policymakers who refocus efforts on improving well-being rather than simply worrying about GDP figures could avoid the forecasted doom and may even see progress.

全球及英国预计将遭受的增长重创，可能导致我们赖以追求幸福感和增长的日常服务水平下降。但如果政策制定者把努力重新聚焦于改善幸福感，而不是仅仅担忧GDP数字，他们就能避免预言中的厄运，甚至可能看到进步。

Text 4   最高法院裁决与政府腐败定义（36–40）

In a rare unanimous ruling, the US Supreme Court has overturned the corruption conviction of a former Virginia governor, Robert McDonnell. But it did so while holding its nose at the ethics of his conduct, which included accepting gifts such as a Rolex watch and a Ferrari automobile from a company seeking access to government.

在一项罕见的一致裁决中，美国最高法院推翻了对前弗吉尼亚州州长罗伯特·麦克唐纳的腐败定罪。但它在这样做的同时，也对其行为的伦理表示嗤之以鼻——他曾从一家寻求接触政府的公司收受劳力士手表、法拉利汽车等礼物。

The high court's decision said the judge in Mr. McDonnell's trial failed to tell a jury that it must look only at his "official acts," or the former governor's decisions on "specific" and "unsettled" issues related to his duties.

高等法院的裁决说，麦克唐纳案审判中的法官未能告诉陪审团，必须只审视他的"公务行为"，即前州长在与职责相关的"具体"和"未决"问题上的决定。

Merely helping a gift-giver gain access to other officials, unless done with clear intent to pressure those officials, is not corruption, the justices found.

大法官们认定，仅仅帮助送礼者接触其他官员，除非带有明确向那些官员施压的意图，否则不构成腐败。

The court did suggest that accepting favors in return for opening doors is "distasteful" and "nasty." But under anti-bribery laws, proof must be made of concrete benefits, such as approval of a contract or regulation. Simply arranging a meeting, making a phone call, or hosting an event is not an "official act."

法院确实表示，为开门提供回报而收受好处是"令人厌恶的"和"肮脏的"。但根据反贿赂法，必须证明有具体利益，如批准某项合同或规定。仅仅安排一次会议、打一通电话或举办一次活动，不算"公务行为"。

The court's ruling is legally sound in defining a kind of favoritism that is not criminal. Elected leaders must be allowed to help supporters deal with bureaucratic problems without fear of prosecution of bribery. "The basic compact underlying representative government," wrote Chief Justice John Roberts for the court, "assumes that public officials will hear from their constituents and act on their concerns."

该裁决在法律上合理地界定了一种不构成犯罪的偏袒行为。民选领导人必须被允许帮助支持者处理官僚问题，而无需担忧被诉贿赂。首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨代表法院写道："代议制政府背后的基本契约，假定公职人员会听取选民的意见，并为他们的关切采取行动。"

But the ruling reinforces the need for citizens and their elected representatives, not the courts, to ensure equality of access to government. Officials must not be allowed to play favorites in providing information or in arranging meetings simply because an individual or group provides a campaign donation or a personal gift. This type of integrity requires well-enforced laws in government transparency, such as records of official meetings, rules on lobbying, and information about each elected leader's source of wealth.

但该裁决强化了公民和他们选出的代表——而不是法院——来确保平等接触政府的必要性。不得允许官员仅仅因为个人或团体提供了竞选捐款或个人礼物，就在提供信息或安排会议时厚此薄彼。这种诚信需要执行良好的政府透明度法律，如公务会议记录、游说规则，以及每位民选领导人财富来源的信息。

Favoritism in official access can fan public perceptions of corruption. But it is not always corruption. Rather officials must avoid double standards, or different types of access for average people and the wealthy. If connections can be bought, a basic premise of democratic society—that all are equal in treatment by government—is undermined. Good governance rests on an understanding of the inherent worth of each individual.

在官方接触上的偏袒会煽动公众对腐败的感知。但它并不总是腐败。相反，官员必须避免双重标准，或为普通人和富人提供不同类型的接触。如果关系可以买卖，那么民主社会的一个基本前提——人人在政府面前平等——就被破坏了。良好的治理建立在对每个人内在价值的理解之上。

The court's ruling is a step forward in the struggle against both corruption and official favoritism.

最高法院的裁决是在打击腐败和官方偏袒斗争中迈出的一步。

36
句意题
答案 C
The underlined sentence (Para. 1) most probably shows that the court ___.划线句子（第 1 段）最有可能表明法院___。
[A] made no compromise in convicting McDonnell.在给麦克唐纳定罪时毫不妥协。
[B] avoided defining the extent of McDonnell's duties.避免界定麦克唐纳职责的范围。
[C] was contemptuous of McDonnell's conduct.
[D] refused to comment on McDonnell's ethics.拒绝对麦克唐纳的伦理问题置评。
💡 考场思路holding its nose = 嗤之以鼻。法院虽然推翻了定罪，但对其行为的伦理表示鄙视。
逐项分析 [A] 在定罪上不妥协 → 相反，推翻了定罪；
[B] 避免界定职责范围 → 无中生有；
[C] 对麦克唐纳行为表示鄙视 → 正确；
[D] 拒绝评论伦理 → 相反，明确评论了。
核心词汇
unanimous adj. 一致的
overturn v. 推翻
contemptuous adj. 鄙视的
bribery n. 贿赂
favoritism n. 偏袒
transparency n. 透明度
37
细节题
答案 A
According to Paragraph 4, an official act is deemed corruptive only if it involves ___.根据第4款，只有涉及___的官方行为才被视为腐败行为。
[A] concrete returns for gift-givers.
[B] sizable gains in the form of gifts.以礼物形式获得的可观收益。
[C] leaking secrets intentionally.故意泄露机密。
[D] breaking contracts officially.正式违约。
💡 考场思路第四段：proof must be made of concrete benefits——必须有具体利益证明。
38
细节题
答案 C
The court's ruling is based on the assumption that public officials are ___.法院的裁决基于公职人员是___的假设。
[A] allowed to focus on the concerns of their supporters.得以专注于其支持者的关切。
[B] qualified to deal independently with bureaucratic issues.有资格独立处理官僚事务。
[C] justified in addressing the needs of their constituents.
[D] exempt from conviction on the charge of favoritism.免于因偏袒指控而被定罪。
💡 考场思路第五段：public officials will hear from their constituents and act on their concerns——官员应听取选民意见并行动，即有理由处理选民需求。
39
细节题
答案 C
Well-enforced laws in government transparency are needed to ___.要___ ，需要执行良好的政府透明度法律。
[A] awaken the conscience of officials.唤醒官员的良知。
[B] allow for certain kinds of lobbying.允许某些形式的游说。
[C] guarantee fair play in official access.
[D] inspire hopes in average people.激发普通人的希望。
💡 考场思路第六段：ensure equality of access to government——确保平等接触政府，即公平对待。
40
态度题
答案 D
The author's attitude toward the court's ruling is ___.作者对法院裁决的态度是___。
[A] sarcastic.讽刺的。
[B] tolerant.宽容的。
[C] skeptical.怀疑的。
[D] supportive.
💡 考场思路末段：The court's ruling is a step forward——作者认为这是进步，即支持。
核心词汇
perception n. 感知
undermine v. 破坏
governance n. 治理
inherent adj. 内在的
Part B · 新题型排序题（41–45）

【题目】关于狄更斯生平的文章。D段已放在开头，B段已放在中间位置。要求把A、C、E、F、G填入41-45。

已知：D（总起：狄更斯是19世纪最伟大的英国小说家）→ 41 → 42 → 43 → 44 → B（《匹克威克外传》的成功确立了狄更斯的名声）→ 45。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
The first published sketch, "A Dinner at Poplar Walk" brought tears to Dickens's eyes when he discovered it in the pages of The Monthly Magazine. From then on his sketches, which appeared under the pen name "Boz" in The Evening Chronicle, earned him a modest reputation.
第一篇发表的速写《波普拉散步道之宴》，当狄更斯在《月刊》上发现它时，曾令他热泪盈眶。此后，他以"博兹"为笔名在《晚宪报》上发表的速写，为他赢得了一份不大却实在的声名。
B
The runaway success of The Pickwick Papers, as it is generally known today, secured Dickens's fame. There were Pickwick coats and Pickwick cigars, and the plump, spectacled hero, Samuel Pickwick, became a national figure.
正如今天人们所熟知的那样，《匹克威克外传》的一炮而红奠定了狄更斯的名声。市面上出现了匹克威克外套和匹克威克雪茄，而那位肥胖戴镜的主人公塞缪尔·匹克威克成了全国知名人物。
C
Soon after Sketches by Boz appeared, a publishing firm approached Dickens to write a story in monthly installments, as a backdrop for a series of woodcuts by the then-famous artist Robert Seymour, who had originated the idea for the story. With characteristic confidence, Dickens successfully insisted that Seymour's pictures illustrate his own story instead. After the first installment, Dickens wrote to the artist and asked him to correct a drawing Dickens felt was not faithful enough to his prose. Seymour made the change, went into his backyard, and expressed his displeasure by committing suicide. Dickens and his publishers simply pressed on with a new artist. The comic novel, The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club, appeared serially in 1836 and 1837, and was first published in book form in 1837.
《博兹速写集》问世后不久，一家出版公司找上狄更斯，请他按月连载一篇故事，作为当时著名画家罗伯特·西摩所创想的一系列木刻的陪衬。狄更斯以一贯的自信，成功坚持要西摩的画来图解他自己的故事。第一期的插图登出后，狄更斯写信给画家，请他修改一幅他觉得不够忠实于自己散文的画。西摩改了画，走进后院，以自杀表达了他的不快。狄更斯和出版商则换了个新画家继续干。这部喜剧小说《匹克威克俱乐部遗稿》于1836和1837年连载，并于1837年首次以书籍形式出版。
D
Charles Dickens is probably the best-known and, to many people, the greatest English novelist of the 19th century. A moralist, satirist, and social reformer. Dickens crafted complex plots and striking characters that capture the panorama of English society.
查尔斯·狄更斯很可能是19世纪最知名、对许多人而言也是最伟大的英国小说家。作为道德家、讽刺家和社会改革者，狄更斯构筑了复杂的情节与鲜明的人物，捕捉了英国社会的全景。
E
Soon after his father's release from prison, Dickens got a better job as errand boy in law offices. He taught himself shorthand to get an even better job later as a court stenographer and as a reporter in Parliament. At the same time, Dickens, who had a reporter's eye for transcribing the life around him especially anything comic or odd, submitted short sketches to obscure magazines.
父亲出狱后不久，狄更斯谋得一份更好的差事——在律师事务所当跑腿小弟。他自学速记，以便日后谋得更好的工作：法庭书记员和议会记者。与此同时，狄更斯有着记者般善于记录周遭生活（尤其是任何滑稽或古怪之事）的眼光，向一些无名杂志投寄短篇速写。
F
Dickens was born in Portsmouth, on England's southern coast. His father was a clerk in the British navy pay office—a respectable position, but with little social status. His paternal grandparents, a steward and a housekeeper possessed even less status, having been servants, and Dickens later concealed their background. Dickens's mother supposedly came from a more respectable family. Yet two years before Dickens's birth, his mother's father was caught stealing and fled to Europe, never to return. The family's increasing poverty forced Dickens out of school at age 12 to work in Warren's Blacking Warehouse, a shoe-polish factory, where the other working boys mocked him as "the young gentleman." His father was then imprisoned for debt. The humiliations of his father's imprisonment and his labor in the blacking factory formed Dickens's greatest wound and became his deepest secret. He could not confide them even to his wife, although they provide the unacknowledged foundation of his fiction.
狄更斯出生于英格兰南部海岸的朴茨茅斯。其父是英国海军薪金处的办事员——地位体面，却少有社会声望。他的祖父母，一位管家与一位女管家，因曾为仆人而身份更低，狄更斯后来隐瞒了他们的背景。狄更斯的母亲据称出自一个更体面的家庭。然而在狄更斯出生前两年，他的外祖父因盗窃被捕并逃往欧洲，再未归来。家境日窘，迫使12岁的狄更斯辍学，到沃伦鞋油厂——一家鞋油工厂——做工，其他童工嘲弄他为"小绅士"。其父随后因债务入狱。父亲入狱的屈辱与在鞋油厂的劳作，构成了狄更斯最大的伤口，也成为他最深的秘密。即便对妻子他也无法吐露，尽管这一切正是其小说不宣的底色。
G
After Pickwick, Dickens plunged into a bleaker world. In Oliver Twist, he traces an orphan's progress from the workhouse to the criminal slums of London. Nicholas Nickleby, his next novel, combines the darkness of Oliver Twist with the sunlight of Pickwick. The popularity of these novels consolidated Dickens as a nationally and internationally celebrated man of letters.
继《匹克威克》之后，狄更斯一头扎进了一个更为黯淡的世界。在《雾都孤儿》中，他追述了一个孤儿从济贫院走向伦敦犯罪贫民窟的历程。他的下一部小说《尼古拉斯·尼克尔贝》将《雾都孤儿》的黑暗与《匹克威克》的明快融为一体。这些小说的走红，巩固了狄更斯作为全国乃至国际知名文坛巨匠的地位。
41
排序题
答案 F
匹配依据D段总起介绍狄更斯是伟大小说家，接下来应讲他的出身。F段：狄更斯出生于朴茨茅斯，父亲是海军出纳员职员，家庭贫困，12岁进厂，父亲因债务入狱——这是生平的开头。
42
排序题
答案 E
匹配依据F段末：父亲入狱、在鞋油厂做工是狄更斯最大伤痛。E段：Soon after his father's release from prison（父亲出狱后不久）——时间顺序承接F段的父亲入狱。
43
排序题
答案 A
匹配依据E段末：狄更斯向杂志投稿短篇素描。A段：The first published sketch...brought tears to Dickens's eyes（第一篇发表的素描）——承接E段的submitted short sketches。
44
排序题
答案 C
匹配依据A段末：以"Boz"为笔名的素描为他赢得 modest reputation。C段：Soon after Sketches by Boz appeared（《Boz素描集》出版后不久）——出版商找他写连载故事，即《匹克威克外传》，直接引出B段。
45
排序题
答案 G
匹配依据B段讲《匹克威克外传》的成功。G段：After Pickwick, Dickens plunged into a bleaker world（《匹克威克》之后，狄更斯进入更黑暗的世界）——列举《雾都孤儿》《尼古拉斯·尼克尔贝》，时间顺序承接B段。
干扰项本题B和D已给出，5个空全部用A、C、E、F、G，无干扰。
Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）
46
翻译
But even as the number of English speakers expands further there are signs that the global predominance of the language may fade within the foreseeable future.
尽管讲英语的人数在进一步增加，但有迹象显示这一语言的全球统治地位在可预见的未来可能会衰落。
采分点① even as 尽管；② predominance 统治地位；③ fade 衰落；④ foreseeable future 可预见的未来。
47
翻译
His analysis should therefore end any self-contentedness among those who may believe that the global position of English is so stable that the young generations of the United Kingdom do not need additional language capabilities.
因此，他的分析会让一些人再也无法自满，这些人或许认为英语的全球地位十分稳固，从而英国的年轻人无需额外的语言能力。
采分点① self-contentedness 自满；② so...that... 如此……以至于……；③ additional language capabilities 额外的语言能力。
48
翻译
many countries are introducing English into the primary-school curriculum but British schoolchildren and students do not appear to be gaining greater encouragement to achieve fluency in other languages.
许多国家都在把英语纳入小学课程，但英国的大、中、小学生却似乎没有得到更多的鼓励去熟练掌握其他语言。
采分点① introduce...into 引入；② curriculum 课程；③ fluency 流利。
49
翻译
The changes identified by David Graddol all present clear and major challenges to the UK's providers of English language teaching to people of other countries and to broader education business sectors.
大卫·格拉多尔所指出的这些变化都对向其他国家的人提供英语教学的英国个人和组织机构，乃至更广泛的教育产业领域，构成了明确的、重大的挑战。
采分点① identified by 所指出的；② present challenges to 对……构成挑战；③ broader sectors 更广泛的领域。
50
翻译
It gives a basis for all organisations which seek to promote the learning and use of English, a basis for planning to meet the possibilities of what could be a very different operating environment.
它为旨在促进英语学习和使用的所有组织机构提供了一个基础，该基础用于规划应对由一种或许会很不一样的运作环境所带来的各种可能。
采分点① a basis for 为……提供基础；② seek to 试图；③ operating environment 运作环境。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 推荐邮件

原题指令 Directions

Write an email to Professor James Cook, a newly arrived Australian professor, to recommend some tourist attractions in your city and explain why they are worth visiting. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the email. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】给新到任的澳大利亚教授詹姆斯·库克写一封电子邮件，推荐你所在城市的一些旅游景点，并说明值得一游的理由。字数约100词。邮件末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

给新来的澳大利亚教授James Cook写一封邮件，推荐你所在城市的一些旅游景点，并说明推荐理由。落款 Li Ming。

审题

① 格式：邮件；② 语气：热情友好；③ 内容：景点名称+特色+推荐理由。

参考范文

Dear Professor Cook,

Welcome to our city! I am writing to recommend a few must-see attractions to help you settle in and enjoy your stay here.

First, I highly recommend the ancient walled district in the city center. Dating back to the Ming Dynasty, it boasts well-preserved traditional architecture, local snacks and a lively night market—ideal for experiencing authentic Chinese culture. Second, the nearby city park is worth a visit; famous for its lake and bamboo groves, it offers a peaceful escape from the busy campus. Finally, the city museum is a fine choice, where you can admire ancient ceramics and learn about local history.

I hope you find these recommendations helpful. Wish you a wonderful time here!

Yours sincerely, Li Ming

【译文】

尊敬的库克教授：

欢迎来到我们的城市！我写信是想推荐几处必游景点，帮助您安顿下来、享受在此的时光。

首先，我强烈推荐市中心的古城街区。它可追溯至明代，拥有保存完好的传统建筑、地方小吃和热闹的夜市——是体验纯正中国文化的绝佳去处。其次，附近的城市公园值得一游；它以湖泊和竹林闻名，是从繁忙校园中抽身静享的好地方。最后，市博物馆也是不错之选，您可欣赏古代陶瓷、了解本地历史。

希望这些推荐对您有用。祝您在此度过美好时光！

谨上，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文《"有书"与"读书"》

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The left picture shows a man lying in a chair before a wall of books, saying proudly, "I have so many books!" The right picture shows the same man sitting at a desk with only one book open, determined to "finish 20 books this year". The title is "Owning books vs. reading books".

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 左图：一个人躺在椅子上，面对满墙书架，得意地说“我有这么多书！”。右图：同一个人坐在书桌前，桌上只摊开一本书，决心满满地说“我争取今年读完20本书”。图题：“有书”与“读书”。

图画描述

左图：一个人躺在椅子上，面对满墙书架，得意地说"我有这么多书！"。右图：同一个人坐在书桌前，桌上只摊开一本书，决心满满地说"我争取今年读完20本书"。图题："有书"与"读书"。

审题框架

三段式：①简要描述图画（有书≠读书）；②阐释含义（拥有资源不等于付诸行动，行动的重要性）；③给出评论。160-200词。

参考范文

The cartoon presents a thought-provoking contrast. In the left picture, a man reclines before a huge bookshelf, proudly boasting, "I have so many books!"; in the right picture, the same man sits at a desk with one open book, determined to "finish twenty books this year." The caption reads: "Having books" versus "Reading books."

The drawing conveys a clear message: merely possessing resources is not the same as putting them to use. Many people accumulate books, degrees or opportunities as a source of pride, yet never apply them in any meaningful way. A library on the shelf earns no respect; only the act of reading, reflecting and applying what one learns brings real growth. This principle holds true not only for reading but for every sphere of life—from physical exercise to professional skills.

From my perspective, we should resist the vanity of "having" and embrace the discipline of "doing." A single book read thoroughly is far more valuable than a thousand volumes left untouched. Let us set concrete goals, follow them through, and turn what we have into what we actually do.

【译文】

漫画呈现了一组发人深省的对比。左图中，一人斜倚在巨大的书架前，得意地说"我有这么多书！"；右图中，同一个人坐在书桌前，摊开一本书，决心"今年读完20本"。图题为："有书"与"读书"。

这幅画传达了一个清晰的道理：仅仅拥有资源，并不等于加以运用。许多人把书、学位或机会当作骄傲的资本，却从不加以真正利用。书架上的藏书不会赢得尊重；唯有阅读、思考并践行所学，才能带来真正的成长。这一原则不仅适用于读书，也适用于生活的方方面面——从锻炼身体到职业技能。

在我看来，我们应抵制"拥有"的虚荣，拥抱"行动"的自律。一本读透的书，远胜千卷束之高阁的藏书。让我们设定具体目标、贯彻始终，把"所有"变为"所为"。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读（信任）

Trust is a tricky business. On the one hand, it's a necessary condition 1 many worthwhile things: child care, friendships, etc. On the other hand, putting your 2 in the wrong place often carries a high 3.

信任是件棘手的事。一方面，它是许多有价值之事（如育儿、友谊等）的必要条件；另一方面，把信任放错地方往往会带来高昂代价。

4, why do we trust at all? Well, because it feels good. 5 people place their trust in an individual or an institution, their brains release oxytocin, a hormone that 6 pleasurable feelings and triggers the herding instinct that prompts humans to 7 with one another. Scientists have found that exposure 8 this hormone puts us in a trusting 9: In a Swiss study, researchers sprayed oxytocin into the noses of half the subjects; those subjects were ready to lend significantly higher amounts of money to strangers than were their 10 who inhaled something else.

那么，我们究竟为什么要信任他人呢？因为信任感觉良好。当人们把信任寄托于某个人或某个机构时，大脑会释放催产素——这种激素能产生愉悦感，并触发群居本能，促使人们彼此建立联系。科学家发现，接触这种激素会让我们处于一种易信任他人的心境：在瑞士的一项研究中，研究人员把催产素喷进一半受试者的鼻子；这些受试者愿意借给陌生人的钱，明显高于吸入其他东西的对照组。

11 for us, we also have a sixth sense for dishonesty that may 12 us. A Canadian study found that children as young as 14 months can differentiate 13 a credible person and a dishonest one. Sixty toddlers were each 14 to an adult tester holding a plastic container. The tester would ask, "What's in here?" before looking into the container, smiling, and exclaiming, "Wow!" Each subject was then invited to look 15. Half of them found a toy; the other half 16 the container was empty—and realized the tester had 17 them.

对我们来说幸运的是，我们对不诚实也有一种第六感，它或许能保护我们。加拿大一项研究发现，仅14个月大的婴儿就能区分可信的人和不诚实的人。60名幼儿分别被引见给一位手持塑料容器的成年测试者。测试者会先问"里面是什么？"，然后看向容器内，微笑着惊呼"哇！"。接着邀请每个幼儿自己往里看。一半孩子发现了玩具；另一半则发现容器是空的——并意识到测试者欺骗了他们。

Among the children who had not been tricked, the majority were 18 to cooperate with the tester in learning a new skill, demonstrating that they trusted his leadership. 19, only five of the 30 children paired with the "20" tester participated in a follow-up activity.

在没有被欺骗的孩子中，大多数都愿意配合测试者学习一项新技能，表明他们信任他的带领。相比之下，在与"不可靠"测试者配对的30名孩子中，只有5人参加了后续活动。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读（自动化与中产阶级）

Among the annoying challenges facing the middle class is one that will probably go unmentioned in the next presidential campaign: What happens when the robots come for their jobs?

中产阶级面临的恼人挑战中有一项很可能在下届总统大选中被忽视：当机器人来抢他们的工作时，会发生什么？

Don't dismiss that possibility entirely. About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated, according to a University of Oxford study, with the middle class disproportionately squeezed. Lower-income jobs like gardening or day care don't appeal to robots. But many middle-class occupations—trucking, financial advice, software engineering—have aroused their interest, or soon will. The rich own the robots, so they will be fine.

别完全不理会这种可能。牛津大学一项研究显示，美国约一半工作面临被自动化的高风险，而中产阶级受到的挤压尤为严重。园艺、日托等低收入工作对机器人没有吸引力。但许多中产阶级职业——卡车运输、理财咨询、软件工程——已经引起了机器人的兴趣，或将很快被盯上。富人拥有机器人，所以他们不会有事。

This isn't to be alarmist. Optimists point out that technological upheaval has benefited workers in the past. The Industrial Revolution didn't go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually raised living standards and created more jobs than it destroyed. Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work. But in the medium term, middle-class workers may need a lot of help adjusting.

这并不是要杞人忧天。乐观者指出，技术剧变过去也曾让工人受益。工业革命对那些被机械化织布机抢了饭碗的卢德派来说并不愉快，但它最终提高了生活水平，创造的岗位多于摧毁的岗位。同样，自动化最终应能提高生产率、通过压低价格刺激需求，并把工人从枯燥繁重的工作中解放出来。但在中期，中产阶级劳动者可能需要大量帮助来适应。

The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training. Curriculums—from grammar school to college—should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication. Vocational schools should do a better job of fostering problem-solving skills and helping students work alongside robots. Online education can supplement the traditional kind. It could make extra training and instruction affordable. Professionals trying to acquire new skills will be able to do so without going into debt.

正如埃里克·布林约尔松和安德鲁·麦卡菲在《第二次机器时代》中所言，第一步应是重新思考教育与职业培训。从小学到大学的课程都应演进：少关注记忆事实，多关注创造力和复杂沟通。职业学校应更好地培养解决问题的能力，帮助学生与机器人协作。在线教育可作为传统教育的补充，让额外培训变得负担得起。想掌握新技能的专业人士也能不再举债学习。

The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier. In previous eras of drastic technological change, entrepreneurs smoothed the transition by dreaming up ways to combine labor and machines. The best uses of 3D printers and virtual reality haven't been invented yet. The U.S. needs the new companies that will invent them.

应对自动化的挑战凸显出美国亟需重振其日渐衰退的商业活力：必须让创办新公司变得更容易。在以往技术剧变的时代，企业家们通过想出把劳动与机器结合的办法来平稳过渡。3D打印和虚拟现实的最佳用途尚未被发明出来。美国需要那些将发明这些用途的新公司。

Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought. Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.

最后，由于自动化有可能拉大资本收入与劳动收入之间的差距，税收和社会保障体系将不得不重新考量。对低工资劳动的征税需要削减，劳动所得税抵免等工资补贴应扩大：这将提高收入、鼓励就业、奖励创造岗位的企业，并减少不平等。

Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation. Destroying the machines that are coming for our jobs would be nuts. But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.

未来几年，技术将以大大小小的方式改善社会，但对那些生活和职业被自动化颠覆的人来说，这算不上安慰。毁掉来抢饭碗的机器是疯了。但帮助劳动者适应的政策不可或缺。

21

Text 2   社交媒体与年轻人的新闻辨别力（26–30）

A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young Americans disapprove of President Trump's use of Twitter. The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president's social media platform.

哈佛大学一项新调查发现，逾三分之二的美国年轻人不认同特朗普总统使用推特。这意味着千禧一代更希望来自白宫的新闻经过其他渠道过滤，而非来自总统的社交媒体平台。

Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines. Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills. Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.

大多数美国人靠社交媒体浏览每日头条。然而，随着对所有媒体的不信任上升，人们或许正开始增强自己的媒体素养技能。这种趋势大有必要。据牛津大学统计，2016年总统大选期间，在政治上举足轻重的密歇根州，推特用户分享的网络内容中有近四分之一是假新闻。BuzzFeed News 的一项调查发现，44%的脸书用户很少或从不相信这家媒体巨头的新闻。

Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace. A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use "distributed trust" to verify stories. They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives—especially those that are open about any bias. "Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints," the survey concluded.

作为数字原住民的年轻人确实越来越擅长在网络空间辨别真伪。奈特基金会对14至24岁年轻人的焦点小组调查发现，他们使用"分布式信任"来核实报道。他们交叉核查来源，偏好来自不同视角的新闻——尤其是那些公开表明自身偏向的报道。调查总结道："许多年轻人承担起自我教育、主动寻找对立观点的重大个人责任。"

Such active research can have another effect. A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people's reliance on social media led to greater political engagement.

这种主动探究还有另一重效果。威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校2014年在澳、英、美开展的一项调查发现，年轻人对社交媒体的依赖带来了更高的政治参与度。

Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests. This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information. A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news lies in "misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news" via social media. In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be the heart of the issue. "This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem," says Roxane Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group.

社交媒体让用户更亲密、更即时地体验新闻事件，同时也允许他们转发新闻作为自身价值观和兴趣的投射。这迫使用户更清楚自己在传递信息中的角色。Barna研究集团的一项调查发现，美国人给出的假新闻现象的首要原因是"读者错误"，而非编造的报道或报道中的事实错误。约三分之一的人表示，假新闻问题在于通过社交媒体"误读或夸大真实新闻"。换言之，在社交媒体上分享新闻的选择或许是问题的核心。Barna集团主编罗克珊·斯通说："这表明在应对这一问题上存在真正的个人责任。"

So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills—and in their choices on when to share on social media.

因此，当年轻人批评一位过度发推特的总统时，他们展现出思维技能上的自律——以及在何时该在社交媒体上分享内容的选择上的自律。

26
细节题

Text 3   NHS与DeepMind的AI医疗协议（31–35）

Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy.

对英国国民医疗服务体系（NHS）与DeepMind之间协议的风险，任何公正的评估都必须首先承认双方本意都不坏。DeepMind是全球领先的人工智能公司之一。这项工作应用于医疗的潜力巨大，但也可能导致权力进一步集中在科技巨头手中。正是在这一背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对NHS旗下的皇家 free 医院信托开出了谴责性裁决：该信托于2015年依据一份含糊的协议将160万患者的记录交给了DeepMind，而该协议几乎没有顾及患者的权利和他们对隐私的期望。

DeepMind has almost apologised. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements—and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.

DeepMind几乎已经道歉。NHS信托也已改正做法。NHS与DeepMind之间进一步的安排（可能会有很多）将受到仔细审查，以确保已向患者征得一切必要许可、所有不必要的数据已被清除。在患者知情同意方面有教训可吸取。但隐私并非此案的唯一角度，甚至不是最重要的角度。德纳姆选择把责任集中在NHS信托身上，因为根据现行法律，是它"控制"数据，而DeepMind仅仅"处理"数据。但这一区分没有抓住要点：赋予数据价值的，正是处理和聚合，而非单纯地占有这些比特。

The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.

重大问题在于：我们如今生活产生的所有数据，其分析成果该由谁受益？隐私法建立在"可识别个人信息会对个人造成损害"这一概念之上。这忽视了监控经济的运作方式。在监控经济中，个人数据只有在与千百万其他人的数据相比较时才获得价值。

The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham's report is a welcome start.

在本案中用隐私法来约束科技巨头，显得有些错位。这种做法没有触及真正的担忧。仅仅说DeepMind开发的算法将造福患者、拯救生命是不够的。关键在于，这些算法将属于一家利用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。如果软件有望像如今的药物那样大规模拯救生命，那么大数据很可能会像大型制药公司那样行事。我们仍处在这场革命的开端，如今的微小选择日后可能产生巨大后果。要避免数字封建主义的未来，需要一场长期斗争。德纳姆女士的报告是一个可喜的开端。

Text 4   美国邮政USPS的财务困境（36–40）

The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue. Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs. There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself on the verge of bankruptcy. Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality.

美国邮政（USPS）持续亏损。它公布2016财年净亏损56亿美元，这是其开支连续第10年超过收入。与此同时，它还有超过1200亿美元无着落的负债，主要用于员工健康和退休成本。这个昔日稳定的联邦机构陷入破产边缘，原因有很多。从根本上说，USPS处在一场历史性挤压之中：一头是技术变革永久降低了对其核心产品——一类邮件——的需求；另一头是监管结构剥夺了管理层根据新现实调整运营的灵活性。

And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS's ultimate overseer—Congress—insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization.

而从邮政工会到贺卡制造商等各类利益集团，都向USPS的最终监管者——国会——施加自利性压力，坚持无论邮政局其他方面如何变化，他们所依赖的现状必须得到保护。这就是近年来改革立法一再失败的原因，结果是邮政局除了推迟至关重要的现代化之外，无力支付账单。

Now comes word that everyone involved—Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system's heaviest users—has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system. Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures. Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions.

现在有消息称，所有相关方——民主党、共和党、邮政局、工会以及该体系的重度用户——终于就一项修复方案达成一致。一项立法正在众议院推进，预计五年内可为USPS节省约286亿美元，可用于支付新车辆等生存措施。资金大部分来自每封信永久涨价1美分，以及将邮政退休人员转入联邦医保。后一项措施将在很大程度上抵消每年预付退休人员医疗保健的财政负担，从而解决USPS及其工会长期以来的抱怨。

If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate—where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform. There's no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency's costs. Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery. That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year. But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House. The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse at the USPS. It is not, however, a sign that they're getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21st century.

即便通过众议院，这项措施仍须过参议院——在那里必定有人会指出，它不过是维持邮政局运转的最最底线，远非全面改革。USPS的集体谈判没有任何改变，考虑到人员成本占该局开支的80%，这是重大疏漏。同样被忽略的还有取消周六信件投递的讨论。这一合乎常理的改动拥有广泛公众支持，每年可为USPS节省20亿美元。但邮政特殊利益集团似乎已将其扼杀，至少在众议院如此。围绕该法案达成的初步共识表明，议员们开始害怕USPS出现政治上难堪的短期崩溃。然而，这并不意味着他们正认真对待面向21世纪的邮政体系转型。
