Part B · 新题型排序题（41–45）— 艾森豪威尔行政办公楼

【题目】选项全文已打乱，C、F两段位置已给出，需将A–G填入41–45。已知顺序：41 → C → 42 → 43 → F → 44 → 45。

[C] State, War, and Navy Building（最初名称）容纳了与制定外交政策最密切相关的三个行政部门，是美国崛起为国际强权时期的建筑，住过许多重要外交官和政治家，发生过许多历史事件。

C为总起介绍段之后的展开：点明该楼的功能与历史地位。

[F] 建设历时17年，逐翼建起；落成时是华盛顿最大办公楼，近2英里黑白瓷砖走廊，内部多用熟铁/灰泥以防火，花岗石楼梯配4000多铸铁栏杆，顶部四个天窗穹顶和两个彩色玻璃圆厅。

F紧接"1871年开工"，讲建设过程与落成规模。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
In December of 1869, Congress appointed a commission to select a site and prepare plans and cost estimates for a new State Department Building. Later, the commission was also charged with finding a site and planning for a new War and Navy Department Building.
1869年12月，国会任命一个委员会，为新国务院大楼选址并拟定方案与费用估算。后来，该委员会还受命为新的陆军暨海军部大楼选址并作规划。
B
Completed in 1875, the State Department's south wing was the first to be occupied, with its elegant four-story library (completed in 1876), Cabinet Room, and Secretary's office.
国务院大楼南翼于1875年落成并率先启用，内有典雅的四层图书馆（1876年竣工）、内阁会议室和国务卿办公室。
C
The State, War, and Navy Building, as it was originally known, housed the three Executive Branch Departments most intimately connected with formulating foreign policy and the making of war and peace. It was where many of the most celebrated national figures of the nation's history made their mark.
这座建筑最初名为国务院、陆军部与海军部大楼，容纳了与制定外交政策和决定战争与和平关系最为密切的三个行政部门。国家历史上许多最负盛名的显要人物，都曾在此留下印记。
D
Many of the most celebrated national figures have participated in historical events that have taken place within the EEOB's granite walls. Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt, William Howard Taft, Dwight D. Eisenhower, and a host of other American presidents and foreign dignitaries have walked its corridors.
众多最负盛名的国家人物都曾参与发生在EEOB花岗岩墙壁之内的历史事件。西奥多·罗斯福、富兰克林·D·罗斯福、威廉·霍华德·塔夫脱、德怀特·D·艾森豪威尔，以及众多其他美国总统与外国政要，都曾走过它的走廊。
E
The Eisenhower Executive Office Building (EEOB) commands a unique position in both the national history and the architectural heritage of the United States. Built from 1871 to 1888, its colorful history and vast, gracefully ornate interior have inspired numerous books, films, and even a song.
艾森豪威尔行政办公楼（EEOB）在美国国家历史与建筑遗产中都占据着独特地位。它建于1871至1888年间，其多姿的历史与广阔而优雅华美的内饰，激发了无数书籍、电影甚至一首歌曲的灵感。
F
Construction took 17 years as the building slowly rose wing by wing. When the EEOB was finished, it was the largest office building in Washington, with nearly two miles of black and white tiled corridors. Its interior was designed with state-of-the-art technology of the day, including fireproofing, electric light, and its own telephone system.
建筑耗时17年，以一翼一翼缓慢拔地而起。EEOB落成时是华盛顿最大的办公建筑，拥有近两英里黑白瓷砖铺就的走廊。其内部采用了当时的尖端技术，包括防火、电灯以及独立的电话系统。
G
The history of the EEOB began long before its foundations were laid. The first executive offices were constructed between 1799 and 1820, and the State Department was located in them. The building's early history was marked by frequent relocation and expansion as the young republic grew.
EEOB的历史远在其奠基之前就已开始。最早的行政办公室建于1799至1820年间，国务院便设于此。随着年轻共和国的成长，这座建筑的早期历史以频繁迁址与扩张为标志。
41
排序题
答案 E
解题依据E段是全文总起："The Eisenhower Executive Office Building (EEOB) commands a unique position in both the national history and the architectural heritage…built from 1871 to 1888…" 先总体介绍该楼地位与建造年代，适合作为首段。
42
排序题
答案 G
解题依据C段后回溯历史：G段"The history of the EEOB began long before its foundations were laid…1799-1820…1866…demolition of the State Department building." 时间线从最早办公场所讲到1866年旧楼被拆，自然引出下文建楼。
43
排序题
答案 A
解题依据G段末"1866年拆除旧国务院大楼"，A段开头"In December of 1869, Congress appointed a commission to select a site…construction began in June of 1871." 时间、事件完美承接；A段末"1871年6月开工"又接F段"Construction took 17 years…"。
44
排序题
答案 B
解题依据F段讲"逐翼建起、落成时规模巨大"，B段"Completed in 1875, the State Department's south wing was the first to be occupied…Navy moved into the east wing in 1879" 具体讲各翼何时投入使用，承接"wing by wing"。
45
排序题
答案 D
解题依据B段讲建筑投入使用，D段"Many of the most celebrated national figures have participated in historical events within the EEOB's granite walls…Theodore and Franklin Roosevelt…Churchill…Pearl Harbor" 列举在此办公过的名人，作结收束全文。
解题铁律排序题抓时间线（1799→1866→1869→1871→1875→1879→1888）和代词/复现词（the building / its wings / historic events）。
Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）— 莎士比亚与戏剧
46
翻译
By the date of his birth Europe was witnessing the passing of the religious drama, and the creation of new forms under the incentive of classical tragedy and comedy.
到他出生时，欧洲正见证宗教戏剧的衰落，以及在古典悲剧和喜剧的激励之下新戏剧形式的诞生。
采分点① by the date of his birth 到他出生时；② witness 见证；③ the passing of ……的衰落/消逝；④ under the incentive of 在……激励下。
47
翻译
no boy who went to a grammar school could be ignorant that the drama was a form of literature which gave glory to Greece and Rome and might yet bring honor to England.
任何上过文法学校的男孩都不会不知道，戏剧是一种文学形式，它曾给希腊和罗马带来荣耀，或许也终将给英国带来荣光。
采分点① cannot be ignorant that 不会不知道（双重否定）；② give glory to 给……带来荣耀；③ might yet 或许终将。
48
翻译
But the professional companies prospered in their permanent theaters, and university men with literary ambitions were quick to turn to these theaters as offering a means of livelihood.
但是，职业剧团在固定剧院里蓬勃发展，那些有文学抱负的大学毕业生也很快转向这些剧院，将其作为一种谋生手段。
采分点① prosper 蓬勃发展；② permanent theaters 固定剧院；③ a means of livelihood 谋生手段。
49
翻译
A native literary drama had been created, its alliance with the public playhouses established, and at least some of its great traditions had been begun.
一种本土的文学戏剧已然形成，它与公共剧院的联盟也已确立，至少其某些伟大传统也已开始。
采分点① native 本土的；② its alliance…established 独立主格结构；③ 并列完成时的翻译要保持时态一致。
50
翻译
To realize how great was the dramatic activity, we must remember further that hosts of plays have been lost, and that probably there is no author of note whose entire work has survived.
要了解当时的戏剧活动是何等繁荣，我们还必须记住，大量剧作已经散佚，而且很可能没有一位知名作家的全部作品都流传了下来。
采分点① To realize 要认识到（不定式作目的）；② hosts of 大量；③ author of note 知名作家；④ survive 流传下来。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 邀请邮件

原题指令 Directions

Write an email to all the international experts on campus, inviting them to attend the graduation ceremony. The email should include the time and place of the ceremony as well as other relevant information. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the email. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】给校内所有国际专家写一封电子邮件，邀请他们参加毕业典礼。邮件应包含典礼的时间、地点及其他相关信息。字数约100词。邮件末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

给校内所有国际专家写一封邮件，邀请他们参加毕业典礼。邮件中应包含典礼的时间、地点及其他相关信息。约100词，落款用"Li Ming"，不要写自己真名。

审题

① 文体：正式邀请邮件；② 必含三要素：时间、地点、其他相关信息（着装/流程/回执）；③ 语气：尊敬、热情。

参考范文

Dear International Experts,

On behalf of the Students' Union, I am writing to cordially invite you to attend our university's graduation ceremony, which will be held in the Main Hall at 9:00 a.m. on Friday, June 21.

The ceremony will include the president's address, the conferring of degrees and a group photograph. As our distinguished guests, you are kindly requested to arrive 30 minutes early and be seated on the platform. Please confirm your attendance by June 14 via the link attached.

We would be deeply honored by your presence. Looking forward to your reply.

Yours sincerely, Li Ming

【译文】

尊敬的国际专家们：

我谨代表学生会，诚挚邀请各位出席我校毕业典礼。典礼将于6月21日（周五）上午9:00在主厅举行。

典礼包括校长致辞、学位授予与集体合影。作为贵宾，请您提前30分钟到场，并在主席台就座。请于6月14日前通过所附链接确认出席。

您的莅临将令我们深感荣幸。期待您的回复。

谨上，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文《选课进行时》

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The cartoon shows a student hesitating before the course-selection system. One speech bubble says the courses are "new in knowledge, innovation-oriented and challenging", while another says they are "high-scoring, easy to pass and with little homework".

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 漫画展示一名学生面对选课系统犹豫不决。一个气泡说课程“知识新、重创新、有难度”，另一个气泡说“给分高、易通过、作业少”。

图画解读

学生面对选课系统，一个气泡是"知识新、重创新、有难度"，另一个气泡是"给分高、易通过、作业少"。漫画揭示大学生选课的功利倾向：避难就易，还是追求真才实学？

审题框架

三段式：①简要描述图画；②点明寓意——选课观折射学习态度；③评论：大学生应重真学问而非分数捷径。160-200词。

参考范文

As is vividly shown in the cartoon, a student hesitates before the course-selection system, caught between two tempting options: courses that are new, innovation-oriented and challenging, and courses that promise high grades, easy credits and little homework.

The drawing conveys a thought-provoking message: course selection mirrors a student's underlying attitude toward learning. Driven by utilitarian concerns, some undergraduates shy away from demanding courses and chase easy credits. While such a strategy may inflate their GPA, it deprives them of the very knowledge and creativity that higher education is meant to cultivate. Real growth rarely comes from the path of least resistance.

From my perspective, university students should prioritize courses that stretch their abilities over those that merely pad their transcripts. After all, it is solid competence, not a glossy report card, that secures one's future in an increasingly competitive world.

【译文】

如漫画生动所示，一名学生在选课系统前犹豫不决，徘徊于两种诱人的选项之间：一类课程新颖、重创新、有难度；另一类则承诺高分、易通过、作业少。

这幅画传达了发人深省的道理：选课折射出学生对学习的根本态度。受功利心驱使，一些大学生回避有挑战的课程、追逐容易拿到的学分。这种策略虽能抬高绩点，却使他们错失了高等教育本应培养的知识与创造力。真正的成长很少来自最省力的那条路。

在我看来，大学生应优先选择能拓展能力的课程，而非仅为装点成绩单的课程。毕竟，在这个日益竞争的世界里，真正保障未来的，是扎实的能力，而非光鲜的成绩单。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读（野外迷路如何找路）

Today, we live in a world where GPS systems, digital maps, and other navigation apps are all available on our smartphones. 1 of us just walk straight into the woods without a phone. But phones 2 on batteries, and batteries can die faster than we realize. 3 you get lost without a phone or a compass, and you 4 can't find north, a few tricks may help you navigate 5 to civilization, one of which is to follow the land.

如今，我们生活在一个GPS、数字地图和其他导航应用都能在智能手机上使用的世界。我们中很少有人会不带手机就径直走进森林。但手机靠电池运行，而电池耗尽的速度比我们意识到的更快。如果你在没有手机或指南针的情况下迷了路，而且实在找不到北，有几个诀窍或许能帮你重新找到回到人类文明的路，其中之一就是顺着地形走。

When you find yourself 6 a trail, but not in a completely 7 area of land, you have to answer two questions: Which 8 is downhill, in this particular area? And where is the nearest water source? Humans overwhelmingly live in valleys, and on supplies of fresh water. 9, if you head downhill, and follow any H₂O you find, you should 10 see signs of people.

当你发现自己偏离了小路，但又并非身处一个完全陌生的地带时，你得回答两个问题：在这一带，哪个方向是下坡？最近的水源在哪里？人类绝大多数聚居在山谷里，靠淡水供给为生。因此，如果你朝下坡走，并循着发现的任何水源，最终应该能看到人的踪迹。

If you've explored the area before, keep an eye out for familiar sights—you may be 11 how quickly identifying a distinctive rock or tree can restore your bearings.

如果你以前探查过这一地区，要留心熟悉的景物——你或许会惊讶地发现，认出一块独特的岩石或一棵树，能多快就让你重新辨明方向。

Another 12: Climb high and look for signs of human habitation. 13, even in dense forest, you should be able to 14 gaps in the tree line due to roads, train tracks, and other paths people carve 15 the woods. Head toward these 16 to find a way out. At night, scan the horizon for 17 light sources, such as fires and streetlights, then walk toward the glow of light pollution.

另一个办法：爬到高处，寻找人类居住的迹象。例如，即便在茂密的森林里，你也应该能发现林线中的缺口——那是人们在林中开辟出的道路、铁轨和其他小径造成的。朝这些缺口走去，就能找到出路。到了夜晚，扫视地平线，寻找人工光源，比如火光和路灯，然后朝光污染的微光走去。

18, assuming you're lost in an area humans tend to frequent, look for the 19 we leave on the landscape. Trail blazes, tire tracks, and other features can 20 you to civilization.

最后，假设你迷失在人类常去的区域，就寻找我们留在大地上的记号。路标刻痕、轮胎印和其他特征，都能把你引向人类文明。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读（银行家奖金与短期主义）

Financial regulators in Britain have imposed a rather unusual rule on the bosses of big banks. Starting next year, any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing. The main purpose of this "clawback" rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions. Yet officials also hope for a much larger benefit: more long-term decision-making, not only by banks but by all corporations, to build a stronger economy for future generations.

英国金融监管机构对大银行的高管们强加了一条相当不寻常的规定。从明年起，如果银行因不当行为接受调查，高管任何固定奖金都可能被推迟10年发放。这条"追回"规定的主要目的，是让银行家对有害的冒险行为负责，并恢复公众对金融机构的信任。但官员们还期望获得一个更大的益处：不仅银行、而是所有公司都做出更多长期决策，为子孙后代建设更强劲的经济。

"Short-termism," or the desire for quick profits, has worsened in publicly traded companies, says the Bank of England's top economist, Andrew Haldane. He quotes a giant of classical economics, Alfred Marshall, in describing this financial impatience as acting like "children who pick the plums out of their pudding to eat them at once" rather than putting them aside to be eaten last.

英国央行首席经济学家安德鲁·霍尔丹表示，"短期主义"——即对快速利润的渴望——在上市公司中愈演愈烈。他引用古典经济学巨匠阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔的话，把这种金融上的急躁比作"孩子把李子从布丁里挑出来马上吃掉"，而不是留到最后再吃。

The average time for holding a stock in both the United States and Britain, he notes, has dropped from seven years to seven months in recent decades. Transient investors, who demand high quarterly profits from companies, can hinder a firm's efforts to invest in long-term research or to build up customer loyalty. This has been dubbed "quarterly capitalism."

他指出，近几十年来，英美两国股票的平均持有时间已从七年降至七个月。短期投资者要求公司季度利润高企，可能妨碍公司投资长期研发或建立客户忠诚度的努力。这被称为"季度资本主义"。

In addition, new digital technologies have allowed more rapid trading of equities, quicker use of information, and thus shorter attention spans in financial markets. "There seems to be a predominance of short-term thinking at the expense of long-term investing," said Commissioner Daniel Gallagher of the US Securities and Exchange Commission in a speech this week.

此外，新数字技术使股票交易更迅速、信息利用更快捷，从而缩短了金融市场的关注时长。美国证券交易委员会委员丹尼尔·加拉格尔本周在一次演讲中说："短期思维似乎正以牺牲长期投资为代价而占据主导。"

In the US, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 has pushed most public companies to defer performance bonuses for senior executives by about a year, slightly helping reduce "short-termism." In its latest survey of CEO pay, The Wall Street Journal finds that "a substantial part" of executive pay is now tied to performance.

在美国，2002年《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》已迫使大多数上市公司将高管绩效奖金推迟约一年发放，略微有助于减少"短期主义"。《华尔街日报》在最新CEO薪酬调查中发现，如今高管薪酬的"相当大一部分"已与业绩挂钩。

Much more could be done to encourage "long-termism," such as changes in the tax code and quicker disclosure of stock acquisitions. In France, shareholders who hold onto a company investment for at least two years can sometimes earn more voting rights in a company.

在鼓励"长期主义"方面，还可以做得更多，比如修改税法、加快股票收购信息披露。在法国，持有一家公司投资至少两年的股东，有时能在公司获得更多投票权。

Within companies, the right compensation design can provide incentives to executives to think beyond their own time at the company and on behalf of all stakeholders. Britain's new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance, not just for the short term but for the long term.

在公司内部，合理的薪酬设计可以激励高管超越自己在公司的任职期限、代表所有利益相关者去思考。英国的新规定提醒银行家：社会关注他们的表现，不仅在短期，更在长期。

21

[B] enhance bankers' sense of responsibility.

Text 2   成绩宽容政策grade forgiveness（26–30）

Grade inflation—the gradual increase in average GPAs (grade-point averages) over the past few decades—is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education, in which students are treated like customers to be pleased. But another, related force — a policy often buried deep in course catalogs called "grade forgiveness" — is helping raise GPAs.

成绩膨胀——即过去几十年平均绩点（GPA）的逐渐上升——常被视为高等教育消费时代的产物，在这个时代学生被当作需要取悦的顾客。但另一个相关因素——一项常被深埋在课程目录中、名为"成绩宽容"的政策——也在推高GPA。

Grade forgiveness allows students to retake a course in which they received a low grade, and the most recent grade or the highest grade is the only one that counts in calculating a student's overall GPA.

成绩宽容允许学生重修一门曾拿过低分的课程，而在计算总GPA时，只取最近一次或最高的那次成绩。

The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years, as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates. When this practice first started decades ago, it was usually limited to freshmen, to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses. But now most colleges, save for many selective campuses, allow all undergraduates, and even graduate students, to get their low grades forgiven.

近年来，随着大学继续竭尽全力留住学生（并收取学费）、提高毕业率，这一鲜为人知做法的使用加速了。几十年前它刚出现时，通常只限于大一新生，让他们在向大学课程过渡困难时，第一学年能有第二次修课机会。但如今，除了许多择优录取的院校外，大多数大学都允许所有本科生、甚至研究生申请成绩宽容。

College officials tend to emphasize that the goal of grade forgiveness is less about the grade itself and more about encouraging students to retake courses critical to their degree program and graduation without incurring a big penalty. "Ultimately," said Jack Miner, Ohio State University's registrar, "we see students achieve more success because they retake a course and do better in subsequent courses or master the content that allows them to graduate on time."

大学官员倾向于强调，成绩宽容的目的与其说在于成绩本身，不如说是鼓励学生重修对其学位项目和毕业至关重要的课程，而不必承受过重惩罚。俄亥俄州立大学教务主任杰克·迈纳说："归根结底，我们看到学生获得了更大成功，因为他们重修一门课后，在后续课程中表现更好，或掌握了让他们能按时毕业的内容。"

That said, there is a way in which grade forgiveness satisfies colleges' own needs as well. For public institutions, state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on metrics such as graduation rates and student retention—so better grades can, by boosting figures like those, mean more money. And anything that raises GPAs will likely make students—who, at the end of the day, are paying the bill—feel they've gotten a better value for their tuition dollars, which is another big concern for colleges.

话虽如此，成绩宽容在某种程度上也满足了大学自身的需要。对公立院校而言，州政府拨款有时部分与毕业率、留校率等指标挂钩——因此更好的成绩能通过抬高这些数字，意味着更多钱。而任何抬高GPA的做法，都 likely 让最终掏钱的学生觉得自己的学费花得更值，这是大学关心的另一大问题。

Indeed, grade forgiveness is just another way that universities are responding to consumers' expectations for higher education. Since students and parents expect a college degree to lead to a job, it is in the best interest of a school to turn out graduates who are as qualified as possible—or at least to appear to be. On this, students' and colleges' incentives seem to be aligned.

的确，成绩宽容不过是大学回应消费者对高等教育期望的又一种方式。既然学生和家长期望大学文凭能带来工作，那么培养出尽可能合格——或至少看起来合格——的毕业生，才符合学校的最大利益。在这一点上，学生和大学的动机似乎是一致的。

26

[A] Colleges' neglect of GPAs.大学对平均绩点（GPA）的忽视。
[B] The influence of consumer culture.
[C] Students' indifference to GPAs.学生对GPA的漠不关心。
[D] The change of course catalogs.课程目录的变化。

Text 3   人工智能伦理与《弗兰肯斯坦》（31–35）

This year marks exactly two centuries since the publication of Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, by Mary Shelley. Even before the invention of the electric light bulb, the author produced a remarkable work of speculative fiction that would foreshadow many ethical questions to be raised by technologies yet to come.

今年恰逢玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦（又名现代普罗米修斯）》出版两百周年。甚至在电灯泡发明之前，这位作者就写出了一部非凡的科幻作品，它预示了未来技术将引发的诸多伦理问题。

Today the rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) raises fundamental questions: "What is intelligence, identify, or consciousness? What makes humans humans?"

如今，人工智能（AI）的迅猛发展提出了根本性问题："什么是智能、身份或意识？是什么使人类成其为人类？"

What is being called artificial general intelligence, machines that would imitate the way humans think, continues to evade scientists. Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look, move, and respond like humans, similar to those recently depicted on popular sci-fi TV series such as "Westworld" and "Humans."

所谓通用人工智能——即能模仿人类思维方式的机器——仍然让科学家捉摸不透。然而，人类依然着迷于那种外观、动作、反应都像人的机器人，就像最近热门科幻剧《西部世界》和《真实的人类》中描绘的那样。

Just how people think is still far too complex to be understood, let alone reproduced, says David Eagleman, a Stanford University neuroscientist. "We are just in a situation where there are no good theories explaining what consciousness actually is and how you could ever build a machine to get there."

斯坦福大学神经科学家大卫·伊格曼说，人类究竟如何思考，仍然太过复杂，难以理解，更别说复制了。"我们目前的处境是：还没有好的理论来解释意识究竟是什么，又该如何造出一台能拥有意识的机器。"

But that doesn't mean crucial ethical issues involving AI aren't at hand. The coming use of autonomous vehicles, for example, poses thorny ethical questions. Human drivers sometimes must make split-second decisions. Their reactions may be a complex combination of instant reflexes, input from past driving experiences, and what their eyes and ears tell them in that moment. AI "vision" today is not nearly as sophisticated as that of humans. And to anticipate every imaginable driving situation is a difficult programming problem.

但这并不意味着涉及AI的关键伦理问题还遥不可及。例如，即将到来的自动驾驶汽车就提出了棘手的伦理问题。人类司机有时必须在瞬间做出决定。他们的反应可能是即时反射、过去驾驶经验的输入，以及那一刻眼睛耳朵所感的复杂结合。如今AI的"视觉"远不如人类精密。而要预见每一种可想象的驾驶情形，是个艰难的编程难题。

Whenever decisions are based on masses of data, "you quickly get into a lot of ethical questions," notes Tan Kiat How, chief executive of a Singapore-based agency that is helping the government develop a voluntary code for the ethical use of AI. Along with Singapore, other governments and mega-corporations are beginning to establish their own guidelines. Britain is setting up a data ethics center. India released its AI ethics strategy this spring.

一家总部位于新加坡、正协助政府制定AI伦理使用自愿准则的机构的首席执行官陈杰豪指出，只要决策基于海量数据，"你很快就会碰到一大堆伦理问题"。与新加坡一道，其他国家政府和大型企业也开始制定各自的指导方针。英国正在设立数据伦理中心。印度今年春天发布了AI伦理战略。

On June 7 Google pledged not to "design or deploy AI" that would cause "overall harm," or to develop AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms. It also pledged not to deploy AI whose use would violate international laws or human rights.

6月7日，谷歌承诺不会"设计或部署"会造成"全面伤害"的AI，不会开发AI制导武器，也不会将AI用于违反国际准则的监控。它还承诺不会部署使用起来会违反国际法或人权的AI。

While the statement is vague, it represents one starting point. So does the idea that decisions made by AI systems should be explainable, transparent, and fair.

尽管这份声明含糊，但它代表了一个起点。AI系统做出的决策应当可解释、透明、公平，这一理念同样如此。

To put it another way: How can we make sure that the thinking of intelligent machines reflects humanity's highest values? Only then will they be useful servants and not Frankenstein's out-of-control monster.

换句话说：我们如何能确保智能机器的思考反映人类最高尚的价值观？唯有如此，它们才会是有用的仆人，而不是弗兰肯斯坦那个失控的怪物。

31

[B] has remained popular for as long as 200 years.已流行长达200年之久。
[C] fascinates AI scientists all over the world.令全球人工智能科学家着迷。
[D] has sparked serious ethical controversies.引发了严重的伦理争议。

Text 4   最高法院在线销售税裁决（36–40）

States will be able to force more people to pay sales tax when they make online purchases under a Supreme Court decision Thursday that will leave shoppers with lighter wallets but is a big financial win for states.

根据最高法院周四的一项裁决，各州将能强制更多人在网购时缴纳销售税——这项裁决会让购物者钱包更瘪，但对各州来说是一场财政上的大胜。

The Supreme Court's opinion Thursday overruled a pair of decades-old decisions that states said cost them billions of dollars in lost revenue annually. The decisions made it more difficult for states to collect sales tax on certain online purchases.

最高法院周四的意见书推翻了两项沿用数十年的旧裁决，各州称这些旧裁决每年让它们损失数十亿美元税收。这些旧裁决使各州更难对某些网购征收销售税。

The cases the court overturned said that if a business was shipping a customer's purchase to a state where the business didn't have a physical presence such as a warehouse or office, the business didn't have to collect sales tax for the state. Customers were generally responsible for paying the sales tax to the state themselves if they weren't charged it, but most didn't realize they owed it and few paid.

被推翻的案件规定：如果一家企业把顾客购买的商品寄到该企业没有实体存在（如仓库或办公室）的州，该企业就不必为该州代征销售税。如果没有被代收，顾客通常有责任自己向州政府缴纳销售税，但大多数人没意识到自己欠税，很少有人缴纳。

Justice Anthony Kennedy wrote that the previous decisions were flawed. "Each year the physical presence rule becomes further removed from economic reality and results in significant revenue losses to the States," he wrote in an opinion joined by four other justices. Kennedy wrote that the rule "limited States' ability to seek long-term prosperity and has prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field."

大法官安东尼·肯尼迪写道，先前的裁决有缺陷。他在一份由另外四名大法官加入的意见书中写道："实体存在规则每年都愈发脱离经济现实，给各州造成重大税收损失。"肯尼迪写道，该规则"限制了各州寻求长期繁荣的能力，并阻碍了市场参与者在公平环境中竞争。"

The ruling is a victory for big chains with a presence in many states, since they usually collect sales tax on online purchases already. Now, rivals will be charging sales tax where they hadn't before. Big chains have been collecting sales tax nationwide because they typically have physical stores in whatever state a purchase is being shipped to. Amazon.com, with its network of warehouses, also collects sales tax in every state that charges it, though third-party sellers who use the site don't have to.

这项裁决对在多州设有实体的大连锁是胜利，因为它们通常早已对网购代征销售税。现在，竞争对手将在以前不征税的地方开始征税。大连锁之所以在全国代征销售税，是因为无论商品寄往哪个州，它们通常都有实体店。亚马逊凭借其仓库网络，也在每个征收销售税的州代征，不过使用该平台的第三方卖家则不必。

Until now, many sellers that have a physical presence in only a single state or a few states have been able to avoid charging sales taxes when they ship to addresses outside those states. Sellers that use eBay and Etsy, which provide platforms for smaller sellers, also haven't been collecting sales tax nationwide. Under the ruling Thursday, states can pass laws requiring out-of-state sellers to collect the state's sales tax from customers and send it to the state.

此前，许多只在一两个州有实体的卖家，在把商品寄到这些州以外地址时，一直得以避开征收销售税。使用eBay和Etsy（为小卖家提供平台）的卖家也一直未在全国代征销售税。根据周四的裁决，各州可通过法律，要求州外卖家向顾客代收本州销售税并上缴州政府。

Retail trade groups praised the ruling, saying it levels the playing field for local and online businesses. The losers, said retail analyst Neil Saunders, are online-only retailers, especially smaller ones. Those retailers may face headaches complying with various state sales tax laws. The Small Business & Entrepreneurship Council advocacy group said in a statement, "Small businesses and internet entrepreneurs are not well served at all by this decision."

零售行业组织赞扬这项裁决，称它为本地企业和在线企业创造了公平竞争环境。零售分析师尼尔·桑德斯说，输家是纯在线零售商，尤其是小型卖家。这些零售商可能会在遵守各州不同销售税法时头疼不已。 advocacy组织"小企业与创业委员会"在一份声明中说："这项裁决对小企业和互联网创业者毫无益处。"

36
细节题
答案 C
The Supreme Court decision Thursday will ___.最高法院周四的决定将___。
[A] put most online business in a dilemma.使多数在线业务陷入两难。
[B] force some states to cut sales tax.迫使一些州削减销售税。
[C] make more online shoppers pay sales tax.
[D] better businesses' relations with states.改善企业与各州的关系。
💡 考场思路首段：force more people to pay sales tax when they make online purchases——让更多网购者缴税。
37
细节题
答案 D
It can be learned from Paragraphs 2 and 3 that the overruled decisions ___.从第2段和第3段中可以了解到，被推翻的决定___。
[A] were widely criticized by online purchases.受到网购的广泛批评（原文逻辑存疑）。
[B] have cost consumers a lot over the years.多年来让消费者付出了巨大代价。
[C] have led to the dominance of e-commerce.导致了电子商务的主导地位。
[D] were considered unfavorable by states.
💡 考场思路第二段：旧裁决让各州每年损失数十亿美元税收——对各州不利。
38
细节题
答案 B
According to Justice Anthony Kennedy, the physical presence rule has ___.根据安东尼·肯尼迪大法官的说法，实体存在规则有___。
[A] hindered economic development.阻碍了经济发展。
[B] harmed fair market competition.
[C] boosted growth in states' revenue.推动了各州财政收入的增长。
[D] brought prosperity to the country.为国家带来繁荣。
💡 考场思路第四段末：该规则"prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field"——破坏了公平竞争。
39
细节题
答案 A
Who are most likely to welcome the Supreme Court ruling?谁最有可能欢迎最高法院的裁决？
[A] Big-chain owners.
[B] Third-party sellers.第三方卖家。
[C] Internet entrepreneurs.互联网企业家。
[D] Small retailers.小型零售商。
💡 考场思路第五段首句：The ruling is a victory for big chains——大连锁是赢家。
40
篇章方法题
答案 B
In dealing with the Supreme Court decision Thursday, the author ___.在处理最高法院周四的裁决时，提交人___。
[A] presents its main points with conflicting views on them.呈现其主要观点并附上相互冲突的看法。
[B] gives a factual account of it and discusses its consequences.
[C] cites some cases related to it and analyzes their implications.引用了与之相关的若干案例并分析了其启示。
[D] describes the long and complicated process of its making.描述了其制作漫长而复杂的过程。
💡 考场思路作者客观陈述裁决内容，然后分析谁受益、谁受损（大连锁赢、小卖家输）——即事实陈述+后果讨论。
核心词汇
overrule v. 推翻
physical presence 实体存在
even playing field 公平竞争环境
revenue n. 税收/收入
level the playing field 公平竞争
comply with 遵守
Part B · 新题型排序题（41–45）— 如何赢得争论

【题目】段落已打乱，C、F两段位置已给出。已知顺序：41 → 42 → F → 43 → C → 44 → 45。

[F] These views of arguments also undermine reason. 若把对话看作斗争或竞赛，你可以靠作弊赢……这些把戏帮不了你理解对方立场或分歧的问题，只能让你"赢"一时。

F批判把争论当斗争/竞赛的错误观点。

[C] None of these will be easy, but you can start even if others refuse to. 下次陈述观点后，认真自问你的论证是否站得住脚；遇到立场不同的人，请他给出理由，公正完整地复述对方论点，不带偏见地评估，提出反驳并倾听回应。

C讲如何具体实践理性争论。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
These tools can help you win every argument—not in the unhelpful sense of beating your opponents but in the better sense of learning about the issues that divide people, learning why they disagree with us and learning to talk and work together with them. If we read others' arguments generously and well, we might still disagree with them, but we will at least understand them—and understanding them is a prerequisite for any productive subsequent action.
这些工具能帮你赢得每一场争论——不是以击败对手这种无益的方式，而是以更好的方式：了解使人们分裂的议题，了解他们为何与我们的意见相左，并学会与他们交谈、合作。如果我们宽厚而妥善地阅读他人的论点，或许仍会不同意他们，但至少能理解他们——而理解他们，是任何富有成效的后续行动的前提。
B
Of course, many discussions are not so successful. Still, we need to be careful not to accuse opponents of bad arguments too quickly. We should also learn to present our own arguments honestly, clearly, and gracefully.
当然，许多讨论并不如此成功。尽管如此，我们仍须谨慎，不要过快指责对方论据拙劣。我们也应当学会诚实、清晰而优雅地呈现自己的论点。
C
None of these will be easy but you can start even if others refuse to. Next time you state your position, formulate an argument for what you claim and explicitly consider opposing positions and the strengths they may have. This can seem confrontational, but it's actually a well-established rhetorical technique: conceding the strengths of others' arguments.
这些都并不容易，但即使他人拒绝，你也可以开始。下次你陈述立场时，为你所主张的内容构建论证，并明确考虑对立立场及其可能的可取之处。这看似对抗，实则是一种公认的老练修辞技巧：承认他人论点的长处。
D
Carnegie would be right if arguments were fights, which is how we often think of them. Like physical fights, verbal fights can leave both sides bloodied. Even when you win, you end up no better off than before the argument. Winning a fight does not win you friends.
若争论是打架——我们也常这样看待它——卡耐基就对了。如同肢体冲突，言语之战也会让双方都流血。即便你赢了，境况也不比争论前更好。打赢一架并不能为你赢得朋友。
E
In his 1936 work How to Win Friends and Influence People, Dale Carnegie wrote: "there is only one way…to get the best of an argument—and that is to avoid it." While that approach might silence or placate your opponent, it does nothing to change the fact that you may be wrong and the other person may be right.
戴尔·卡耐基在1936年的著作《如何赢得朋友和影响他人》中写道："只有一个办法……在争论中占上风——那就是避免争论。"尽管那种做法或许能让对手沉默或平息，却丝毫改变不了你可能错、而对方可能对的事实。
F
These views of arguments also undermine reason. If you see a conversation as a fight or competition, you can win by cheating as long as you don't get caught. You will be rewarded for crushing your opponent, not for finding the truth. This is a mistake.
这些对争论的看法也损害了理性。如果你把一场对话看作打架或竞赛，那么只要不被抓到，你尽可以靠欺骗取胜。你会因击垮对手而非发现真相而受奖赏。这是个错误。
G
There is a better way to win arguments. Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage in our state, and I do not. You present a number of cogent arguments. They are good, but you can do better. Instead of automatically criticizing my otherwise cogent arguments, you would show that my position is plausible, by revealing the contexts in which it is valid.
有一种更好的方式去赢得争论。想象你赞成提高本州的最低工资，而我不赞成。你提出若干有力的论点。它们不错，但你还能做得更好。你不会自动地批评我那些本也站得住脚的论点，而是会揭示其成立的语境，从而表明我的立场也有其合理之处。
41
排序题
答案 B
解题依据B段引用卡耐基《人性的弱点》："赢得争论的唯一办法就是避免争论"，并指出这种对争论的厌恶源于对争论的错误看法——作为全文引子引出话题，适合首段。
42
排序题
答案 G
解题依据B段末说卡耐基"avoid arguments"，G段接着说"如果争论真的是战斗（我们常这么想），卡耐基就是对的。像肢体打斗一样，口舌之争也会两败俱伤……"——B提出"避免争论"，G解释为什么把争论当战斗就该避免，完美承接。
43
排序题
答案 E
解题依据F段末说这些把戏只能让你"win—in one way"，E段开头"There is a better way to win arguments. Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage…"——F批判错误赢法，E引出"更好的赢法"并举例，转折承接。
44
排序题
答案 D
解题依据C段讲如何理性争论的具体做法，D段"Of course, many discussions are not so successful. Still, we need to be careful not to accuse opponents of bad arguments too quickly… Humility requires you to recognize weaknesses in your own arguments…"——C讲理想做法，D补充现实中的评估与谦逊，承接自然。
45
排序题
答案 A
解题依据A段"These tools can help you win every argument—not in the unhelpful sense of beating your opponents but in the better sense of learning about the issues that divide people…"——"These tools"指代D、C段讲的方法，总结收束全文。
解题铁律抓指代（These views / These tools）和转折（There is a better way / Of course），是排序题的黄金线索。
Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）— 医学期刊的坏科学
46
翻译
There is a great deal of this kind of nonsense in the medical journals which, when taken up by broadcasters and the lay press, generates both health scares and short-lived dietary enthusiasms.
医学期刊中充斥着大量这类无稽之谈，一旦被广播公司和非专业报刊炒作，就既引发健康恐慌，也带来转瞬即逝的饮食狂热。
采分点① a great deal of 大量；② take up 炒作/采纳；③ lay press 非专业报刊；④ health scares 健康恐慌。
47
翻译
nowadays anyone applying for a research post has to have published twice the number of papers that would have been required for the same post only 10 years ago.
如今，任何申请研究职位的人必须发表的论文数量，是仅10年前同一职位所要求数量的两倍。
采分点① applying for a research post 申请研究职位（现在分词作定语）；② twice the number of 两倍数量；③ 比较结构的翻译。
48
翻译
Attempts have been made to curb this tendency, for example, by trying to incorporate some measure of quality as well as quantity into the assessment of an applicant's papers.
人们已做出种种尝试来遏制这一倾向，例如，在评估申请人论文时，除了数量之外还试图纳入某种质量衡量标准。
采分点① Attempts have been made 已做出尝试（被动转主动）；② curb 遏制；③ incorporate…into 把……纳入；④ as well as 除……之外。
49
翻译
This would be reasonable enough if it were not for the fact that scientists can easily arrange to cite themselves in their future publications, or get associates to do so for them in return for similar favours.
要不是这样一个事实——科学家可以轻易安排在自己未来的出版物中引用自己，或请同事代为引用以回报类似的人情——这一本就足够合理了。
采分点① if it were not for 要不是（虚拟语气）；② cite 引用；③ in return for 作为……回报；④ favour 人情/恩惠。
50
翻译
If we are serious about ensuring that our science is both meaningful and reproducible, we must ensure that our institutions encourage that kind of science.
如果我们真的想确保科学既有意义又可重复，就必须确保我们的制度能够鼓励这种科学。
采分点① be serious about 认真对待；② reproducible 可重复的；③ institutions 制度/机构。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 回复志愿者咨询邮件

原题指令 Directions

Suppose you work for the university's "Aid Rural Primary Schools" program. Write a reply email to an international student volunteer who has inquired about the program, giving a detailed account of its specific arrangements. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the email. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】假设你在校“援助乡村小学”项目工作。给一名咨询该项目情况的国际学生志愿者写一封回信，详细说明项目的具体安排。字数约100词。邮件末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

假设你在大学"援助乡村小学"项目工作。写一封邮件回复一名国际学生志愿者的咨询，详细说明项目的具体安排。约100词，落款用"Li Ming"。

审题

① 文体：回复咨询的邮件；② 内容：项目时间、地点、工作内容、食宿交通等细节；③ 语气：热情友好。

参考范文

Dear Friend,

Thank you for your interest in our "Aiding Rural Primary School" program. I am writing to share the details you asked about.

The program will run from July 10 to August 10 in a primary school in a remote village in Hunan. As a volunteer, you will teach oral English to pupils aged 8 to 12, four classes a day from Monday to Friday. We will cover your round-trip train fare, provide free accommodation at the school, and arrange simple meals with local teachers. No prior teaching experience is required, though patience and an open mind are essential.

If you are ready to join us, please reply with your resume by June 30.

Yours sincerely, Li Ming

【译文】

亲爱的朋友：

感谢你对"援助乡村小学"项目的关注。我写信是想说明你询问的具体安排。

项目将于7月10日至8月10日在湖南一所偏远乡村小学开展。作为志愿者，你将为8至12岁的学生教授英语口语，周一至周五每天四节课。我们将承担你的往返火车票、提供校内免费住宿，并与当地老师一同安排简餐。无需教学经验，但耐心与开放的心态必不可少。

若你准备加入，请于6月30日前附上简历回复我们。

谨上，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文《途中》

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The cartoon shows two climbers halfway up a mountain. One, discouraged, says, "I'm tired; I won't climb any more." The other encourages him, "Don't move! Rest a while and then keep going."

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 漫画中两名登山者爬到半山腰，一人泄气地说“累了，我不爬了”，另一人鼓励道“别动！休息一下再接着爬。”

图画解读

两个登山者在半山腰，一个泄气说"累了，我不爬了"，另一个鼓励道"别动！休息一下再接着爬。"漫画寓意：面对困难，短暂休息后应坚持不懈，切勿半途而废。

审题框架

三段式：①描述图画；②点明寓意——坚持的重要性；③评论：学习与人生路上贵在坚持。160-200词。

参考范文

As is vividly depicted in the cartoon, two climbers are struggling halfway up a mountain. One, exhausted, complains, "I'm tired. I quit," while the other urges him, "Don't give up! Just rest a while, then keep climbing."

The drawing conveys an inspiring message: on the road to any goal, fatigue is natural, but quitting is never the answer. A proper rest merely recharges us; what ultimately counts is the resolve to press on. This holds especially true for a student preparing for the graduate entrance exam. There will be days when weariness and self-doubt overwhelm us, yet those who pause to catch their breath and then continue are the ones who reach the summit. Giving up halfway would waste all the effort already invested.

From my perspective, perseverance is the single most decisive factor between success and failure. Instead of yielding to momentary tiredness, we should rest strategically and keep moving, for the peak belongs to those who never truly stop.

【译文】

如漫画生动描绘，两名登山者正在半山腰艰难前行。一人精疲力竭地抱怨："累了，我不爬了"；另一人则劝道："别放弃！歇一下，接着爬。"

这幅画传递了鼓舞人心的讯息：在通往任何目标的路上，疲惫是常态，但放弃绝不可取。适度的休息只是为我们充电；真正关键的是继续前行的决心。对备战考研的学生而言尤其如此。总有些日子，疲惫与自我怀疑会将我们淹没，然而那些稍作喘息便继续前行的人，才是登顶之人。半途而废只会让已付出的努力付诸东流。

在我看来，坚持是成败之间最具决定性的因素。与其向一时的疲惫屈服，不如策略性地休息、继续向前，因为山顶属于那些从未真正停下的人。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读（FSA丙烯酰胺健康警告）

Even if families don't sit down to eat together as frequently as before, millions of Britons will nonetheless have got a share this weekend of one of the nation's great traditions: the Sunday roast. 1 a cold winter's day, few culinary pleasures can 2 it. Yet as we report now, the food police are determined that this 3 should be rendered yet another guilty pleasure 4 to damage our health.

即便各家各户不再像从前那样常常同桌吃饭，这个周末仍有数百万英国人会分享这个国家最伟大的传统之一：周日烤肉。在一个寒冷的冬日，几乎没有什么美食乐趣能与之媲美。然而正如我们现在报道的，食品警察决意要把这种享受变成又一个被认定会损害健康的"罪恶快感"。

The Food Standards Authority (FSA) has 5 a public warning about the risks of a compound called acrylamide that forms in some foods cooked 6 high temperatures. This means that people should 7 crisping their roast potatoes, reject thin-crust pizzas and only 8 toast their bread. But where is the evidence to support such alarmist advice? 9 studies have shown that acrylamide can cause neurological damage in mice, there is no 10 evidence that it causes cancer in humans.

英国食品标准局（FSA）已就一种名为丙烯酰胺的化合物的风险发布公开警告——该化合物在高温烹制某些食物时产生。这意味着人们应避免把烤土豆烤得酥脆，拒绝薄底披萨，面包也只能微微烘烤。但是，支持这种危言耸听建议的证据在哪里？虽然研究已表明丙烯酰胺会对小鼠造成神经损伤，但尚无确凿证据证明它会导致人类癌症。

Scientists say the compound is 11 to cause cancer but have no hard scientific proof. 12 the precautionary principle, it could be argued that it is 13 to follow the FSA advice. 14, it was rumoured that smoking caused cancer for years before the evidence was found to prove a 15.

科学家说这种化合物可能致癌，但没有确凿的科学证据。基于预防原则，可以说听从FSA的建议是明智之举。毕竟，在找到证据证明吸烟与癌症的关联之前，吸烟致癌的传闻已经流传多年。

Doubtless a piece of boiled beef can always be 16 up on Sunday alongside some steamed vegetables, without the Yorkshire pudding and no wine. But would life be worth living? 17, the FSA says it is not telling people to cut out roast foods 18, but to reduce their lifetime intake. However, its 19 risks coming across as being pushy and overprotective. Constant health scares just 20 with no one listening.

毫无疑问，周日一盘煮牛肉总可以配上些蒸蔬菜上桌，没有约克郡布丁，也没有葡萄酒。但这样的生活还值得过吗？平心而论，FSA说它并不是叫人们完全戒掉烤制食品，而是减少终其一生的摄入量。然而，它这场宣传有显得咄咄逼人、过度保护之嫌。没完没了的健康恐吓最终只会无人理睬。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读（英国"文化小镇"奖）

A group of Labour MPs, among them Yvette Cooper, are bringing in the new year with a call to institute a UK "town of culture" award. The proposal is that it should sit alongside the existing city of culture title, which was held by Hull in 2017, and has been awarded to Coventry for 2021. Cooper and her colleagues argue that the success of the crown for Hull, where it brought in £220m of investment and an avalanche of arts, ought not to be confined to cities. Britain's town, it is true, are not prevented from applying, but they generally lack the resources to put together a bid to beat their bigger competitors. A town of culture award could, it is argued, become an annual event, attracting funding and creating jobs.

一批工党议员——伊薇特·库珀就在其中——在新年伊始呼吁设立英国"文化小镇"奖。提议是让它与现有的"文化之城"称号并列：该称号2017年由赫尔获得，2021年颁给考文垂。库珀及其同事认为，赫尔封冠后吸引了2.2亿英镑投资和大量艺术活动，这种成功不应只局限于城市。诚然，英国的小镇并未被禁止申请，但它们普遍缺乏资源来组织竞标以击败更大的竞争者。他们认为，"文化小镇"奖可成为一年一度的盛事，吸引资金、创造就业。

Some might see the proposal as a booze prize for the fact that Britain is no longer able to apply for the much more prestigious title of European capital of culture, a sought-after award bagged by Glasgow in 1990 and Liverpool in 2008. A cynic might speculate that the UK is on the verge of disappearing into an endless fever of self-celebration in its desperation to reinvent itself for the post-Brexit world: after town of culture, who knows what will follow — village of culture? Suburb of culture? Hamlet of culture?

有人可能会把这项提议看作一种安慰奖，因为英国已无力角逐更负盛名的"欧洲文化之都"称号——这一炙手可热的奖项曾于1990年和2008年分别被格拉斯哥和利物浦摘得。愤世嫉俗者可能揣测，英国为在脱欧后的世界重塑自我而孤注一掷，正濒临陷入一场没完没了的自我庆祝狂热：文化小镇之后，谁知道还会冒出什么——文化村庄？文化郊区？文化小村落？

It is also wise to recall that such titles are not a cure-all. A badly run "year of culture" washes in and out of a place like the tide, bringing prominence for a spell but leaving no lasting benefits to the community. The really successful holders of such titles are those that do a great deal more than fill hotel bedrooms and bring in high-profile arts events and good press for a year. They transform the aspirations of the people who live there; they nudge the self-image of the city into a bolder and more optimistic light. It is hard to get right, and requires a remarkable degree of vision, as well as cooperation between city authorities, the private sector, community groups and cultural organisations. But it can be done: Glasgow's year as European capital of culture can certainly be seen as one of a complex series of factors that have turned the city into the powerhouse of art, music and theatre that it remains today.

同样明智的是要记住，这类称号并非万灵药。运作糟糕的"文化年"像潮水一样涨了又退，只带来一阵风光，却不给社区留下持久益处。真正成功的称号拥有者，所做的远不止填满酒店客房、在一年内带来高调艺术活动和正面报道。他们改变当地居民的抱负；他们把城市的自我形象推向更大胆、更乐观的方向。要做对很难，需要非凡的远见，以及市政当局、私营部门、社区团体和文化机构之间的合作。但这并非不可能：格拉斯哥的"欧洲文化之都"之年，完全可以被看作把这座城市变为今日艺术、音乐和戏剧重镇的一系列复杂因素之一。

A "town of culture" could be not just about the arts but about honouring a town's peculiarities — helping sustain its high street, supporting local facilities and above all celebrating its people. Jeremy Wright, the culture secretary, should welcome this positive, hope-filled proposal, and turn it into action.

"文化小镇"不应只关乎艺术，更应关乎褒扬一个小镇的独特之处——帮助维持其商业街、支持本地设施，最重要的是礼赞它的人民。文化大臣杰里米·赖特应当欢迎这项积极、充满希望的提议，并将其付诸行动。

Text 2   科学出版业的印钞机模式（26–30）

Scientific publishing has long been a licence to print money. Scientists need journals in which to publish their research, so they will supply the articles without monetary reward. Other scientists perform the specialised work of peer review also for free, because it is a central element in the acquisition of status and the production of scientific knowledge.

长期以来，科学出版一直是台印钞机。科学家需要期刊发表自己的研究，于是他们无偿提供稿件。另一些科学家也免费承担同行评审的专业工作，因为这是获取地位、生产科学知识的核心环节。

With the content of papers secured for free, the publisher needs only to find a market for its journal. Until this century, university libraries were not very price sensitive. Scientific publishers routinely report profit margins approaching 40% on their operations, at a time when the rest of the publishing industry is in an existential crisis.

论文内容既已免费到手，出版商只需为自己的期刊找到市场即可。直到本世纪之前，大学图书馆对价格并不敏感。在出版业其他领域深陷生存危机之际，科学出版商却 routinely 报告其运营利润率接近40%。

The Dutch giant Elsevier, which claims to publish 25% of the scientific papers produced in the world, made profits of more than £900m last year, while UK universities alone spent more than £210m in 2016 to enable researchers to access their own publicly funded research; both figures seem to rise unstoppably despite increasingly desperate efforts to change them.

荷兰巨头爱思唯尔声称出版了全球25%的科学论文，去年获利超9亿英镑；而仅英国各大学在2016年就花费超过2.1亿英镑，才能让研究者获取他们自己由公共资金资助的研究成果；尽管各方愈发拼命地想改变这两个数字，它们却似乎仍不可阻挡地上涨。

The most drastic, and thoroughly illegal, reaction has been the emergence of Sci-Hub, a kind of global photocopier for scientific papers, set up in 2012, which now claims to offer access to every paywalled article published since 2015. The success of Sci-Hub, which relies on researchers passing on copies they have themselves legally accessed, shows the legal ecosystem has lost legitimacy among its users and must be transformed so that it works for all participants.

最激烈、也完全非法的反应，是Sci-Hub的出现——这台2012年建立的全球科学论文复印机，如今声称能获取2015年以来每一篇付费墙后的文章。Sci-Hub靠研究者转发自己合法获取的副本而成功，这表明合法生态系统已在用户中失去正当性，必须加以改造，才能服务于所有参与者。

In Britain the move towards open access publishing has been driven by funding bodies. In some ways it has been very successful. More than half of all British scientific research is now published under open access terms: either freely available from the moment of publication, or paywalled for a year or more so that the publishers can make a profit before being placed on general release.

在英国，向开放获取出版的转型由资助机构推动。在某些方面它非常成功。如今英国一半以上的科学研究以开放获取条款发表：要么一经发表即可免费获取，要么付费墙保留一年或更久，好让出版商在公开发布前先赚到钱。

Yet the new system has not worked out any cheaper for the universities. Publishers have responded to the demand that they make their product free to readers by charging their writers fees to cover the costs of preparing an article. These range from around £500 to $5,000. A report last year pointed out that the costs both of subscriptions and of these "article preparation costs" had been steadily rising at a rate above inflation. In some ways the scientific publishing model resembles the economy of the social internet: labour is provided free in exchange for the hope of status, while huge profits are made by a few big firms who run the market places. In both cases, we need a rebalancing of power.

然而，新体系并没有让大学花得更便宜。出版商对"产品向读者免费"的要求做出回应的方式，是向作者收费以支付文章制作成本。费用从约500英镑到5000美元不等。去年一份报告指出，订阅成本和这些"文章制作费"都在以高于通胀的速度稳步上涨。在某些方面，科学出版模式酷似社交互联网经济：劳动被免费提供，以换取对地位的渴望，而运营市场的少数大公司赚取巨额利润。在这两种情形中，我们都需要重新平衡权力。

peer review 同行评审

paywalled adj. 付费墙的
legitimacy n. 正当性
open access 开放获取
rebalancing n. 再平衡
Text 3   企业董事会性别配额制之争（31–35）

Progressives often support diversity mandates as a path to equality and a way to level the playing field. But all too often such policies are an insincere form of virtue-signaling that benefits only the most privileged and does little to help average people.

进步派常支持多样性强制规定，视其为通向平等、公平竞争环境的途径。但这类政策往往是一种虚伪的"道德标榜"，只让最特权者受益，对普通人几乎毫无帮助。

A pair of bills sponsored by Massachusetts state Senator Jason Lewis and House Speaker Pro Tempore Patricia Haddad, to ensure "gender parity" on boards and commissions, provide a case in point.

马萨诸塞州参议员杰森·刘易斯和众议院临时议长帕特里夏·哈达德提出的两项法案——旨在确保董事会和委员会的"性别平等"——就是一个很好的例子。

Haddad and Lewis are concerned that more than half the state-government boards are less than 40 percent female. In order to ensure that elite women have more such opportunities, they have proposed imposing government quotas. If the bills become law, state boards and commissions will be required to set aside 50 percent of board seats for women by 2022.

哈达德和刘易斯担心，超过一半的州政府董事会中女性比例不足40%。为确保精英女性有更多此类机会，他们提议实施政府配额。若法案成法，到2022年各州董事会和委员会须为女性保留50%的席位。

The bills are similar to a measure recently adopted in California, which last year became the first state to require gender quotas for private companies. In signing the measure, California Governor Jerry Brown admitted that the law, which expressly classifies people on the basis of sex, is probably unconstitutional.

这两项法案类似于加州最近通过的一项措施——加州去年成为首个对私营企业强制性别配额的州。在签署该措施时，加州州长杰里·布朗承认，这部公然以性别对人分类的法律很可能违宪。

The US Supreme Court frowns on sex-based classifications unless they are designed to address an "important" policy interest. Because the California law applies to all boards, even where there is no history of prior discrimination, courts are likely to rule that the law violates the constitutional guarantee of "equal protection."

美国最高法院不赞成基于性别的分类，除非其旨在解决"重要的"政策利益。由于加州法律适用于所有董事会，即便在那些没有过往歧视历史的地方，法院也很可能裁定该法律违反了宪法"平等保护"的保障。

But are such government mandates even necessary? Female participation on corporate boards may not currently mirror the percentage of women in the general population, but so what?

但这样的政府强制规定真的有必要吗？企业董事会的女性比例目前或许未能反映女性在总人口中的比例，但那又怎样？

The number of women on corporate boards has been steadily increasing without government interference. According to a study by Catalyst, between 2010 and 2015 the share of women on the boards of global corporations increased by 54 percent.

即便没有政府干预，企业董事会的女性人数也一直在稳步增加。根据Catalyst的一项研究，2010至2015年间，全球公司董事会中女性的比例增加了54%。

Requiring companies to make gender the primary qualification for board membership will inevitably lead to less experienced private sector boards. That is exactly what happened when Norway adopted a nationwide corporate gender quota.

要求企业把性别作为董事会成员的首要资历，将不可避免地导致私营部门董事会经验不足。挪威在全国实行企业性别配额时，情况正是如此。

Writing in The New Republic, Alice Lee notes that increasing the number of opportunities for board membership without increasing the pool of qualified women to serve on such boards has led to a "golden skirt" phenomenon, where the same elite women scoop up multiple seats on a variety of boards.

艾丽斯·李在《新共和》撰文指出，增加董事会席位机会、却不扩大合格女性人才库，导致了"金色裙摆"现象——同一批精英女性包揽各家董事会的多个席位。

Next time somebody pushes corporate quotas as a way to promote gender equity, remember that such policies are largely self-serving measures that make their sponsors feel good but do little to help average women.

下次再有人把企业配额作为促进性别平等的手段来推销时，请记住：这类政策在很大程度上是自利之举，让发起人自我感觉良好，对普通女性却帮助甚微。

31

Text 4   法国数字服务税（GAFA税）（36–40）

Last Thursday, the French Senate passed a digital services tax, which would impose an entirely new tax on large multinationals that provide digital services to consumers or users in France. Digital services include everything from providing a platform for selling goods and services online to targeting advertising based on user data, and the tax applies to gross revenue from such services. Many French politicians and media outlets have referred to this as a "GAFA tax," meaning that it is designed to apply primarily to companies such as Google, Apple, Facebook and Amazon — in other words, multinational tech companies based in the United States.

上周四，法国参议院通过了一项数字服务税，将对向法国消费者或用户提供数字服务的大型跨国公司征收一项全新税种。数字服务无所不包，从提供在线销售商品和服务的平台，到基于用户数据投放定向广告；该税适用于此类服务的总收入。许多法国政客和媒体称之为"GAFA税"，意思是它主要针对谷歌、苹果、脸书和亚马逊等公司——也就是总部设在美国的跨国科技公司。

The digital services tax now awaits the signature of President Emmanuel Macron, who has expressed support for the measure, and it could go into effect within the next few weeks. But it has already sparked significant controversy, with the United States trade representative opening an investigation into whether the tax discriminates against American companies, which in turn could lead to trade sanctions against France.

这项数字服务税目前正等待埃马纽埃尔·马克龙总统签署——他已表示支持该措施，几周内即可生效。但它已引发重大争议：美国贸易代表已展开调查，认定该税是否歧视美国公司，而这反过来可能导致对法国的贸易制裁。

The French tax is not just a unilateral move by one country in need of revenue. Instead, the digital services tax is part of a much larger trend, with countries over the past few years proposing or putting in place an alphabet soup of new international tax provisions. These have included Britain's DPT (diverted profits tax), Australia's MAAL (multinational anti-avoidance law), and India's SEP (significant economic presence) test, to name but a few. At the same time, the European Union, Spain, Britain and several other countries have all seriously contemplated digital services taxes.

法国这项税并非一个需要财政收入的国家单方面的举动。相反，数字服务税是一股更大趋势的一部分：过去几年，各国提出或实施了一大堆新的国际税收条款，缩写名目繁多。其中包括英国的DPT（转移利润税）、澳大利亚的MAAL（跨国反避税法）、印度的SEP（显著经济存在）测试，等等。与此同时，欧盟、西班牙、英国和其他几个国家都在认真考虑征收数字服务税。

These unilateral developments differ in their specifics, but they are all designed to tax multinationals on income and revenue that countries believe they should have a right to tax, even if international tax rules do not grant them that right. In other words, they all share a view that the international tax system has failed to keep up with the current economy.

这些单方面举措细节各异，但都旨在就各国认为自己有权征税的收入和利润对跨国公司征税——即便国际税收规则并未授予它们这一权利。换言之，它们都认同这样一种观点：现行国际税收体系已跟不上当前经济的发展。

In response to these many unilateral measures, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) is currently working with 131 countries to reach a consensus by the end of 2020 on an international solution. Both France and the United States are involved in the organization's work, but France's digital services tax and the American response raise questions about what the future holds for the international tax system.

为应对这众多单方面举措，经济合作与发展组织（OECD）目前正与131个国家合作，力争在2020年底前就国际解决方案达成共识。法国和美国都参与了该组织的工作，但法国的数字服务税和美国的反应，给国际税收体系的未来蒙上了疑问。

France's planned tax is a clear warning: Unless a broad consensus can be reached on reforming the international tax system, other nations are likely to follow suit, and American companies will face a cascade of different taxes from dozens of nations that will prove burdensome and costly.

法国拟征的这项税是一个明确警告：除非就改革国际税收体系达成广泛共识，否则其他国家很可能纷纷效仿，美国企业将面临来自几十个国家的一连串不同税收，这将是沉重而代价高昂的。

36

【选项】A.眼神注视很短暂 B.对视过久天生显粗鲁 C.眼神接触是友好社交信号 D.性格影响人对视的反应 E.眼神接触背后的生物学因素正被研究 F.多数人与陌生人对视不自在 G.眼神接触也可能有攻击性。

Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）— 文艺复兴与理性时代
46
翻译
With the Church's teachings and ways of thinking being eclipsed by the Renaissance, the gap between the Medieval and modern periods had been bridged, leading to new and unexplored intellectual territories.
随着教会的教义和思维方式因文艺复兴而黯然失色，中世纪与近代之间的鸿沟得以弥合，从而开辟出全新的、尚未探索的知识领域。
采分点① eclipse 使黯然失色；② bridge the gap 弥合鸿沟；③ leading to 现在分词作结果；④ unexplored territories 未探索领域。
47
翻译
Before each of their revelations, many thinkers at the time had sustained more ancient ways of thinking, including the geo-centric view that the Earth was at the centre of our universe.
在他们各自做出重大发现之前，当时的许多思想家一直沿用更为古老的思维方式，其中就包括"地球处于宇宙中心"的地心说。
采分点① revelation 启示/重大发现；② sustain 维持/沿用；③ geo-centric view 地心说；④ 同位语从句的处理。
48
翻译
Despite attempts by the Church to suppress this new generation of logicians and rationalists, more explanations for how the universe functioned were being made at a rate that the people could no longer ignore.
尽管教会试图压制这新一代逻辑学家和理性主义者，但关于宇宙如何运行的新解释仍在不断涌现，其速度之快已让人们无法再忽视。
采分点① suppress 镇压/压制；② rationalist 理性主义者；③ at a rate that 以……速度；④ 被动语态的中文处理。
49
翻译
As many took on the duty of trying to integrate reasoning and scientific philosophies into the world, the Renaissance was over and it was time for a new era — the Age of Reason.
当许多人承担起将理性和科学哲学融入现实世界的重任时，文艺复兴便告结束，一个新时代——理性时代——到来了。
采分点① take on the duty 承担责任；② integrate…into 把……融入；③ it was time for 是……的时候了。
50
翻译
Such actions to seek knowledge and to understand what information we already knew were captured by the Latin phrase 'sapere aude' or 'dare to know', after Immanuel Kant used it in his essay "An Answer to the Question: What is Enlightenment?".
这种追求知识、理解已知信息的行动，被概括为拉丁语箴言"sapere aude"，即"敢于求知"——这是伊曼努尔·康德在其文章《回答这个问题：什么是启蒙？》中所用的。
采分点① capture 概括/捕捉；② sapere aude 敢于求知（音译+意译）；③ after 此处意为"效仿/源自"；④ 书名号的使用。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 通知

原题指令 Directions

The Student Union has delegated you to notify international students of an upcoming singing contest. Write a notice of about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the notice.

【译文】学生会委派你通知留学生即将举行一场歌唱比赛。写一则约100词的通知。通知末尾不要署自己的名字。

题目

校学生会委派你通知国际学生即将举办的歌唱比赛。写一则约100词的通知。落款不要用自己真名。

审题

① 文体：通知（Notice）；② 内容：比赛时间、地点、参赛对象、报名方式；③ 语气：正式、清晰。

参考范文

Notice

Aiming to enrich campus life and promote cultural exchange, the Students' Union will hold an English Singing Contest on the evening of December 25 in the University Hall.

All international students are warmly welcome to participate. Each contestant may perform one English song, lasting no more than five minutes. Those interested are requested to sign up at the Students' Union office before December 18. Prizes will be awarded to the top three, and every participant will receive a souvenir.

For further information, please contact us via the campus network. We look forward to your active participation.

The Students' Union

【译文】

通知

为丰富校园生活、促进文化交流，学生会将于12月25日晚在大学礼堂举办英语歌唱比赛。

我们热忱欢迎所有国际学生参加。每位选手可演唱一首英文歌曲，时长不超过五分钟。有意者请于12月18日前到学生会办公室报名。前三名将获奖，所有参与者都将获赠纪念品。

更多信息请通过校园网联系我们。期待你的积极参与。

学生会

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文《习惯》

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The two pictures show different study habits. The girl on the left, facing a pile of homework, thinks, "I'll only feel relieved if I finish it as early as possible." The boy on the right, staring at an empty desk, thinks, "I won't start until the last minute."

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 两幅图对比不同的学习习惯。左边女生面对堆积的作业，心想“尽早完成才放心”；右边男生对着空空的书桌发呆，心想“不到最后不动手”。

图画解读

左右两幅图：左边女生面对堆积的作业，气泡"尽早完成才放心"；右边男生对着空空的书桌发呆，气泡"不到最后不动手"。漫画对比两种习惯：未雨绸缪 vs 拖延症。

审题框架

三段式：①对比描述两幅图；②点明寓意——好习惯是成功之基，拖延误事；③评论：青年应养成今日事今日毕的好习惯。160-200词。

参考范文

The two pictures present a sharp contrast in study habits. On the left, a diligent student tackles her piles of assignments ahead of schedule, reassured by the thought that finishing early brings peace of mind. On the right, a chronic procrastinator sits idly before an empty desk, putting off all work until the last minute.

The implied message is thought-provoking: habits, though seemingly trivial, shape our future. The student who finishes tasks promptly enjoys both high efficiency and a sense of control, whereas the inveterate procrastinator repeatedly burns the midnight oil, submits shoddy work and lives under constant stress. As the saying goes, a stitch in time saves nine. Small daily habits, accumulated over years, determine whether we thrive or merely muddle through.

From my perspective, university students should consciously cultivate the good habit of getting things done early. Procrastination only drains our potential, while a proactive routine paves the way to academic excellence and, ultimately, a brighter career.

【译文】

两幅图呈现出学习习惯上的鲜明对比。左边，一名勤奋的学生提前处理堆积的作业，想着"早点完成才放心"而安心；右边，一名惯于拖延的人对着空桌发呆，把所有事拖到最后一刻。

其中寓意发人深省：习惯虽看似琐碎，却塑造我们的未来。及时完成任务的学生既高效又有掌控感；而积习难改的拖延者则屡屡熬夜、交出差强人意的作业、长期活在压力之下。常言道，及时一针省九针。经年累月的小习惯，决定了我们究竟出类拔萃还是浑浑噩噩。

在我看来，大学生应有意识地养成"今日事今日毕"的好习惯。拖延只会耗尽我们的潜力，而主动的节奏则为学业卓越、乃至更光明的职业铺平道路。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读（流体智力与腹部脂肪）

Fluid intelligence is the type of intelligence that has to do with short-term memory and the ability to think quickly, logically, and abstractly in order to solve new problems. It 1 in young adulthood, levels out for a period of time, and then 2 starts to slowly decline as we age. But 3 aging is inevitable, scientists are finding out that certain changes in brain function may not be.

流体智力是一种与短期记忆以及为解决新问题而快速、合乎逻辑、抽象思考的能力相关的智力。它在青年时期达到顶峰，平稳维持一段时间，然后随着年龄增长而逐渐开始缓慢下降。但尽管衰老不可避免，科学家却发现大脑功能的某些变化或许并非必然。

One study found that muscle loss and the 4 of body fat around the abdomen are associated with a decline in fluid intelligence. This suggests the 5 that lifestyle factors might help prevent or 6 this type of decline.

一项研究发现，肌肉流失以及腹部周围脂肪的堆积，与流体智力下降有关。这表明存在这样一种可能：生活方式因素或许有助于预防或延缓这种衰退。

The researchers looked at data that 7 measurements of lean muscle and abdominal fat from more than 4,000 middle-to-older-aged men and women and 8 that data to reported changes in fluid intelligence over a six-year period. They found that middle-aged people 9 higher measures of abdominal fat 10 worse on measures of fluid intelligence as the years 11.

研究人员考察了相关数据，其中包含4000多名中老年男女的精瘦肌肉和腹部脂肪测量值，并将这些数据与六年间所记录的流体智力变化进行比较。他们发现，随着岁月流逝，腹部脂肪含量较高的中年人，在流体智力测试中得分更差。

For women, the association may be 12 to changes in immunity that resulted from excess abdominal fat; in men, the immune system did not appear to be 13. It is hoped that future studies could 14 these differences and perhaps lead to different 15 for men and women.

对女性而言，这种关联或许可归因于腹部脂肪过多引起的免疫力变化；而在男性身上，免疫系统似乎并未牵涉其中。人们希望未来的研究能解释这些差异，并或许能为男性和女性带来不同的对策。

16, there are steps you can 17 to help reduce abdominal fat and maintain lean muscle mass as you age in order to protect both your physical and mental 18. The two highly recommended lifestyle approaches are maintaining or increasing your 19 of aerobic exercise and following a Mediterranean-style 20 that is high in fiber and eliminates highly processed foods.

与此同时，随着年龄增长，你可以采取一些措施来帮助减少腹部脂肪、保持精瘦肌肉量，从而保护身心两方面的健康。两种备受推荐的生活方式是：保持或增加有氧运动水平；遵循高纤维、剔除高度加工食品的地中海式饮食。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读（英国铁路票价上涨）

How can Britain's train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares? It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise. This year's rise, an average of 2.7 per cent, may be a fraction lower than last year's, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation.

英国铁路运营商究竟要如何为又一次提高客运票价辩解？这已成为一场冷酷却雷打不动的年度仪式：每年一月铁路出行成本就上涨，给那些别无选择、只能靠铁路通勤或出行的人平添沉重负担。今年平均2.7%的涨幅或许比去年略低一点，但仍远高于官方消费者价格指数（CPI）衡量的通胀水平。

Successive governments have permitted such increases on the grounds that the cost of investing in and running the rail network should be borne by those who use it, rather than the general taxpayer. Why, the argument goes, should a car-driving pensioner from Lincolnshire have to subsidise the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey? Equally, there is a sense that the travails of commuters in the South East, many of whom will face among the biggest rises, have received too much attention compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North.

历届政府都以如下理由允许涨价：投资和运营铁路网的成本应由使用者承担，而非普通纳税人。其论点是：一个来自林肯郡、开车出行的退休老人，凭什么要补贴萨里郡股票经纪人的日常通勤？同样，人们也觉得，东南部通勤者的艰辛（其中许多人将面临最大涨幅之一）得到了过多关注，相比之下，那些必须忍受中部和北部相对落后基础设施的人却被忽视了。

However, over the past 12 months, those commuters have also experienced some of the worst rail strikes in years. It is all very well train operators trumpeting the improvements they are making to the network, but passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel. The responsibility for the latest wave of strikes rests on the unions. However, there is a strong case that those who have been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered.

然而，过去12个月里，这些通勤者还经历了多年来最严重的几轮铁路罢工。铁路运营商大张旗鼓地宣扬他们对路网所做的改善固然很好，但乘客既然如今支付了大笔旅费，就理应能期待基本的服务水平。最新这波罢工的责任在工会。尽管如此，完全有理由认为，那些受劳工行动影响最严重的人，应当为其所遭受的 disruption 获得赔偿。

The Government has pledged to change the law to introduce a minimum service requirement so that, even when strikes occur, services can continue to operate. This should form part of a wider package of measures to address the long-running problems on Britain's railways. Yes, more investment is needed, but passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely if they must also endure cramped, unreliable services, interrupted by regular chaos when timetables are changed, or planned maintenance is managed incompetently. The threat of nationalisation may have been seen off for now, but it will return with a vengeance if the justified anger of passengers is not addressed in short order.

政府已承诺修改法律，引入最低服务要求，以便即便发生罢工，列车也能继续运行。这应成为解决英国铁路长期问题的更广泛一揽子措施的一部分。是的，需要更多投资，但如果乘客还得忍受拥挤、不可靠的服务——还要被时刻表变更时的经常性混乱、或计划内维护的拙劣管理所打断——他们不会愿意无限期地多掏钱。国有化的威胁眼下或许已被击退，但如果乘客理所当然的愤怒得不到及时解决，它必将猛烈卷土重来。

Text 2   印尼反贫困项目与森林砍伐（26–30）

Last year marked the third year in a row that Indonesia's bleak rate of deforestation has slowed in pace. One reason for the turnaround may be the country's antipoverty program.

去年是印尼触目惊心的森林砍伐速度连续第三年放缓。这一转变的原因之一，可能是该国的反贫困项目。

In 2007, Indonesia started phasing in a program that gives money to its poorest residents under certain conditions, such as requiring people to keep kids in school or get regular medical care. Called conditional cash transfers or CCTs, these social assistance programs are designed to reduce inequality and break the cycle of poverty. They're already used in dozens of countries worldwide. In Indonesia, the program has provided enough food and medicine to substantially reduce severe growth problems among children.

2007年，印尼开始逐步推行一项计划：在满足一定条件下向最贫困居民发放现金，比如要求人们让孩子继续上学或定期就医。这类社会救助方案被称为"有条件现金转移"（CCT），旨在减少不平等、打破贫困的循环。它已被世界几十个国家采用。在印尼，该项目提供了充足的食物和药品，大幅减少了儿童中严重的发育问题。

But CCT programs don't generally consider effects on the environment. In fact, poverty alleviation and environmental protection are often viewed as conflicting goals, says Paul Ferraro, an economist at Johns Hopkins University.

但CCT项目通常不考虑对环境的影响。约翰斯·霍普金斯大学经济学家保罗·费拉罗说，事实上，减贫与环保常被视为相互冲突的目标。

That's because economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation, while protecting the environment is sometimes correlated with greater poverty. However, those correlations don't prove cause and effect. The only previous study analyzing causality, based on an area in Mexico that had instituted CCTs, supported the traditional view. There, as people got more money, some of them may have more cleared land for cattle to raise for meat, Ferraro says.

这是因为经济增长可能与环境退化相关，而保护环境有时又与更严重的贫困相关。然而，这些相关性并不能证明因果关系。此前唯一一项分析因果关系的研究基于墨西哥一个实施CCT的地区，它支持了传统观点。费拉罗说，在那里，随着人们拿到更多钱，有些人可能就清理出更多土地来养牛取肉。

Such programs do not have to negatively affect the environment, though. Ferraro wanted to see if Indonesia's poverty-alleviation program was affecting deforestation. Indonesia has the third-largest area of tropical forest in the world and one of the highest deforestation rates.

不过，这类项目并非必然对环境造成负面影响。费拉罗想弄清印尼的减贫项目是否影响了森林砍伐。印尼拥有世界第三大热带森林面积，却也是森林砍伐率最高的国家之一。

Ferraro analyzed satellite data showing annual forest loss from 2008 to 2012—including during Indonesia's phase-in of the antipoverty program—in 7,468 forested villages across 15 provinces. "We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation," Ferraro says.

费拉罗分析了2008至2012年显示年度森林流失的卫星数据——其中涵盖印尼逐步推行反贫困项目的时期——涉及15个省7468个森林村落。"我们发现，该项目与森林砍伐率下降30%相关，"费拉罗说。

That's likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says. Typically, if rains are delayed, people may clear land to plant more rice to supplement their harvests. With the CCTs, individuals instead can use the money to supplement their harvests.

费拉罗说，这很可能是因为农村贫困人口把这笔钱当作应对恶劣天气的临时保险。通常，如果降雨推迟，人们可能会清理土地多种水稻以补充收成。有了CCT，人们反而可以用这笔钱直接补充收成。

Whether this research translates elsewhere is anybody's guess. Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice and market access. And regardless of transferability, the study shows that what's good for people may also be good for the environment. Even if this program didn't reduce poverty, Ferraro says, "the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs."

这项研究能否推广到别处，谁也说不准。费拉罗认为，由于种稻的重要性、市场可达性等共同点，结果或许可推广到亚洲其他地区。但无论可否推广，该研究表明：对人有利的事，可能也对环境有利。费拉罗说，即便这个项目没有减贫，"仅从避免的二氧化碳排放来看，其价值就已超过项目成本。"

Text 3   维多利亚时代照片里为什么不笑（31–35）

As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?). I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir. People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh. They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.

作为一名总在寻找能促使我们重新评估过去的文字或图像的历史学家，我痴迷于寻找那些展现维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片（还有什么比这更能打破19世纪拘谨刻板的印象呢？）。我找到了不少——自从把它们发到推特上，就引起了不小的轰动。人们惊讶地看到证据：维多利亚人也有乐趣，也会笑，而且确实笑过。他们注意到，随着百年左右的隔阂因我们共有的笑的体验而消弭，维多利亚人似乎突然变得更像活生生的人。

Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance. How do we explain this trend?

当然，我得承认，我收藏的"微笑的维多利亚人"在1840至1900年间浩如烟海的肖像摄影作品中只占极小比例；其中绝大多数是被拍者在绘景背景前凄惨僵硬地摆姿势，或心不在焉地凝视中景。我们该如何解释这一趋势？

During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs. The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.

在1840和1850年代摄影术早期，曝光时间之长是出了名的：达盖尔银版法（在镀银铜板上成像）可能要几分钟才能完成，被拍者一旦挪动位置或调整肢体，照片就会模糊。要在相机施展魔法时一直保持咧嘴笑，实在难以想象，于是一种不置可否的木然凝视就成了常态。

But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous. Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.

但到1880年代，曝光时间已大大缩短，勃朗尼箱式相机和其他便携相机的问世意味着——尽管以今天的数码标准仍算慢——曝光几乎是瞬间完成的。到1890年代，自然的笑容已相对容易捕捉，因此我们必须到别处寻找维多利亚人仍不愿微笑的原因。

One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin. "Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene. A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).

一种解释可能是：露齿傻笑会有失体面。维多利亚时代一句流行格言说："大自然给我们嘴唇，就是为了遮住牙齿。"这暗示在正规牙科学诞生之前，口腔卫生状况往往令人震惊。在维多利亚社会，一口健康、整洁、整齐的"珍珠白牙"是罕见景象，是超级富豪的专属（即便那时，口腔卫生也并无保障）。

A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened teeth) lacked class: drunks, tramps and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons. Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".

露齿大笑（尤其是牙齿有缝或发黑时）不够体面：醉汉、流浪汉和音乐厅表演者才会扮鬼脸、咧嘴笑得像刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下露出牙龈的柴郡猫那样宽，但对有教养的人来说这并不好看。就连喜爱开怀大笑的马克·吐温也说，说到肖像照，"没有什么比一个愚蠢可笑的微笑被永远定格更糟糕的了。"

Text 4   网络中立性之争（36–40）

From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals. That's why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the internet.

从宽带时代早期起，消费者和网络公司的拥护者就担心：出售宽带连接的有线电视和电话公司有能力、也有动机偏袒关联网站、打压竞争对手。正因如此，人们强烈要求制定规则，防止宽带供应商在网上挑选赢家和输家，保护作为互联网命脉的自由与创新。

Yet that demand has been almost impossible to win—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either.

然而，这一诉求几乎不可能实现——部分原因是来自宽带供应商、反监管保守派和法院的阻力。一家联邦上诉法院周二再度介入，但它非但没有提供急需的解决方案，反而延长了这场争斗。摆在哥伦比亚特区联邦上诉法院面前的，是联邦通信委员会（FCC）2017年按党派路线投票通过的最新网络中立立场。这份共和党起草的命令不仅废除了FCC在2015年民主党占多数时通过的严格网络中立规则，还否决了该委员会要求宽带供应商做任何事的权力。该命令还宣布，州和地方政府也不能监管宽带供应商。

The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV. Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals' streaming services but not their own.

该委员会辩称，其他机构会防范反竞争行为，比如像AT&T这样提供宽带的集团，以牺牲奈飞和苹果电视为代价偏袒自家的视频流媒体服务。然而，FCC也终止了对那些宽带供应商的调查——这些供应商对竞争对手的流媒体服务设数据上限，却对自己的服务不设限。

On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move. But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that "the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service," and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to "avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism."

周二，上诉法院一致维持了2017年放松宽带供应商监管的命令，援引了最高法院2005年一项支持类似放松监管举措的裁决。但帕特里夏·米利特法官在一份协同意见中正当地指出："这一结果与现代宽带服务的现实脱节"，并表示国会或最高法院可以介入，以"避免让互联网监管陷入技术上的过时状态"。

In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC's attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission's power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order. That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC's abdication.

与此同时，法院驳回了FCC试图阻止所有州级网络中立规则的尝试，但保留了该委员会优先于那些破坏其命令的个别州法的权力。这意味着会有更多像司法部与加州之间那样的争斗——加州在FCC放弃监管后颁布了一项强硬的网络中立法。

The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act. It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.

无休止的法律争斗和FCC内部的反复摇摆，迫切要求国会采取行动。国会需要一劳永逸地授予委员会明确权力，禁止宽带供应商干预其网络上的流量，并制定明确规则保护网络的开放与创新。

Part B · 新题型七选五（41–45）— AI如何帮企业（而非取代员工）

【题目】从A–G中选出5句填入41–45，两个多余选项。文章分五小节：更好的招聘实践 / 更有效的营销 / 帮客户省钱 / 提高准确性 / 保护维护基础设施。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
AI replaces the boring parts of your job. If you're doing research, you can have AI go out and look for relevant sources and information that otherwise you just wouldn't have time for.
人工智能取代你工作中枯燥的部分。如果你在做研究，你可以让人工智能去搜寻相关的资料与信息——否则你根本没时间去找。
B
One accounting firm, EY, uses an AI system that helps review contracts during an audit. This process, along with employees reviewing the contracts, is faster and more accurate.

Before, they might not insure the ones who felt like a high risk or charge them too much, or they would charge them too little and then it would cost the company money.

我们也在为客户提供更优的渠道，而不是靠拿起电话去完成那些超出人力规模的事情。

Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）— 二战后高等教育扩张
46
翻译
Those societies came out of the war with levels of enrollment that had been roughly constant at 3-5% of the relevant age groups during the decades before the war.
这些经历了二战的国家，战前数十年适龄人口的高校入学率一直维持在3%至5%左右。
采分点① come out of the war 走出战争；② enrollment 入学率；③ roughly constant 大致稳定；④ relevant age groups 相关年龄组。

And the demand that rose in those societies for entry to higher education extended to groups and social classes that had not thought of attending a university before the war.
在这些国家里，接受高等教育的需求日益高涨，已扩展到战前从未想过接受大学教育的各个团体以及社会阶层。
采分点① demand that rose 高涨的需求；② entry to higher education 进入高等教育；③ extended to 扩展到；④ 两个定语从句的处理。

In many countries of Western Europe, the numbers of students in higher education doubled within five-year periods during the 1960s and doubled again in seven, eight, or 10 years by the middle of the 1970s.

and when the new staff are predominantly young men and women fresh from postgraduate study, they largely define the norms of academic life in that faculty.
并且当新员工主要是刚毕业的研究生时，他们就在很大程度上确定了该院系学术生活的规范。

High growth rates increased the chances for academic innovation; they also weakened the forms and processes by which teachers and students are admitted into a community of scholars during periods of stability or slow growth.

Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 求职建议邮件

原题指令 Directions

One of your foreign friends has just graduated from college and intends to find a job in China. Write an email to give him/her some advice. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the email. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】你的一位外国朋友刚从大学毕业，打算在中国找工作。写一封电子邮件给他/她提些建议。字数约100词。邮件末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

你的一位外国朋友刚大学毕业，打算在中国找工作。写一封邮件给他/她提些建议。约100词，落款用"Li Ming"。

审题

① 文体：给朋友的建议邮件；② 内容：2-3条具体求职建议（如学汉语、利用校友网络、了解中国职场文化）；③ 语气：友好真诚。

参考范文

Dear Friend,

Congratulations on your graduation! I was thrilled to hear that you plan to pursue your career in China, and I would like to offer some practical advice.

First, if your Chinese is not yet fluent, an intensive language course will greatly broaden your job options. Second, consider leveraging your university's alumni network in cities like Shanghai or Shenzhen, where multinationals and start-ups are most active. Finally, it helps to familiarize yourself with local workplace culture, such as the emphasis on teamwork and personal connections. I would be delighted to introduce you to some of my contacts.

Wish you every success in your job hunt!

Yours, Li Ming

【译文】

亲爱的朋友：

祝贺你毕业！得知你打算在中国发展事业，我十分高兴，想提供一些实用建议。

首先，若你的中文尚不流利，参加强化语言课程将大幅拓宽求职选择。其次，不妨借助校友网络，在上海、深圳等跨国公司与初创企业最活跃的城市寻找机会。最后，了解本地职场文化也有帮助，例如对团队协作与人脉的重视。我很乐意把你引荐给我的一些朋友。

祝你求职一切顺利！

你的，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文《学唱戏》

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The cartoon shows a child in traditional Chinese opera costume saying to his father, "Dad, many classmates think learning opera is no fun." The father replies, "Don't you like it yourself? That's enough."

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 漫画中一个扮成戏曲行当的孩子对爸爸说：“爸爸，好多同学觉得学唱戏不好玩。”父亲回答：“你自己不是喜欢吗？那就足够了。”

图画解读

扮成戏曲行当的孩子对爸爸说："爸爸，好多同学觉得学唱戏不好玩。"父亲回答："你自己不是喜欢吗？那就足够了。"漫画寓意：面对他人不理解，坚持自己真正热爱的事物，不必随波逐流。

审题框架

三段式：①描述父子对话；②点明寓意——听从内心热爱，而非盲从他人评价；③评论：坚守热爱方能有所成就。160-200词。

参考范文

The cartoon depicts a touching dialogue between a father and his son in traditional Chinese opera costume. The child worries that many classmates find learning opera boring, to which the father gently replies, "But don't you love it yourself? That is enough."

The message is both simple and profound: when we are genuinely passionate about something, the judgment of others should not dictate our choices. Too often, young people abandon their true interests simply because peers dismiss them as unfashionable or impractical. Yet it is precisely such devotion to what one loves—not to what others expect—that sustains long-term commitment and eventual mastery. Whether it is a niche art form like Peking opera or any other pursuit, inner conviction matters more than external approval.

From my perspective, we should all learn from the wise father. Rather than hesitating because others disapprove, we should have the courage to follow our own hearts. After all, the life we live is our own, and genuine passion is the best compass we have.

【译文】

漫画描绘了一段感人的父子对话。扮成戏曲行当的孩子对父亲说，很多同学觉得学唱戏不好玩；父亲温柔地回答："你自己不是喜欢吗？那就足够了。"

这个道理朴素而深刻：当我们真正热爱某件事时，他人的评判不应左右我们的选择。太多年轻人仅仅因为同伴认为某爱好不时髦或不实用，就放弃自己真正的兴趣。然而，恰恰是这种对所爱之物的执着——而非对他人的迎合——支撑着长久的投入与最终的精通。无论像京剧这样小众的艺术，还是其他追求，内心的笃定都比外界的认可更重要。

在我看来，我们都应向那位睿智的父亲学习。与其因他人不认同而犹豫，不如勇敢追随自己的内心。毕竟，我们过的是自己的人生，而真诚的热爱是最好的指南针。
