Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读

The idea that plants have some degree of consciousness first took root in the early 2000s; the term "plant neurobiology" was 1 around the notion that some aspects of plant behavior could be 2 to intelligence in animals. 3 plants lack brains, the firing of electrical signals in their stems and leaves nonetheless triggered responses that 4 consciousness, researchers previously reported.

植物具有某种程度意识的观点最早在21世纪初生根发芽；"植物神经生物学"这一术语是围绕这样一种观念创造出来的：植物行为的某些方面可以与动物的智力相提并论。研究人员此前报告称，尽管植物没有大脑，但其茎和叶中电信号的发放仍然引发了暗示意识存在的反应。

But such an idea is bunk, according to the authors of the new article. Plant biology is complex and fascinating, but it 5 so greatly from that of animals that so-called 6 of plants' intelligence is intriguing but inconclusive, the scientists wrote. In animals, neurobiology refers to the biological mechanisms through which a nervous system regulates behavior, according to Harvard University's Mind Brain Behavior Interfaculty Initiative. Over millions of years, brains in diverse animal species have evolved to produce behaviors that experts identify as intelligent: Among them are reasoning and problem-solving, tool use and self-recognition.

但新文章的作者们认为，这种观点是无稽之谈。科学家们写道，植物生物学复杂而迷人，但它与动物生物学差异如此之大，以至于所谓植物智力的证据虽然引人入胜，却并不能令人信服。在动物中，神经生物学指的是神经系统调节行为的生物机制，据哈佛大学心智大脑行为跨院系计划称。数百万年来，不同动物物种的大脑进化出了专家所认定的智力行为：其中包括推理与解决问题、工具使用和自我识别。

Beginning in 2006, some scientists have 7 that plants possess neuron-like cells that interact with hormones and neurotransmitters, 8 "a plant nervous system, 9 to that in animals," said lead study author Lincoln Taiz, a professor emeritus of molecular, cell and developmental biology at the University of California Santa Cruz.

该研究的主要作者、加州大学圣克鲁兹分校分子、细胞与发育生物学荣誉教授林肯·泰兹表示，从2006年开始，一些科学家主张植物拥有类似神经元的细胞，这些细胞与激素和神经递质相互作用，从而形成"一种植物神经系统，与动物的神经系统类似"。

"They 10 claimed that plants have 'brain-like command centers' at their root tips," Taiz told Live Science in an email.

泰兹在一封邮件中告诉《生活科学》："他们甚至声称植物在根尖处有'类似大脑的指挥中心'。"

This 11 makes sense if you simplify the workings of a complex brain, 12 it to an array of electrical pulses; cells in plants also communicate through electrical signals, according to the article. 13, the signaling in a plant is only 14 similar to the billions of synapses firing in a complex animal brain, which is more than "a mass of cells that communicate by electricity," Taiz said.

如果你把复杂大脑的工作方式简化为一系列电脉冲，这种观点就说得通了；文章称，植物细胞也通过电信号进行交流。然而，植物中的信号传导只是表面上类似于复杂动物大脑中数十亿个突触的发放，动物大脑远不止"一团通过电交流的细胞"，泰兹说。

"For consciousness to evolve, a brain with a threshold 15 of complexity and capacity is required," he 16.

他补充道："意识的进化需要一个达到一定复杂程度和容量门槛的大脑。"

Other researchers who recently investigated the neuroscience of consciousness—awareness of one's world and a sense of self—found that in animals, only vertebrates, arthropods and cephalopods had brains complex enough to enable them to be conscious.

其他近期研究意识神经科学（对自身所处世界的觉知和自我感）的研究人员发现，在动物中，只有脊椎动物、节肢动物和头足类动物拥有足够复杂的大脑，能够产生意识。

"If the lower animals—which have nervous systems—lack consciousness, the 17 that plants without nervous systems have consciousness are effectively nil," Taiz said.

泰兹说："如果有神经系统的低等动物都缺乏意识，那么没有神经系统的植物拥有意识的可能性实际上为零。"

And what's so great about consciousness, anyway? Plants can't run away from 18, so investing energy in a body system that 19 a threat and can feel pain would be a very 20 evolutionary strategy, according to the article.

话说回来，意识到底有什么了不起的呢？植物无法逃离危险，因此根据这篇文章，把能量投入一个能够识别威胁并感知疼痛的身体系统，将是一个非常糟糕的进化策略。

动词辨析题
答案 A coined
the term "plant neurobiology" was ___ around the notion that…术语“植物神经生物学”是___围绕着……的概念
[A] coined 创造（新词）
[B] discovered 发现
[C] collected 收集
[D] issued 发布
💡 考场思路主语是 the term"plant neurobiology"（植物神经生物学这一术语），术语是被"创造、杜撰"出来的。coin a term 是固定搭配，意为"创造新术语"。
逐项排除 [B] discovered 发现——术语不是自然界原有的，是新近提出的；
[C] collected 收集——不与 term 搭配；
[D] issued 发布——多指期刊、发行物正式发布，不符合术语被创造的语境。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

People often grumble that plastics are too durable. Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are ubiquitous and don't break down easily. But some plastic materials change over time. They crack and frizzle. They "weep" out additives. They melt into sludge. All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects. The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, David Bowie costumes, the first artificial heart.

人们常常抱怨塑料太耐用了。从珠穆朗玛峰到马里亚纳海沟，水瓶、购物袋和其他垃圾散落地球，因为塑料无处不在且不易分解。但有些塑料材料会随时间变化。它们开裂、卷曲。它们"渗出"添加剂。它们融成污泥。所有这些都给博物馆等试图保护具有重要文化意义物品的机构带来了巨大麻烦。面临风险的塑料制品种类令人眼花缭乱：早期收音机、先锋派雕塑、迪士尼电影的赛璐璐动画剧照、大卫·鲍伊的服装、第一颗人工心脏。

Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn't always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands (RCE). "It's like baking a cake: If you don't have exact amounts, it goes wrong," she says. "The object you make is already a time bomb."

荷兰文化遗产局（RCE）的聚合物化学家西娅·范·奥斯滕（几年前退休）说，某些手工艺品尤其脆弱，因为一些塑料艺术先驱并不总是知道如何正确混合原料。"这就像烤蛋糕：如果用量不精确，就会出错，"她说，"你制作的物品已经是一颗定时炸弹。"

And sometimes, it's not the artist's fault. In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces. Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen "nature carpet" — large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons. He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets — which meant they had to be durable.

而有时，这并非艺术家的错。20世纪60年代，意大利艺术家皮耶罗·吉拉尔迪开始创作数百件色彩鲜艳的泡沫作品。这些作品包括小束玫瑰和其他物品，以及几十块"自然地毯"——用泡沫南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜装饰的大长方形地毯。他希望观众能在地毯上走动——这意味着它们必须耐用。

Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable. It's especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi's pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling. Museums locked some of them away in the dark.

不幸的是，他使用的聚氨酯泡沫本身就不稳定。它尤其容易受到光照损害，到20世纪90年代中期，吉拉尔迪的南瓜、玫瑰和其他造型已经开裂碎裂。博物馆将其中一些锁在暗处。

So van Oosten and colleagues at RCE began to study ways to protect polyurethane. First, they took foam samples similar to the nature carpets and infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals that modern manufacturers often use. Van Oosten calls those chemicals "sunscreens" because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers. Then the team used xenon lamps to artificially age both treated and untreated samples, and examined them under high-powered microscopes. The results were encouraging. Samples that lacked sunscreen had withered under the barrage of photons: The molecular "struts" shoring up the foam were 42% thinner and notably more brittle than before the lamp treatment. The struts in samples with sunscreen decreased by as little as 12.5%. Armed with that knowledge, conservators working with RCE infused several Gilardi sculptures, including two nature carpets, with the sunscreen to stabilize them. Van Oosten is proud that several have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases. Long called the "queen of plastics," in 2012, van Oosten was knighted in the Netherlands for her efforts to preserve plastic objects and spread knowledge to other institutes.

因此，范·奥斯滕和RCE的同事开始研究保护聚氨酯的方法。首先，他们取了与自然地毯相似的泡沫样本，给其中一些注入现代制造商常用的稳定和固结化学物质。范·奥斯滕称这些化学物质为"防晒霜"，因为它们的目标是防止进一步的光照损害并重建磨损的聚合物纤维。然后团队用氙灯对处理过和未处理过的样本进行人工老化，并在高倍显微镜下检查。结果令人鼓舞。缺乏"防晒霜"的样本在光子的轰击下枯萎了：支撑泡沫的分子"支柱"比灯照处理前细了42%，且明显更脆。涂了"防晒霜"的样本中，支柱仅减少了12.5%。掌握这些知识后，与RCE合作的修复人员给几件吉拉尔迪雕塑（包括两块自然地毯）注入"防晒霜"以稳定它们。范·奥斯滕很自豪，其中几件甚至已再次展出，尽管有时放在保护罩下。范·奥斯滕长期被称为"塑料女王"，2012年因其在保护塑料制品和向其他机构传播知识方面的努力而被授予荷兰爵士爵位。

Despite such success stories, preservation of plastics will likely get harder. Old objects continue to deteriorate. Worse, biodegradable plastics, designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.

尽管有这样的成功故事，塑料的保存可能会变得更加困难。旧物品持续恶化。更糟的是，旨在分解的可生物降解塑料正变得越来越普遍。

And more is at stake here than individual objects. Ferreira notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history — Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on — after examining artifacts in museums. We now live in an age of plastic, she says, "and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve…will have a strong impact on how in the future we'll be seen."

这里利害攸关的不仅仅是单个物品。费雷拉指出，考古学家最初是在检查博物馆中的手工艺品之后，才定义了人类历史上的伟大材料时代——石器时代、铁器时代等等。我们现在生活在塑料时代，她说，"而我们今天决定收集什么、决定保存什么……将对未来人们如何看待我们产生强烈影响。"

Text 2   Z世代与大学学位价值（26–30）

As the latest crop of students pen their UCAS form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Gen Z (and their parents) need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.

当最新一批学生填写大学申请表、权衡各种选择时，或许值得思考一下：学位的意义、目的和价值发生了怎样的变化，以及Z世代（及其父母）在开启教育旅程第三阶段时需要考虑什么。

Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued (just as governments hiked up the cost of getting one). Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility. Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles; a percentage which is double the average amongst the OECD.

千禧一代被告知，如果你学业优异、拿到体面的学位，这辈子就有保障了。但这一承诺被证明是欠缺的。随着学位变得普及，它贬值了（正如政府推高了获得学位的成本）。教育不再是可靠的社会流动途径。如今，英国28%的毕业生从事着非毕业生岗位；这一比例是经合组织平均水平的两倍。

This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.

这并不是说拿学位毫无意义，而是要强调学位并不适合所有人，从课堂到阶梯教室的转变并非不可避免，还有其他选择。

Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Gen Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset. Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles—just as Penguin did in 2016.

值得庆幸的是，有迹象表明这已经在发生，Z世代试图从千禧一代前辈那里吸取教训，即使父母和老师往往仍固守学位思维。雇主早就看到了招聘中学毕业生的好处——他们往往比毕业生更敬业、更忠诚。许多雇主也看到了取消某些岗位学位要求的好处——就像企鹅兰登书屋在2016年所做的那样。

For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense (albeit expensive) to have two.

对于那些把学位作为理想途径的人，请考虑这很可能只是众多学位中的第一个。在这个通才时代，拥有特定知识或技能是有回报的。研究生现在比本科生多挣40%。当我们越来越多人都有学位时，拥有两个学位是明智的（尽管昂贵）。

It is unlikely that Gen Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly up-skilling throughout their career to stay agile, relevant and employable. It has been estimated that this generation due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfillment and desire for diversity will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.

Z世代不太可能在18岁或21岁就结束教育；他们需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能，以保持敏捷、与时俱进和可雇佣性。据估计，由于技术压力、对个人成就的渴望和对多样性的追求，这一代人在职业生涯中将为17个不同的雇主工作，经历五种不同的职业。教育——而不仅仅是在校园里获得的知识——将是Z世代职业轨迹的核心部分。

I have often heard older generations talk about their degree (even if it was gained decades ago) in the present and personal tense: "I am a geographer or 'I am a classicist'". Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.

我经常听到老一代人用现在时和个人化的口吻谈论他们的学位（即使是几十年前拿到的）："我是地理学家"或"我是古典学者"。他们的儿女绝不会说这样的话；好像他们已经知道学位不会以同样的方式定义他们。

Text 3   艺术与科学合作（31–35）

Enlightening, stimulating, inspiring, fun. These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experiences of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers. Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.

富有启发、令人振奋、鼓舞人心、有趣。这些是《自然》杂志读者用来描述他们在一系列关于艺术家与研究人员合作的文章中所体验到的艺术与科学合作的词汇。在约350名回复配套民意调查的人中，近40%表示曾与艺术家合作；几乎所有人都表示未来会考虑这样做。

Such an encouraging result is not surprising. Public engagement has become essential to many research projects. Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists and designers to help them to communicate their work to new audiences. "Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning," one respondent said. "The experience is very liberating for me, as a scientist," said another. "There's often a visual aspect to my science that generating and publishing data does not convey."

这样令人鼓舞的结果并不意外。公众参与已成为许多研究项目的必要组成部分。科学家越来越多地寻找视觉艺术家和设计师，帮助他们向新的受众传播自己的工作。"艺术家帮助科学家接触更广泛的受众，并建立促进学习的情感联系，"一位受访者说。"作为一名科学家，这种经历让我非常解放，"另一位说，"我的科学中常常有视觉层面的东西，是生成和发布数据所无法传达的。"

One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the senses came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra in Australia performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season — provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub in Melbourne. The work was entitled The (Uncertain) Four Seasons, and variations of the score containing local data were sent to every major orchestra in the world. The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations.

艺术家与科学家如何共同震撼感官的一个例子发生在上个月，当时澳大利亚悉尼交响乐团演奏了改编版安东尼奥·维瓦尔第的《四季》。他们通过注入墨尔本莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的最新每季气候预测数据，重新诠释了这部有300年历史的乐谱。这部作品名为《（不确定的）四季》，包含当地数据的乐谱变体被发送给世界上每一个主要交响乐团。这场演出是在11月联合国大会之前发出的创造性行动呼吁。

But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street. Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll; however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements. Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study—even if these are reasons why scientists seek opportunities to work with artists. The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work. Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art.

但真正的合作必须是双向的。回复《自然》调查的艺术家比科学家少；然而，几位受访者指出，艺术家不应仅仅帮助科学家满足传播需求。他们的工作也不应只被视为研究对象——即使这些是科学家寻求与艺术家合作机会的原因。当科学家和艺术家在项目中有共同利益、能够共同设计并能相互批评对方的工作时，这种联盟才最有价值。这种方法既能催生新研究，也能产生有感染力的艺术。

More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) in Cambridge to explore the role of technology in culture. The centre was established during the Vietnam War, when many scientists in the United States were being criticized for working on defence contracts. Its founders believed that artists and scientists could, together, create a vision for a more humane world. They deliberately focused their projects around light — hence the 'visual studies' in the name. Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration, says Seth Riskin, a visual-arts researcher at the MIT Museum who previously worked at CAVS.

半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院（MIT）在剑桥开设了高等视觉研究中心（CAVS），探索技术在文化中的作用。该中心成立于越南战争期间，当时美国许多科学家因从事国防合同工作而受到批评。其创始人相信，艺术家和科学家可以共同创造一个更人道世界的愿景。他们刻意将项目聚焦于光——因此名称中有"视觉研究"。光是艺术家和科学家都感兴趣的东西，因此可以成为合作的基础，曾在CAVS工作的MIT博物馆视觉艺术研究员塞斯·里斯金说。

The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other. Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.

艺术与科学合作的范围需要超越研究传播的必要目的，参与者也不能陷入相互刻板印象的陷阱。艺术家和科学家都沉浸在发现与发明之中，挑战与批判对两者同样重要。

Text 4   雇佣关系法与不当解雇（36–40）

The personal grievance provisions of the Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause. Instead, dismissals must be justified. Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way.

2000年《雇佣关系法》（ERA）的个人申诉条款禁止雇主无正当理由解雇员工。相反，解雇必须有正当理由。雇主既必须说明理由，又必须以程序公正的方式行事。

Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from "unjustified dismissals". The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management. Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.

个人申诉程序旨在保护普通工人的工作免受"不当解雇"。其前提是普通合同法缺乏足够保障，使工人免受管理层任意行为的侵害。老板只需简单给员工合同通知就解雇人的日子早已一去不复返。

But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives. As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance. The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure. Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them. Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal.

但这些条款在适用于高薪经理和高管时给企业带来了困难。无数董事会和企业主可以证明，限制公司解雇表现不佳、收入丰厚的经理，就像给提高生产率和整体业绩踩了手刹。C级经理和A级经理之间的差距，很可能就是企业成败的差距。就是保住普通工人工作还是失去它们的差距。然而，平庸已经不足以成为解雇的理由。

Consequently — and paradoxically — laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.

因此——而且矛盾的是——为保护普通工人工作而出台的法律，可能正在将这些工作置于风险之中。

If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing underperforming managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages. Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.

即使不将工作置于风险之中，在就业保护法限制企业主解雇表现不佳经理的范围内，这些法律也会制约企业生产率，从而制约工人工资。事实上，在《新西兰生产率悖论的国际视角》（2014）中，生产力委员会特别指出管理能力低下是该国生产率增长不佳的一个原因。

Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures. Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff. This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment. And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.

高薪经理本身也不能免于ERA不当解雇程序造成的伤害。因为就业保护法增加了解雇员工的成本，雇主在招聘新员工时更加谨慎。这使得边缘经理更难找到工作。而且公司给员工的工资更低，因为公司承担了雇佣安排出错的负担。

Society also suffers from excessive employment protections. Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall wellbeing.

社会也因过度的就业保护而受损。严格的解雇法规对生产率增长产生不利影响，并阻碍繁荣和整体福祉。

Across the Tasman, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws. In New Zealand, a 2016 private members' Bill tried to permit firms and high-income employees to contract out of the unjustified dismissal regime. However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.

隔着塔斯曼海，澳大利亚通过将收入超过特定"高收入门槛"的员工排除在不当解雇法保护之外，来应对这一悖论。在新西兰，2016年一项私人议员法案试图允许公司和高收入员工通过合同退出不当解雇制度。然而，提出的机制难以操作，该法案在当年晚些时候政府换届后被投票否决。

Part B · 新题型观点匹配（41–45）

【题目】阅读关于"反对动物园"文章的五位评论者观点，从A–G中为(41)–(45)匹配观点。两个多余选项。

(41) Teri Byrd：我是兽医，曾在动物园和野生动物公园工作多年。两者都声称以动物福利和保护为目的。这都是假的。它们都是盈利机构，利润比动物状况重要得多。动物园里的非洲狮数量超过饲养能力就被"淘汰"。熊崽、海豹等被用来盈利，没用了就"淘汰"或放生。早就该让这些机构透明化，早该把动物园从我们文化中消灭。

Byrd 核心：动物园唯利是图，应关闭。

(42) Karen R Sime：作为动物学教授和常去动物园的人，我同意Emma Marris说动物园展示悲伤残忍，但她低估了动物园的教育价值。虽然很多游客不读教育牌，但那些真正对保护产生兴趣的人累积起来很多。我州大学校园的动物学项目吸引了很多学生，动物园参观是他们学生物的关键经历。

Sime 核心：动物园在激发年轻人从事相关科学方面作用重大。

(43) Greg Newberry：Emma Marris的文章是对成千上万孜孜不倦改善动物和地球生活的热情工作者的侮辱和伤害。她用过时研究和几十年前的例子破坏组织的崇高使命。动物园和水族馆处于保护前沿，在不断改善对动物的照顾。动物园里的困境动物能得到比我们当地医院大多数人更好的治疗。

Newberry 核心：动物园不遗余力照顾动物，不应受不公批评。

(44) Dean Gallea：作为环保主义者和素食者，我本应和Emma Marris站在一边。但我认为运营良好的动物园和其中忍受圈养的英勇动物确实服务于更高目的。如果没有机会近距离观察这些美丽野生动物，更多人会被驱使去野生地区寻找、打扰甚至猎杀它们。动物园就像自然历史和考古博物馆，满足我们接触这些生物的需求，同时让绝大多数生物在自然环境中不受打扰。

Gallea 核心：动物园省去人们跑荒野，从而有助于野生动物保护。

(45) John Fraser：Emma Marris选择性描述和误读了我们研究的发现。我们研究关注动物园经历如何影响人们对自身和自然的看法，提取的数据绝没有贬低动物园参观中学到的东西。动物园是思考的工具，为来自各种背景的人提供接触动物和自然的机会，提供保护的关键声音。

Fraser 核心：Marris歪曲了我们的发现，研究实际证明动物园是人与自然不可或缺的纽带。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
Zoos which spare no effort to take care of animals should not be subjected to unfair criticism.
不遗余力照料动物的动物园，不应遭受不公正的批评。
B
To pressure zoos to spend less on their animals would lead to inhumane outcomes for the precious creatures in their care.
迫使动物园减少对动物的投入，会给它们所照管的珍贵生灵带来不人道的后果。
C
While animals in captivity deserve sympathy, zoos play a significant role in starting young people down the path of related sciences.
尽管圈养动物值得同情，但动物园在引导年轻人走上相关科学之路上发挥着重要作用。
D
Zoos save people trips to wilderness areas and thus contribute to wildlife conservation.
动物园让人们省去前往荒野的奔波，从而有助于野生动物保护。
E
For wild animals that cannot be returned to their natural habitats, zoos offer the best alternative.
对于无法回归自然栖息地的野生动物，动物园提供了最佳的替代方案。
F
Zoos should have been closed down as they prioritize money making over animals' wellbeing.
动物园早该关闭，因为它们把赚钱置于动物福祉之上。
G
Marris distorts our findings which actually prove that zoos serve as an indispensable link between man and nature.
马里斯歪曲了我们的研究结果——而研究恰恰证明，动物园是人与自然界之间不可或缺的纽带。

Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）
46
翻译
It was also, and this is unknown even to many people well read about the period, a battle between those who made codes and those who broke them.
这场斗争也是一场编写密码者与破译密码者之间的战争，但是这一点甚至对那些熟知这一时期历史的人们来说都是未知的。
采分点① It 指代上一句的 struggle，需明确译出"这场斗争"；② well read about the period 熟知这一时期历史的；③ made codes 编写密码，broke them 破译密码。
47
翻译
It listed many documents in code that had been captured from the French army of Spain, and whose secrets had been revealed by the work of George Scovell, an officer in British headquarters.
这本书的附录中列出了从西班牙的法军那里缴获的许多密码文件，这些文件的秘密由英国总部的一位军官乔治·斯科维尔（George Scovell）揭露了出来。
采分点① It 指代上文的 appendix 附录；② 两个并列定语从句 that had been captured 和 whose secrets had been revealed 分别修饰 documents；③ an officer in British headquarters 是 George Scovell 的同位语。
48
翻译
he could not analyze carefully what this obscure officer may or may not have contributed to that great struggle between nations or indeed tell us anything much about the man himself.
阿曼（Oman）无法仔细分析这位名不见经传的军官对那场国家间的伟大斗争有没有做出贡献，也确实无法告诉我们任何有关此人的更多事情。
采分点① obscure 此处意为"名不见经传的"；② contribute to 对……做出贡献；③ tell us anything much about 告诉我们关于……的很多事情。
49
翻译
There may have been many spies and intelligence officers during the Napoleonic Wars, but it is usually extremely difficult to find the material they actually provided or worked on.
在拿破仑战争时期，也许存在很多间谍和情报官员，但通常难以找到他们实际提供或者破译的情报资料。
采分点① There may have been 也许存在；② during the Napoleonic Wars 在拿破仑战争时期；③ they actually provided or worked on 是省略连词的定语从句修饰 material。
50
翻译
Just as the code breaking has its wider relevance in the struggle for Spain, so his attempts to make his way up the promotion ladder speak volumes about British society.
正如破解密码对于西班牙之战更为重要，斯科维尔加官进爵的尝试也将英国社会形态展现得淋漓尽致。
采分点① Just as…so… 正如……也一样；② make one's way up the promotion ladder 加官进爵；③ speak volumes about 充分说明/淋漓尽致展现。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 邀请信

原题指令 Directions

Write an email to a professor at a British university, inviting him/her to organize a team to participate in the International Innovation Contest to be held at your university. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the email. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】给英国一所大学的教授写一封电子邮件，邀请他/她组建一支队伍，参加在你校举办的国际创新大赛。字数约100词。邮件末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

写一封邮件给一位英国大学教授，邀请他/她组织一支队伍参加在你校举办的国际创新大赛。约100词，落款Li Ming。

审题

① 格式：邮件/邀请信；② 语气：正式礼貌；③ 内容：代表委员会邀请、赛事时间地点、期待回复。

参考范文

Dear Professor Bruce,

On behalf of the International Innovation Contest Committee, I am writing to invite you to organize a team to participate in the upcoming global innovation competition.

The contest will be held in the Hall of the Innovation Center from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. on May 15. The schedule is as follows: an opening ceremony first; then contestants from various countries will present their works revolving around cutting-edge science and technology; finally, awards and certificates will be conferred on the outstanding teams. We believe your participation will bring fresh ideas and inspiring perspectives.

We sincerely hope you and your team can join us. Looking forward to your favorable reply.

Sincerely yours, Li Ming

【译文】

尊敬的布鲁斯教授：

我谨代表国际创新大赛组委会，写信邀请您组织一支队伍参加即将举行的全球创新大赛。

比赛将于5月15日14:00至17:00在创新中心大厅举行。流程如下：首先举行开幕式；随后各国选手将展示围绕前沿科技的作品；最后向优秀团队颁发奖项与证书。我们相信，您的参与将带来新颖的思路与启发性视角。

我们真诚希望您和您的团队能够参加。期待您的佳音。

谨上，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The cartoon shows two students in front of a campus billboard advertising lectures. A girl says, "They're not related to our major, so they won't help." A boy says, "Go and listen; it'll surely do you good."

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 漫画中校园讲座广告牌前，两名学生对话。女生说：“不是我们一个专业的，听了也没有多大用。”男生说：“去听一下，肯定有好处。”

题目

图画：校园讲座广告牌前，两个学生对话。女生说："不是我们一个专业的，听了也没有多大用。"男生说："去听一下，肯定有好处。"要求：简要描述图画、阐释含义、给出评论。160-200词。

审题框架

三段式：①描述图画（两种对待跨专业讲座的态度）；②阐释含义（大学生应广泛涉猎知识而非局限本专业）；③评论（跨学科知识的重要性）。

参考范文

The cartoon captures a familiar campus scene. In front of a billboard advertising various lectures, a girl complains to her friend, "They're not related to our major, so they won't help our study." Her companion replies, "Go and listen; there's bound to be some benefit."

Simple as it is, the picture reflects a prevalent mindset: some students limit themselves strictly to their own discipline and dismiss knowledge from other fields. Yet in an era of rapid change, those with broad horizons and multiple skills adapt far better and prove more competitive. As the saying goes, knowledge is never a burden. Cross-disciplinary learning not only sparks creativity but may also become the very key to solving problems within one's major.

From my perspective, we should cultivate the habit of lifelong, wide-ranging learning. Universities ought to encourage students to explore diverse possibilities, for only by staying hungry for knowledge can we grow into versatile talents.

【译文】

漫画捕捉了一个熟悉的校园场景。在一块满是各类讲座信息的广告牌前，一名女生对同伴抱怨："又不是我们专业的，听了也没多大用。"同伴却答道："去听一下，肯定有好处。"

画面虽简单，却折射出一种普遍心态：一些学生把自己严格局限在本专业之内，轻视其他领域的知识。然而在快速变迁的时代，视野开阔、技能多元的人适应力更强，也更具竞争力。常言道，艺多不压身。跨学科学习不仅激发创造力，更可能成为破解本专业难题的关键。

在我看来，我们应培养终身、广博学习的习惯。大学应鼓励学生探索多样可能，因为唯有保持对知识的饥渴，我们才能成长为复合型人才。

Section I   Use of English · 完形填空逐句精读

Caravanserais were roadside inns that were built along the Silk Road in areas including China, North Africa and the Middle East. They were typically 1 outside the walls of a city or village and were usually funded by governments or 2 patrons.

商队驿站是沿着丝绸之路修建的路边客栈，分布地区包括中国、北非和中东。它们通常位于城市或村庄的城墙外，资金通常由政府或私人捐助者提供。

This word "Caravanserais" is a 3 of the Persian word "karvan", which means a group of travellers or a caravan, and seray, a palace or enclosed building. The Persian caravan was used to 4 groups of people who travelled together across the ancient network for safety reasons, 5 merchants, travellers or pilgrims.

"Caravanserais"一词是波斯语"karvan"（意为一群旅行者或商队）与"seray"（宫殿或围合建筑）的组合。波斯语中的 caravan 一词被用来描述那些出于安全原因结伴穿越古代路网的人群，例如商人、旅行者或朝圣者。

From the 10th century onwards, as merchant and travel routes became more developed, the 6 of the Caravanserais increased and they served as a safe place for people to rest at night. Travellers on the Silk Road 7 the possibility of being attacked by thieves or being 8 to extreme conditions. For this reason, Caravanserais were strategically placed 9 they could be reached in a day's travel time.

从10世纪起，随着商路和旅行路线更加发达，商队驿站的建设增多，它们成为人们夜间休息的安全场所。丝绸之路上的旅行者面临被盗贼袭击或遭受极端天气的风险。因此，商队驿站在战略上被布置在一天行程即可到达的位置。

Caravanserais served as an informal 10 point for the various people who travelled the Silk Road. 11, those structures became important centers for culture 12 and interaction, with travellers sharing their cultures, ideas and beliefs, 13 taking knowledge with them, greatly 14 the development of several civilizations.

商队驿站是丝绸之路上各色旅行者非正式的汇聚点。因此，这些建筑成为文化交流与互动的重要中心，旅行者分享各自的文化、思想和信仰，同时将知识传播到各地，极大地影响了若干文明的发展。

Caravanserais were also an important marketplace for commodities and 15 in the trade of goods along the Silk Road. 16, it was frequently the first stop merchants looking to sell their wares and 17 supplies for their own journeys. It is 18 that around 120000 to 150000 caravanserais were built along the Silk Road, 19 only about 3000 are known to remain today, many of which are in 20.

商队驿站也是商品的重要集市，在丝绸之路货物贸易中发挥了辅助作用。事实上，它往往是商人出售货物和为自己的旅程储备补给的第一站。据推测，丝绸之路沿线曾修建了约12万至15万座商队驿站，然而如今已知仅存约3000座，其中许多已沦为废墟。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

The weather in Texas may have cooled since the recent extreme heat, but the temperature will be high at the State Board of Education meeting in Austin this month as officials debate how climate change is taught in Texas schools.

自从最近的极端高温以来，得克萨斯州的天气可能已经转凉，但本月在奥斯汀举行的州教育委员会会议上气氛将会十分热烈，因为官员们将辩论得州学校应如何教授气候变化内容。

Pat Hardy, who sympathized with views of the energy sector, is resisting the proposed change to science standards for pre-teen pupils. These would emphasise the primacy of human activity in recent climate change and encourage discussion of mitigation measures.

帕特·哈迪同情能源行业的观点，她正抵制对学龄儿童科学课程标准的拟议修改。这些修改将强调人类活动在近期气候变化中的首要作用，并鼓励讨论减缓措施。

Most scientists and experts sharply dispute Hardy's views. "They casually dismiss the career work of scholars and scientists as just another misguided opinion," says Dan Quinn, senior communications strategist at the Texas Freedom Network, a non-profit group that monitors public education. "What millions of Texas kids learn in their public schools is determined too often by the political ideology of partisan board members, rather than facts and sound scholarship."

大多数科学家和专家强烈反对哈迪的观点。"他们随意 dismissing学者和科学家的毕生工作，认为那不过是又一种被误导的观点，"监督公共教育的非营利组织得州自由网络的高级传播策略师丹·奎因说。"数百万得州孩子在公立学校学到的东西，往往是由党派校董成员的政治意识形态决定的，而不是事实和可靠的学术研究。"

Such debate reflects fierce discussion across the US and around the world, as researchers, policymakers, teachers and students step up demands for a greater focus on teaching about the facts of climate change in schools.

这类辩论反映了美国乃至全球范围内的激烈讨论，研究人员、政策制定者、教师和学生都在强烈要求学校更加重视气候变化事实的教学。

A study last year by the National Center for Science Education, a non-profit group of scientists and teachers, looking at how state public schools across the country address climate change in science classes, gave barely half of US states a grade B+ or higher. Among the 10 worst performers were some of the most populous states, including Texas, which was given the lowest grade (F) and has a disproportionate influence because its textbooks are widely sold elsewhere.

去年，由科学家和教师组成的非营利组织国家科学教育中心进行了一项研究，考察全美各州公立学校在科学课中如何处理气候变化内容，结果仅有不到一半的州获得B+或更高评级。在表现最差的10个州中，包括一些人口最多的州，其中得州获得最低评级（F），但其教材在其他地区广泛销售，因此影响力远超其本身。

Glenn Branch, the centre's deputy director, cautions that setting state-level science standards is only one limited benchmark in a country that decentralises decisions to local school boards. Even if a state is considered a high performer in its science standards, "that does not mean it will be taught", he says.

该中心副主任格伦·布赖恩提醒说，在一个将决策权下放给地方校董会的国家，制定州级科学标准只是一个有限的基准。即使一个州被认为在科学标准方面表现优异，"那也不意味着它就会被教授"，他说。

Another issue is that while climate change is well integrated into some subjects and at some ages — such as earth and space sciences in high schools — it is not as well represented in curricula for younger children and in subjects that are more widely taught, such as biology and chemistry. It is also less prominent in many social studies courses.

另一个问题是，虽然气候变化在某些学科和年龄段（如高中的地球与空间科学）中得到了很好的融入，但在低龄儿童课程以及生物、化学等更广泛教授的学科中，体现得并不充分。它在许多社会研究课程中也不那么突出。

Branch points out that, even if a growing number of official guidelines and textbooks reflect scientific consensus on climate change, unofficial educational materials that convey more slanted perspectives are being distributed to teachers. They include materials sponsored by libertarian think-tanks and energy industry associations.

布赖恩指出，即使越来越多的官方指南和教科书反映了关于气候变化的科学共识，传达更偏激观点的非官方教材正在被分发给教师。其中包括由自由意志主义智库和能源行业协会赞助的材料。

21

Text 2   短租民宿监管（26–30）

Communities throughout the region have been attempting to regulate short-term rentals since sites like Airbnb took off in the 2010s. Now, with record-high home prices and historically low inventory, there's an increased urgency in such regulation, particularly among those who worry that developers will come in and buy up swaths of housing to flip for a fortune on the short-term rental market.

自Airbnb等网站在2010年代兴起以来，整个地区的社区一直试图监管短租。如今，随着房价创历史新高、库存处于历史低位，这种监管的紧迫性增加了，尤其是在那些担心开发商会大量购房、然后在短租市场上高价倒卖的人当中。

In New Hampshire, where the rental vacancy rate has dropped below 1 percent, housing advocates fear unchecked short-term rentals will put further pressure on an already strained market. The state Legislature recently voted against a bill that would've made it illegal for towns to create legislation restricting short-term rentals.

在新罕布什尔州，租金空置率已降至1%以下，住房倡导者担心不受约束的短租会给本已紧张的市场带来进一步压力。州议会最近投票否决了一项法案，该法案本会将各镇立法限制短租定为非法。

"We are at a crisis level on the supply of rental housing, so anytime you're taking the tool out of the toolkit for communities to address this, you're potentially taking supply off the market that's already incredibly stressed," said Nick Taylor, executive director of the Workforce Housing Coalition of the Greater Seacoast. Without enough affordable housing in southern New Hampshire towns, "employers are having a hard time attracting employees, and workers are having a hard time finding a place to live," Taylor said.

"我们在租赁住房供应方面已处于危机水平，所以任何时候你把社区解决这个问题的工具从工具箱里拿走，你都可能正在从已经极度紧张的市场中抽走供应，"大海岸劳动力住房联盟执行主任尼克·泰勒说。新罕布什尔州南部城镇没有足够的可负担住房，"雇主很难吸引员工，工人也很难找到住处，"泰勒说。

However, short-term rentals also provide housing for tourists, a crucial part of the economies in places like Nantucket, Cape Cod, or the towns that make up New Hampshire's Seacoast and Lakes Region, pointed out Ryan Castle, CEO of the Cape Cod & Islands Association of Realtors. "A lot of workers are servicing the tourist industry, and the tourism industry is serviced by those people coming in short term," Castle said, "and so it's a cyclical effect."

然而，短租也为游客提供了住宿，而旅游业是楠塔基特、科德角或新罕布什尔州海岸和湖区城镇等地经济的重要组成部分，科德角和岛屿房地产经纪人协会首席执行官瑞安·卡斯尔指出。"很多工人在为旅游业服务，而旅游业又由那些短期来的人服务，"卡斯尔说，"所以这是一个循环效应。"

Short-term rentals themselves are not the crux of the issue, said Keren Horn, an affordable housing policy expert at the University of Massachusetts Boston. "I think individuals being able to rent out their second home as a good thing. If it's their vacation home anyway, and it's just empty, why can't you make money off it?" Horn said. Issues arise, however, when developers attempt to create large-scale short-term rental facilities — de facto hotels — to bypass taxes and regulations. "I think the question is, shouldn't a developer who's really building a hotel, but disguising it as not a hotel, be treated and taxed and regulated like a hotel?" Horn said.

麻省大学波士顿分校可负担住房政策专家凯伦·霍恩说，短租本身并不是问题的关键。"我认为个人能够出租第二套房是件好事。如果反正就是度假屋，而且空着，为什么不能靠它赚钱呢？"霍恩说。然而，当开发商试图创建大规模短租设施——实际上的酒店——以逃避税收和监管时，问题就来了。"我认为问题在于，一个实际上在建酒店却伪装成不是酒店的开发商，难道不应该像酒店一样被对待、征税和监管吗？"霍恩说。

At the end of 2018, Governor Charlie Baker signed a bill to rein in those potential investor-buyers. "The bill requires every rental host to register with the state, mandates they carry insurance, and opens the potential for local taxes on top of a new state levy," the Globe reported. Boston took things even further, limiting who is authorized to rent out their home, and requiring renters to register with the city's Inspectional Services Department.

2018年底，州长查理·贝克签署了一项法案来约束这些潜在的投资者买家。"该法案要求每一位出租房东在州里注册，强制他们购买保险，并开启了在新的州税之上征收地方税的可能，"《环球报》报道。波士顿走得更远，限制谁有权出租房屋，并要求租客向城市检查服务部门注册。

Horn said similar registration requirements could benefit other struggling cities and towns. The only way to solve the issue, however, is by creating more housing. "If we want to make a change in the housing market, the main one is we have to build a lot more."

霍恩说，类似的注册要求可能会让其他陷入困境的城镇受益。然而，解决这个问题的唯一方法是建造更多住房。"如果我们想改变住房市场，主要方法就是我们必须建造更多。"

Text 3   水石书店与企鹅兰登之争（31–35）

If you're heading for your nearest branch of Waterstones in search of the Duchess of Sussex's new children's book The Bench, you might have to be prepared to hunt around a bit; the same may be true of The President's Daughter, the new thriller by Bill Clinton and James Patterson. Both of these books are published next week by Penguin Random House, a company currently involved in a stand-off with Waterstones.

如果你去最近的水石书店分店寻找苏塞克斯公爵夫人的新书《长椅》，你可能得做好翻找一番的准备；比尔·克林顿和詹姆斯·帕特森的新惊悚小说《总统的女儿》可能也是如此。这两本书都由企鹅兰登书屋于下周出版，而该公司目前正与水石书店陷入对峙。

The problem began late last year, when Penguin Random House confirmed that it had introduced a credit limit with Waterstones "at a very significant level". The trade magazine The Bookseller reported that Waterstones branch managers were being told to remove PRH books from prominent areas such as tables, display spaces and windows, and were "quietly retiring them to their relevant sections".

问题始于去年年底，当时企鹅兰登书屋证实已对水石书店实施了"非常高水平"的信用额度限制。行业杂志《书商》报道称，水石书店分店经理被告知将PRH的书从桌子、展示区和橱窗等显眼位置移走，并"悄悄把它们退到相应区域"。

PRH declined to comment on the issue, but a spokesperson for Waterstones told me: "Waterstones are currently operating with reduced credit terms from PRH, the only publisher in the UK to place any limitations on our ability to trade. We are not boycotting PRH titles but we are doing our utmost to ensure that availability for customers remains good despite the lower overall levels of stock. We do this generally by giving their titles less prominent positioning within our bookshops." "We are hopeful with our shops now open again that normality will return and that we will be allowed to buy appropriately. Certainly, our shops are exceptionally busy and book sales are very strong. The sales for our May Books of the Month surpassed any month since 2018."

PRH拒绝对此置评，但水石书店发言人告诉我："水石书店目前正以PRH降低的信用条款运营，PRH是英国唯一对我们交易能力设置限制的出版商。我们并非抵制PRH的书，但我们正在尽最大努力确保尽管整体库存水平较低，顾客仍然能买到。我们通常通过在书店内给它们的书不那么显眼的位置来做到这一点。""我们希望随着门店重新开业，一切恢复正常，我们能被允许适当采购。当然，我们的门店异常繁忙，图书销售非常强劲。我们五月选书的销量超过了2018年以来的任何一个月。"

In the meantime, PRH authors have been the losers – as have customers, who might expect the new titles from the country's biggest publisher to be prominently displayed by its biggest book retailer. Big-name PRH authors may suffer a bit, but it's those mid-list authors, who normally rely on Waterstones staff's passion for promoting books by lesser-known writers, who will be praying for an end to the dispute.

与此同时，PRH的作者成了输家——顾客也是，他们可能期望这个国家最大出版商的新书能在最大图书零售商处得到显著展示。PRH的大牌作者可能受点影响，但真正指望水石书店员工热情推广不知名作家作品的中间书目作者，才会祈祷争端早日结束。

It comes at a time when authors are already worried about the consequences of the proposed merger between PRH and another big publisher, Simon & Schuster – the reduction in the number of unaligned UK publishers is likely to lead to fewer bidding wars, lower advances, and more conformity in terms of what is published. And one wonders if PRH would have been confident enough to deal with Waterstones in the way it has if it weren't quite such a big company (it was formed with the merger of Penguin and Random House in 2013) and likely to get bigger.

此时作家们已经在担心PRH与另一家大出版商西蒙与舒斯特拟议合并的后果——英国独立出版商数量减少可能导致竞价战减少、预付金降低、出版内容更加趋同。人们不禁要问，如果PRH不是一家如此大的公司（2013年由企鹅兰登书屋合并而成）而且可能更大，它是否还会有信心这样对待水石书店。

"This is all part of a wider change towards concentration of power and cartels. Literary agencies are getting bigger to have the clout to negotiate better terms with publishers, publishers consolidating to deal with Amazon," says Lownie. "The publishing industry talks about diversity in terms of authors and staff but it also needs a plurality of ways of delivering intellectual contact, choice and different voices. After all, many of the most interesting books in recent years have come from small publishers."

"这是权力集中和卡特尔化这一更广泛变革的一部分。文学机构正在变得更大，以便有实力与出版商谈更好的条件，出版商则在整合以应对亚马逊，"洛尼说。"出版业谈论作者和员工的多样性，但它也需要多种传递思想接触、选择和不同声音的方式。毕竟，近年来许多最有趣的书都来自小出版商。"

We shall see whether that plurality is a casualty of the current need among publishers to be big enough to take on all-comers.

我们将看看这种多样性是否会成为当前出版商追求大到足以应对所有来者这一需求的牺牲品。

Text 4   论文引用操纵（36–40）

Scientific papers are the recordkeepers of progress in research. Each year researchers publish millions of papers in more than 30,000 journals. The scientific community measures the quality of those papers in a number of ways, including the perceived quality of the journal (as reflected by the title's impact factor) and the number of citations a specific paper accumulates. The careers of scientists and the reputation of their institutions depend on the number and prestige of the papers they produce, but even more so on the citations attracted by these papers.

科学论文是研究进展的记录者。每年研究人员在3万多种期刊上发表数百万篇论文。科学界以多种方式衡量这些论文的质量，包括期刊的感知质量（体现在期刊的影响因子上）以及特定论文积累的引用次数。科学家的职业和机构的声誉取决于他们发表论文的数量和声望，但更取决于这些论文吸引的引用。

In recent years, there have been several episodes of scientific fraud, including completely made-up data, massaged or doctored figures, multiple publications of the same data, theft of complete articles, plagiarism of another's work, and self-plagiarism. And some scientists have come up with another way to artificially boost the number of citations to their work.

近年来，发生了几起科学欺诈事件，包括完全编造数据、篡改数字、同一数据多次发表、整篇文章盗窃、抄袭他人作品和自我抄袭。一些科学家还想出了另一种人为增加其作品引用次数的方法。

Citation cartels, where journals, authors, and institutions conspire to inflate citation numbers, have existed for a long time. In 2016, researchers developed an algorithm to recognize suspicious citation patterns, including groups of authors that disproportionately cite one another and groups of journals that cite each other frequently to increase the impact factors of their publications. Recently, I came across yet another expression of this so-called support behavior: so-called support service consultancies that provide language and other editorial support to individual authors and to journals sometimes advise contributors to add a number of citations to their articles and the articles of colleagues. Some of these consultancies are also active in organizing conferences and can advise that citations be added to conference proceedings. In this manner, a single editor can drive hundreds of citations in the direction of his own articles or those of colleagues that may be in his circle.

引用卡特尔——期刊、作者和机构合谋虚增引用次数——已经存在很长时间了。2016年，研究人员开发了一种算法来识别可疑引用模式，包括不成比例地互相引用的作者群体，以及频繁互相引用以提高其出版物影响因子的期刊群体。最近，我又发现了这种所谓支持行为的另一种表现：为个人作者和期刊提供语言和其他编辑支持的所谓支持服务咨询公司，有时会建议投稿者在自己的文章和同事的文章中添加大量引用。其中一些咨询公司还积极组织会议，并可能建议在会议论文集中添加引用。通过这种方式，一个编辑就能将数百次引用引导到自己的文章或其圈子中同事的文章上。

How insidious is this type of citation manipulation? In one example, an individual—acting as author, editor, and consultant—was able to use at least 15 journals as citation providers to articles published by five scientists at three universities. The problem is rampant in Scopus, which includes a high number of new "international" journals. In fact, a listing in Scopus seems to be a criterion to be targeted in this type of citation manipulation.

这种引用操纵有多隐蔽？在一个例子中，一个人——同时扮演作者、编辑和顾问——能够利用至少15种期刊为三所大学五位科学家发表的文章提供引用。这个问题在Scopus中尤为猖獗，因为它收录了大量新兴"国际"期刊。事实上，被Scopus收录似乎就成了这种引用操纵的目标标准。

36
细节题
答案 B
According to Paragraph 1, the careers of scientists can be determined by ___.根据第1款，科学家的职业生涯可以由___决定。
[A] how many citations their works contain其作品包含多少引用
[B] how many times their papers are cited
[C] the prestige of the people they work with他们所共事之人的声望
[D] the status they have in scientific circles他们在科学界的地位
💡 考场思路第一段末："The careers of scientists... depend on... the citations attracted by these papers"——论文被引用的次数。注意区别：citations their works contain（自己文章里引用了别人多少次）vs citations attracted（自己文章被别人引用了多少次）。
逐项分析 [A] 自己作品包含多少引用 → 偷换，是被引用；
[B] 论文被引用多少次 → 正确；
[C] 合作者声望 → 未提及；
[D] 科学界地位 → 是结果不是决定因素。
核心词汇
impact factor 影响因子
citation n. 引用
fraud n. 欺诈
plagiarism n. 抄袭
cartel n. 卡特尔/垄断联盟
insidious adj. 隐蔽的
37
细节题
答案 C
The support service consultancies tend to ___.支持服务咨询公司倾向于___。
[A] recommended journals to their clients向客户推荐期刊
[B] list citation patterns for their clients为客户列出引文模式
[C] ask authors to include extra citation
[D] advise contributors to cite each other建议投稿者互相引用
💡 考场思路第三段：咨询公司"advise contributors to add a number of citations to their articles"——建议作者在文章中添加额外引用。
38
细节题
答案 A
The function of the milk cow journals is to ___.奶牛期刊的功能是___。
[A] boost citation counts for certain authors
[B] help scholars publish articles at low cost帮助学者低成本发表文章
[C] instruct first time contributors指导首次投稿者
[D] increase the readership of new journals增加新期刊的读者群
💡 考场思路"奶牛期刊"(milk cow journals)即第三段中互相引用的期刊群体，功能是为特定作者虚增引用次数。
39
细节题
答案 B
What can be learned about Scopus from the last two paragraph?从最后两段中可以学到什么关于Scopus的信息？
[A] It fosters competition among citation providers它促进了引文提供方之间的竞争
[B] It has the capability to identify suspicious citation
[C] It hinders the growth of international journals它阻碍了国际期刊的发展
[D] It is established to prevent citation manipulation它的设立是为了防止引用操纵
💡 考场思路第三段提到2016年开发了算法识别可疑引用模式，末段说Scopus收录大量新国际期刊、问题猖獗——反向推断Scopus有能力识别可疑引用（否则不会成为目标标准）。
40
推断题
答案 D
What should an author do to deal with citation manipulation?作者应该如何处理引文操纵？
[A] Take legal action采取法律行动
[B] Demand an apology要求道歉
[C] Seek professional advice寻求专业建议
[D] Reveal their misconduct

Part B · 新题型排序题（41–45）

【题目】将以下段落重新排序组成连贯文章。A、E、H三段已固定给出。请从A–G中为(41)–(45)选出正确顺序。

[A]（已给出）去年是著名风景摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊拍摄黄石系列照片150周年。他拍摄了大提顿山脉、老忠实泉和科罗拉多落基山脉等标志性地标的首批照片。

[E]（已给出）旅程于1871年6月8日在犹他州奥格登正式开始。近四个月里，几十人骑马前往蒙大拿，沿黄石河行进，最终到达黄石湖周围。那年秋天，他们在怀俄明州本特堡完成了勘测。

[H]（已给出）也许最重要的是，这些照片提供了后来送达政府官员的文献证据。勘测结束几周后，海登将团队的观察整理成一份详尽报告，旨在说服参议员和众议员以及内政部等政府机构的同事，黄石应该被保护。

正确顺序：A → 41(B) → 42(F) → 43(D) → E → 44(C) → 45(G) → H

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–H
A
Last year marks the 150th anniversary of a series of Yellowstone photographs by the renowned landscape photographer William Henry Jackson. He captured the first-ever shots of iconic landmarks such as the Tetons, Old Faithful and the Colorado Rockies, on a late 19th-century expedition through the Yellowstone Basin that was conducted by the head of the U.S. Geological and Geographical Survey of the Territories, Ferdinand V. Hayden. The team included a meteorologist, a zoologist, a mineralogist, and an agricultural statistician.
去年是著名风景摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊拍摄黄石系列照片150周年。在19世纪末由领地地质与地理调查局负责人费迪南德·V·海登率领的远征中，杰克逊穿越黄石盆地，拍下了大提顿山脉、老忠实泉和科罗拉多落基山脉等地标性景观的首批照片。团队中还包括一位气象学家、动物学家、矿物学家和农业统计学家。
B
Two centuries ago, the idea of preserving nature, rather than exploiting it, was a novel one to many U.S. settlers. One of the turning points in public support for land conservation efforts—and recognizing the magnificence of the Yellowstone region in particular—came in the form of vivid photographs.
两个世纪前，"保护自然而非开发自然"对许多美国定居者而言还是个新鲜念头。公众转而支持土地保护努力——尤其是认识到黄石地区的壮美——其转折点之一，正是以生动照片的形式到来的。
C
As an effective Washington operator, Hayden sensed that he could capitalize on the expedition's stunning visuals. He asked Jackson to print out large copies and distributed them, along with reproductions of Moran's paintings, to each member of Congress. "The visualization, particularly those photographs, really hit home that this is something that has to be protected," says Murphy.
作为一名精明的华盛顿操盘手，海登意识到他可以借远征那些震撼的影像大做文章。他让杰克逊冲印大幅照片，连同莫兰画作的复制品，分发给每一位国会议员。墨菲说："这些可视化影像，尤其是那些照片，真正让人意识到这是必须加以保护的东西。"
D
Through the trip, Jackson juggled multiple cameras and plate sizes using the "collodion process" that required him to coat the plates with a chemical mixture, then expose them and develop the resulting images with a portable darkroom. The crude technique required educated guesses on exposure times, and involved heavy, awkward equipment—several men had to assist in its transportation. Despite these challenges, Jackson captured dozens of striking photos, ranging from majestic images like his now-famous snapshot of Old Faithful, to casual portraits of expedition members at the camp.
在整个行程中，杰克逊用"火棉胶法"摆弄多台相机与多种底片尺寸——他须将底片涂上化学混合液，再曝光，并用便携暗房冲洗成像。这种原始技术需要对曝光时间作出有根据的猜测，且涉及笨重不便的设备——得好几个人帮忙搬运。尽管困难重重，杰克逊仍拍下数十张引人注目的照片，既有如如今闻名遐迩的老忠实泉那样的壮丽影像，也有营地里远征队员的随意肖像。
E
The journey officially began in Ogden, Utah, on June 8, 1871. Over nearly four months, dozens of men made their way on horseback into Montana and traversed along the Yellowstone River and around Yellowstone Lake. That fall, they concluded the survey in Fort Bridger, Wyoming.
远征于1871年6月8日在犹他州奥格登正式启程。在将近四个月里，数十人骑马进入蒙大拿，沿黄石河行进并绕黄石湖一周。那年秋天，他们在怀俄明州的布里杰堡结束了勘测。
F
Though Native Americans (and later miners and fur trappers) had long recognized the area's riches, most Americans did not. That's why Hayden's expedition aimed to produce a fuller understanding of the Yellowstone River region, from its hot springs and waterfalls to its variety of flora and fauna. In addition to the entourage of scientists, the team also included artists: Painter Thomas Moran and photographer William Henry Jackson were charged with capturing this astounding natural beauty and sharing it with the world.
尽管美洲原住民（以及后来的矿工和毛皮捕猎者）早就认识到这片地区的富饶，大多数美国人却并未察觉。正因如此，海登的远征旨在让人更全面地认识黄石河地区——从温泉、瀑布到多样的动植物。除了一队科学家，团队还包括艺术家：画家托马斯·莫兰与摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊，受命捕捉这令人惊叹的自然之美并与世界分享。
G
The bill proved largely popular and sailed through Congress with large majorities in favor. In quick succession, the Senate and House passed legislation protecting Yellowstone in early 1872. That March, President Ulysses S. Grant signed an act into law that established Yellowstone as the world's first national park. While some locals opposed to the designation, the decision was largely accepted—and Jackson's photos played a key role in the fight to protect the area. "I don't believe that the legal protection would have happened in the timeframe that it did without those images." says Heather Hansen, journalist and author of Prophets and Moguls, Rangers and Rogues, Bison and Bears: 100 Years of the National Park Service.
该法案总体颇受欢迎，以压倒性多数在国会顺利通过。紧接着，参众两院于1872年初通过了保护黄石的立法。当年3月，尤利西斯·S·格兰特总统签署法案，将黄石确立为世界上第一个国家公园。尽管一些地方人士反对这一认定，该决定总体上被接受——而杰克逊的照片在保护该地区的斗争中发挥了关键作用。记者兼《先知与大亨、游侠与恶棍、野牛与熊：国家公园管理局百年史》一书的作者希瑟·汉森说："我相信，若没有那些影像，法律保护绝不会在那样的时间框架内实现。"
H
Perhaps most importantly, the images provided documentary evidence of the park's sights that later made its way to government officials. Weeks after completing the expedition, Hayden collected his team's observations into an extensive report aimed at convincing senators and representatives, along with colleagues at government agencies like the Department of Interior, that Yellowstone ought to be preserved.
或许最重要的是，这些影像提供了公园景致的文献证据，后来送达政府官员手中。完成远征几周后，海登将团队的观察整理成一份详尽的报告，旨在说服参议员、众议员，以及内政部等政府机构的同僚：黄石应当被保护。
41
排序题
答案 B
排序依据[B] 两个世纪前，保护自然而非开发自然对许多美国定居者来说还是新鲜事。公众支持土地保护的转折点之一——尤其是认识到黄石地区的壮丽——来自生动的照片。→ 紧接A段（杰克逊拍黄石照片150周年），引入背景：当时人们不认为要保护自然，正是照片改变了这一点。
42
排序题
答案 F
排序依据[F] 尽管原住民（以及后来的矿工和皮毛猎人）早就认识到该地区的宝藏，大多数美国人却不知道。这就是为什么海登的远征旨在全面了解黄石河地区。除了科学家随行团队，还包括艺术家：画家托马斯·莫兰和摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊负责捕捉这令人惊叹的自然之美并与世界分享。→ 承接B段"照片推动保护"，引出海登远征及其团队（含杰克逊），为E段旅程开始做铺垫。
43
排序题
答案 D
排序依据[D] 尽管原住民（以及后来的矿工和皮毛猎人）早就认识到该地区的宝藏，大多数美国人却不知道。这就是为什么海登的远征旨在全面了解黄石河地区……（与F段内容呼应，进一步补充远征目的和团队构成）→ 在E段（旅程开始）之前，最后交代远征的人员构成。
44
排序题
答案 C
排序依据[C] 作为华盛顿有效的操盘手，海登意识到他可以利用远征的震撼视觉素材。他让杰克逊打印大尺寸照片，连同莫兰画作的复制品，分发给每位国会议员。"视觉化，特别是那些照片，真正让大家意识到这是需要保护的东西，"墨菲说。→ E段旅程结束后，海登开始利用照片游说国会，逻辑顺承。
45
排序题
答案 G
排序依据[G] 该法案大受欢迎，在国会以压倒性多数通过。紧接着，参议院和众议院都在1872年初通过了保护黄石的立法。3月，尤利西斯·S·格兰特总统签署成为法律，建立了世界上第一个国家公园。→ 紧接C段游说国会，法案通过、总统签署，最后由H段总结照片的作用。
干扰项本题为排序题，需利用首尾句衔接和时间线（1871远征→1872立法→150周年回顾）判断。

Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 通知

原题指令 Directions

Write a notice to recruit a student for Professor Smith's research project on campus sports. The notice should specify the duties and requirements of the job. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the notice. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】写一则通知，为史密斯教授关于校园体育活动的研究项目招募一名学生。通知应明确该工作的职责与要求。字数约100词。通知末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

写一则通知，为史密斯教授关于校园体育活动的研究项目招募一名学生。明确该工作的职责和要求。约100词，落款Li Ming。

审题

① 格式：通知(Notice)；② 内容：招募目的、职责（收集分析数据、组织会议、独立处理问题）、要求（有组织、热情、耐心、沟通能力强）、截止日期和联系方式。

参考范文

Notice

December 24, 2022

The Students' Union is recruiting a student assistant for Professor Smith's research project on campus sports activities. This notice specifies the duties and requirements of the position.

The main duty is to collect and analyze data on campus sports activities. In addition, you will help organize daily meetings with Professor Smith and other members, and handle related problems independently. The ideal candidate should be highly organized, enthusiastic and patient, with strong communication skills.

The application deadline is January 31, 2023. For questions or assistance, please call 1234567 or email sports@univ.edu.cn.

Li Ming

【译文】

通知

2022年12月24日

学生会将为史密斯教授关于校园体育活动的研究项目招募一名学生助理。本通知说明该职位的职责与要求。

主要职责是收集并分析校园体育活动的相关数据。此外，你需协助组织与史密斯教授及其他成员的日常会议，并独立处理相关事务。理想人选应极具条理性、热情且有耐心，并具备较强的沟通能力。

报名截止日期为2023年1月31日。如有疑问或需帮助，请致电1234567或发邮件至sports@univ.edu.cn。

李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图画作文

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The drawing shows a bridge crowded with villagers watching a dragon-boat race on the river. Two old men stand on the bank; one says, "How wonderful! The dragon-boat race in our village is getting livelier and livelier."

【译文】根据下面的图画写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述图画；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 图画中一座桥上挤满了观看龙舟赛的村民，河中龙舟竞渡；两位老人站在岸边，其中一位说：“真好呀，咱们村的龙舟比赛越来越热闹了。”

题目

图画：一座桥上挤满了观看龙舟赛的人群，河中龙舟竞渡，两位老人站在岸边，其中一位说："真好呀，咱们村的龙舟比赛越来越热闹了。"要求：简要描述图画、阐释含义、给出评论。160-200词。

审题框架

三段式：①描述图画（农村龙舟赛越来越热闹）；②阐释含义（传统文化复兴/乡村振兴/传统节日焕发新生）；③评论（保护传统文化、文化自信）。

参考范文

As is vividly depicted, a crowd of villagers gathers on an arched bridge to watch an exciting dragon-boat race, while two elderly men stand by the riverbank. One remarks with a delighted smile, "How wonderful! The dragon-boat race in our village is livelier than ever."

The drawing conveys a thought-provoking message: traditional Chinese culture is experiencing a remarkable revival in rural areas. Dragon-boat racing, rooted in the Dragon Boat Festival and the memory of the ancient poet Qu Yuan, once faded in many villages. Yet in recent years such events have regained their appeal. On the one hand, the government's rural revitalization and cultural-confidence campaigns have provided funding and guidance; on the other, villagers have come to see traditional festivals not as outdated customs but as precious heritage that strengthens community bonds.

From my perspective, this trend is both encouraging and meaningful. To keep our traditions alive, we should not only hold festive events but also invite the young to participate and innovate. Only in this way can our cultural roots stay vibrant for generations to come.

【译文】

如生动描绘所示，一群村民聚集在拱桥上观看热闹的龙舟竞渡，两位老人站在岸边。其中一位面带欣喜地感叹："真好呀，咱们村的龙舟比赛越来越热闹了。"

这幅画传达了发人深省的道理：中国传统文化正在乡村迎来显著的复兴。龙舟赛根植于端午节与对古代诗人屈原的纪念，曾在许多村庄式微；然而近年来这类活动重焕生机。一方面，政府的乡村振兴与文化自信举措提供了资金与引导；另一方面，村民也逐渐认识到传统节日并非过时习俗，而是能凝聚社区、巩固认同的珍贵遗产。

在我看来，这一趋势既令人鼓舞又意义深远。要让传统生生不息，我们不仅要办节庆，更要吸引年轻人参与并创新。唯其如此，文化之根才能代代鲜活。

逻辑关系题
答案 D Without
___ the need to be touched to open or close, automatic doors are essential…___需要触摸才能打开或关闭，自动门是必不可少的……
[A] Through 通过
[B] Despite 尽管
[C] Besides 此外
[D] Without 不需要
💡 考场思路看到 automatic doors 这个词，第一反应是"自动=不用手碰"。空格后 the need to be touched（被触碰的需求），自动门之所以叫自动门，就是因为它"不需要"被触碰。这是对自动门基本定义的考查。
逐项排除 [A] Through the need…"通过需要被触碰"——语义不通，自动门不是通过触碰来工作的；
[B] Despite the need…"尽管需要被触碰"——这与自动门特性完全相反；
[C] Besides the need…"除了需要被触碰之外还……"——暗示自动门也需要触碰，错；
[D] Without the need…"不需要被触碰"——完美对应 automatic 的定义。
语法点睛逗号前面是介词短语作状语，主句是 automatic doors are essential…。Without 引导的介词短语表"没有……的情况下"，是完形常考的逻辑开头。

Reading Part A · Text 1 逐句精读

Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of them. The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.

大约两千年前，当罗马人开始从苏格兰撤离时，他们留下了一件奇特的宝藏：10吨铁钉，将近一百万枚。这批铁钉窖藏于1960年被发现，埋在一个四米深、上面覆盖两米砾石的坑中。

Why had the Romans buried a million nails? The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron. The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.

罗马人为什么要埋下一百万枚铁钉？最可能的解释是撤退仓促，他们不想让当地喀里多尼亚人拿到这十吨武器级铁。罗马人把铁钉埋得如此之深，以至于近两千年都未被发现。

Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith's labour in a nail even more than the raw material. As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate. This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes. The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.

后来的文明社会甚至更看重一枚铁钉中熟练铁匠的劳动，而非原材料本身。正如罗马·阿格拉瓦尔在其新著《螺母与螺栓》中所解释的那样，17世纪初的弗吉尼亚人如果打算搬家，有时会烧掉自己的房子。这是为了回收宝贵的铁钉——筛完灰烬后还能再用。一个人居然会为了回收铁钉而烧掉整栋房子，这足以说明当时这种看似简单的技术是多么稀缺、昂贵和宝贵。

The price of nails fell by 90 per cent between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper. According to Sichel, although the falling price was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.

正如经济学家丹尼尔·西舍尔在一篇研究论文中指出的，从18世纪末到20世纪中叶，铁钉价格下跌了90%。据西舍尔所说，虽然价格下跌部分是由于更便宜的铁和能源，但主要功劳在于铁钉制造商找到了更高效的把钢变成钉子的方法。

Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven't changed much. Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails. It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of nails since 1695, but to ask the question of nails makes perfect sense.

铁钉本身这些年也有变化，但西舍尔研究它们是因为它们变化不大。罗马的灯和战车与LED灯条和跑车截然不同，但罗马的铁钉至今仍然是铁钉。试图追踪1695年以来铁钉价格的变化似乎有些荒谬，但研究铁钉这个问题却完全合理。

I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price. I am an economist, after all. After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I've learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it's the cheap technologies that change the world.

我毫不避讳自己对日常物品一个特定特征的痴迷：价格。毕竟我是个经济学家。在写了两本关于发明史的书之后，我学到的一件事是：虽然那些令人着迷的复杂技术获得了所有关注，但真正改变世界的却是廉价技术。

The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost — and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper. Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are poised to reclaim the global energy system.

古腾堡印刷机改变文明，不是通过改变书写的本质，而是通过改变书写的成本——而如果没有一种常被忽视的技术（纸张）带来书写载体价格的同步暴跌，印刷机也难有作为。太阳能电池板在变便宜之前只有一些小众用途；如今它们正准备重塑全球能源体系。

细节推断题
答案 D
The Romans buried the nails probably for the sake of ___.罗马人埋钉子可能是为了___。
[A] saving them for future use将它们保存以备将来使用
[B] keeping them from rusting防止它们生锈
[C] letting them grow in value让它们增值
[D] hiding them from the locals
💡 考场思路题干 Romans buried the nails 定位第二段。关键句："they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron"——不想让当地人拿到武器级铁。get their hands on = 得到。
逐项分析 [A] 留着以后用 → 原文说撤退匆忙，不是存起来；
[B] 防止生锈 → 无中生有；
[C] 让它们升值 → 无中生有；
[D] 藏起来不让当地人拿到 → 正确，对应 didn't want...getting their hands on。
核心词汇
weapon-grade adj. 武器级的
hoard n. 窖藏
withdrawal n. 撤退
millennia n. 千年（复数）
get one's hands on 弄到手
rushed adj. 匆忙的
22
例证题
答案 D
The example of early 17th-century Virginians is used to ___.17世纪初弗吉尼亚人的例子被用来___。
[A] highlight the thriftiness of early American colonists凸显早期美洲殖民者的节俭
[B] illustrate the high status of blacksmiths in that period展现那一时期铁匠的崇高地位
[C] contrast the attitudes of different civilisations towards nails对比不同文明对钉子的态度
[D] show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time
💡 考场思路例证题答案=例子前后的论点句。例子后一句："burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was"——烧掉房子只为回收钉子，说明制钉技术有多宝贵。
逐项分析 [A] 夸殖民者节俭 → 例子不是为了夸节俭；
[B] 说铁匠地位高 → 过度推断；
[C] 对比不同文明态度 → 只有一个例子，没有对比；
[D] 说明制钉技术珍贵 → 正确，scarce, costly, valuable = preciousness。
题型铁律例证题（be used to / is mentioned to）答案永远不在例子本身，而在例子前后的论点句。

答案 A
What played the major role in lowering the price of nails after the late 1700s?在19世纪后期之后，什么在降低指甲价格方面发挥了主要作用？
[A] Increased productivity.

💡 考场思路定位第四段。原文："most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails"——主要功劳在于更高效的生产方法。more efficient ways = increased productivity。
逐项分析 [A] 生产率提高 → 正确；
[B] 新能源 → 原文 cheaper energy 只是 partly；
[C] 市场竞争 → 未提及；
[D] 原材料降价 → cheaper iron 也只是 partly，不是 major role。

细节推断题
答案 B
It can be learned from Paragraph 5 that nails ___.从第5段可以了解到，钉子___。

[B] 自罗马时代基本没变 → 正确；
[C] 研究少 → 无中生有；
[D] 最重要发明之一 → 过度拔高。

Text 2   从狩猎采集社会学育儿（26–30）

Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested. The idea is based on studies of communities such as the Kung of Botswana, where each child is cared for by many adults. Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones and "baby-wearing", in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm.

研究人员提出，从非洲狩猎采集者那里获得的育儿秘诀，可能是养出更快乐孩子的关键。这一观点基于对博茨瓦纳昆人等社群的研究，在这些社群中每个孩子由许多成年人共同照料。昆人四岁大的孩子就会帮忙照顾更小的孩子，而"背婴"（用背带把婴儿背在身上）被视为常态。

According to Dr Nikhil Chaudhary, an evolutionary anthropologist at Cambridge University, these practices, known as alloparenting, could lead to less anxiety for children and parents.

剑桥大学进化人类学家尼基尔·乔杜里博士表示，这些被称为"共同育儿"的做法可能会减轻孩子和父母的焦虑。

Dr Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life. In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people's home with a nursery. The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting. Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years to mirror the unsupervised mixed-age playgroups in hunter-gatherer communities.

儿童精神病学家安妮·斯瓦内普尔博士认为，有办法将这些做法融入西方生活。在德国，一个项目将养老院与幼儿园配对。养老院住户帮忙照看孩子，这种安排类似于共同育儿。另一项措施是鼓励不同年级的孩子建立友谊，以效仿狩猎采集社会中那种无人看管的混龄游戏小组。

In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history. This abrupt shift to an "intensive mothering narrative", which suggests that mothers should manage childcare alone, was likely to have been harmful. "Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences," they wrote.

研究人员在《儿童心理学与精神病学杂志》上发表的一篇论文中指出，西方核心家庭是一项打破进化史的新近发明。这种向"密集母亲叙事"的突然转变（即认为母亲应独自承担育儿责任）很可能是有害的。他们写道："这种叙事会导致母亲疲惫，并产生危险后果。"

By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child's care. One previous study looked at the Efe people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour.

相比之下，在狩猎采集社会中，父母以外的成年人可以提供孩子近一半的照料。此前一项研究考察了刚果民主共和国的埃菲人。研究发现，婴儿在18周大时平均每天有14个共同照料者，每小时被传递给不同的照料者8次。

Chaudhary said that parents now had less childcare support from family and social networks than during most of humans' evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to a child's wellbeing. An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers — this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three.

乔杜里说，如今父母从家庭和社会网络获得的育儿支持比人类进化史上大部分时期都要少，但引入额外的照料者可以减轻压力和母亲抑郁，这可能对孩子的福祉产生连锁益处。狩猎采集社会的婴儿可能有十几个照料者——这与英国托儿所形成鲜明对比，英国规定2-3岁儿童的师生比为1:4。

While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western "instructive teaching", where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents might "also enhance their own social development".

狩猎采集社会的孩子在混龄游戏小组中通过观察和模仿学习，而研究人员表示，西方那种要求学生静坐的"说教式教学"可能导致注意力缺陷多动障碍等问题。乔杜里说，英国应该探索让年长子女帮父母带孩子是否"也能促进他们自身的社交发展"。

26

[C] 教大孩子育儿 → 片面；
[D] 父母背婴儿 → 这是 baby-wearing，不是 alloparenting。

Text 3   AI生成艺术与艺术家维权（31–35）

A Polish digital artist who uses classical painting styles to create dreamy fantasy landscapes, Greg Rutkowski has made illustrations for games such as Dungeons & Dragons: The Gathering. And he's become a sudden hit in the new world of text-to-image AI generation.

波兰数字艺术家格雷格·鲁特科夫斯基用古典绘画风格创作梦幻般的奇幻风景，曾为《龙与地下城： Gathering》等游戏绘制插图。如今他在文生图AI新世界中突然走红。

His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new open-source AI art generator Stable Diffusion. The tool, along with other popular image-generation AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts. For example, type in "Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon" and Rutkowski's system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski's style.

他独特的风格如今是新开源AI艺术生成器Stable Diffusion中最常用的提示词之一。该工具与其他流行的图像生成AI模型一样，允许任何人根据文本提示词创作令人印象深刻的图像。例如，输入"持剑、带着魔法火球球与恶龙搏斗的巫师"，Rutkowski的系统就会生成与Rutkowski风格作品相差无几的图像。

But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the Internet, without artist consent and proper attribution to artists. As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright. And artists like Rutkowski have had enough.

但这些开源程序是通过从互联网上抓取图像构建的，未经艺术家同意，也没有适当署名。因此，它们引发了关于伦理和版权的棘手问题。而像鲁特科夫斯基这样的艺术家已经受够了。

According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million Stable Diffusion images and prompts, Rutkowski's name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times. Rutkowski initially was surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences. Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published. The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but it wasn't his.

据追踪了超过1000万张Stable Diffusion图像和提示词的Lexica网站统计，鲁特科夫斯基的名字被用作提示词约9.3万次。鲁特科夫斯基起初很惊讶，但认为这可能是触达新观众的好方法。后来他搜索自己的名字，想看看自己的作品是否已被发表。结果搜出来的作品署着他的名字，但不是他画的。

"It's been just a month. What about in a year? I probably won't be able to find my work out there because the internet will be flooded with AI art," Rutkowski said. "That's concerning."

"才一个月而已。一年后会怎样？我可能再也找不到自己的作品了，因为互联网将充斥着AI艺术。"鲁特科夫斯基说，"这令人担忧。"

Other artists besides Rutkowski have been surprised by the apparent popularity of their work in text-to-image generators — and some are now fighting back.

除鲁特科夫斯基外，其他艺术家也对自己作品在文生图生成器中的明显受欢迎程度感到惊讶——有些人现在开始反击。

Karla Ortiz, an illustrator based in San Francisco who found her work in Stable Diffusion's data set, has been raising awareness about the issues around AI art and copyright. Artists say they risk losing income as people start using AI-generated images based on copyrighted material for commercial purposes. But it's also a lot more personal, Ortiz says, arguing that art is so closely linked to a person, it could raise data protection and privacy problems.

旧金山插画师卡拉·奥尔蒂斯发现自己的作品出现在Stable Diffusion的数据集中，她一直在提高人们对AI艺术和版权问题的认识。艺术家们表示，随着人们开始将基于受版权保护材料生成的AI图像用于商业目的，他们面临收入损失的风险。奥尔蒂斯说，这还关乎更深层的个人问题，艺术与人紧密相连，可能引发数据保护和隐私问题。

"There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this," says Ortiz. The group is in its early days of mobilisation, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulation. One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.

"艺术家行业内部正在形成一个联盟，研究如何解决或缓解这个问题，"奥尔蒂斯说。该组织仍处于动员初期，可能包括推动新政策或监管。一个建议是，AI模型可以用公共领域的图像进行训练，AI公司可以与博物馆和艺术家建立合作关系，奥尔蒂斯说。

Text 4   切萨皮克湾湿地保护（36–40）

The miracle of the Chesapeake Bay lies not in its depths, but in the complexity of its natural construction, the interaction of fresh and saline water and the mix of land and water. The shallows provide homes for hundreds of species while storing floodwaters, filtering pollutants from water, and protecting nearby communities from potentially destructive storm surges.

切萨皮克湾的奇迹不在于其深度，而在于其自然构造的复杂性——淡水与咸水的交汇、陆地与水域的交融。浅滩为数百物种提供栖息地，同时储存洪水、过滤水中污染物，并保护附近社区免受破坏性风暴潮的侵袭。

All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways. Specifically, a 5-4 majority decided that wetlands protected by the EPA under its Clean Water Act authority must have a "continuous surface connection" to bodies of water. This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests often at odds with environmental rules. And it carries "significant repercussions" for water quality and flood control throughout the United States, as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed.

上月底，美国最高法院在一起爱达荷州案件中作出裁决，大幅削弱了美国环保署（EPA）监管湿地和水道的权力，这一切都被置于巨大风险之中。具体而言，5:4的多数意见裁定，EPA根据《清洁水法》授权保护的湿地必须与水体有"连续的地表连接"。监管范围的缩小是建筑商、矿业运营商和其他经常与环境规则发生冲突的商业利益集团的胜利。正如大法官布雷特·卡瓦诺所观察到的，这对全美国的水质和防洪都带来了"重大影响"。

In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections. But that's a very shortsighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay. The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don't respect state boundaries. The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends to Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware. Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v. EPA? Perhaps some, but all? That seems unlikely.

在马里兰州，好消息是有许多州级法律提供湿地保护。但这是一种非常短视的看法，尤其是在切萨皮克湾问题上。现实是，水以及随水而来的污染物不尊重州界。切萨皮克湾的流域面积达6.4万平方英里，延伸至弗吉尼亚、宾夕法尼亚、纽约、西弗吉尼亚、哥伦比亚特区和特拉华州。这些辖区会提供Sackett案中被拒绝的同等保护吗？也许有些会，但全部？似乎不太可能。

It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors. And it's a reminder that the EPA's involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states. Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren't thinking about next year's blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impacts downstream.

把这类法院裁决仅仅看作维护地主权利，实在太容易了，也具有误导性，因为其后果对邻居们可能如此严重。这也提醒人们，EPA对切萨皮克湾项目的长期参与至关重要，它是超越邻州财力雄厚特殊利益集团影响的手段。举个有说服力的例子：宾夕法尼亚州的农民在决定是否在田里施肥时，并不会想到马里兰明年的蓝蟹收成，但流入附近小溪的径流会对下游产生巨大影响。

And so we would also call on state lawmakers from Richmond to Albany to consider reviewing their own wetlands protections and see for themselves the enormous stakes involved. We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes so shallow you could not paddle a boat across them but teaming with aquatic life. It's worth the scenic drive.

因此，我们也呼吁从里士满到奥尔巴尼的州议员们审视各自的湿地保护措施，亲自看看其中牵涉的巨大利害关系。我们可以邀请他们参观多切斯特县的黑水国家野生动物保护区，那里白头鹰翱翔在潮汐湿地上空，湿地浅到划船都过不去，却充满水生生物。这趟风景之旅值得一走。

36

What can be inferred about the EPA's involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program?关于美国环保署参与切萨皮克湾计划，可以推断出什么？

Part B · 新题型信息匹配（41–45）

【题目】阅读关于美国博物馆归还文物的五位评论者观点，从A–G中为(41)–(45)匹配观点。两个多余选项。

(41) Hannah：在尼日利亚，人们无法去史密森尼看贝宁青铜器。这些文物应作为他们文化遗产和民族自豪感的一部分提供给他们。它们在美国博物馆里除了当猎奇物件毫无用处。

Hannah 核心观点：文物在原属国才有意义，在西方博物馆只是猎奇品。

(42) Buck：精确复制品可以大量制作。博物馆和政府可以探索用复制品解决归还问题。展品讲述的故事才重要，货币价值次要。

Buck 核心观点：复制品足以替代，重要的是故事不是原件。

(43) Sara：博物馆文物能激发学习。但无论租借、合法购买还是条约取得都应被认可，窃取他族文物是可憎的。

Sara 核心观点：获取文物的方式必须正当合法，偷窃不可接受。

(44) Victor：古代艺术应归还原属国。外国无权扣留。原属国安保可能不如外国，但看看波士顿加德纳博物馆被盗案——哪里都不安全。

Victor 核心观点：安保担忧不能成为不归还的借口。

(45) Julia：为什么美国人比尼日利亚人更有权看贝宁青铜器？为什么伦敦人能随时看埃尔金大理石而雅典人不行？"西方更能保护文物"这个假设站不住脚。

Julia 核心观点：反对归还者的逻辑本身就有缺陷。

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
It is clear that the countries of origin have never been compensated for the stolen artifacts.
显然，文物原属国从未因被窃走的文物得到过任何补偿。
B
It is a flawed line of reasoning to argue against returning artifacts to their countries of origin.
反对将文物归还原属国，这种论证思路本身是有缺陷的。
C
Museum visitors can still learn as much from artifacts' copies after the originals are returned.
原件归还之后，博物馆参观者仍能从文物的复制品中学到同样多的东西。
D
Reproductions, even if perfectly made, cannot take the place of the authentic objects.
复制品即便制作得再完美，也无法取代真品。
E
The real value of artifacts can only be recognized in their countries of origin rather than anywhere else.
文物的真正价值只能在原属国、而非任何其他地方被认识。
F
Ways to get artifacts from other countries must be decent and lawful.
从他国获取文物的方式必须正当且合法。
G
Concern over security is no excuse for refusing to return artifacts to their countries of origin.
对安全的担忧，不能成为拒绝将文物归还原属国的借口。
41
匹配题
答案 E
匹配[E] 文物的真正价值只有在其原属国才能被认识。→ 对应Hannah说文物在国外只是猎奇品。
42
匹配题
答案 C
匹配[C] 原作归还后，参观者仍能从复制品中学到同样多。→ 对应Buck说复制品+故事才重要。
43
匹配题
答案 F
匹配[F] 获取文物的方式必须正当合法。→ 对应Sara说合法购买/条约可以，偷窃可憎。
44
匹配题
答案 G
匹配[G] 对安保的担忧不能成为拒绝归还的借口。→ 对应Victor说哪里都不安全。
45
匹配题
答案 B
匹配[B] 反对归还原属国的论证思路有缺陷。→ 对应Julia连续反问指出对方逻辑漏洞。
干扰项[A]原属国从未获补偿（未提）；[D]完美复制品也不能替代真品（与Buck相反）。
Part C · 英译汉逐句翻译（46–50）
46
翻译
They sometimes travel more than sixty miles to find food or water, and are very good at working out where other elephants are—even when they are out of sight.
它们有时跋涉六十多英里寻找食物或水，并且非常善于判断其他大象的位置——即使那些大象不在视线范围内。
采分点① travel more than sixty miles 跋涉六十多英里；② work out 判断/弄清楚；③ out of sight 视线之外。
47
翻译
The researchers are convinced that the elephants always know precisely where they are in relation to all the resources they need, and can therefore take shortcuts, as well as following familiar routes.
研究人员确信，大象总是准确知道自己相对于所需全部资源的位置，因此既能走捷径，也能循着熟悉的路线行进。
采分点① be convinced that 确信；② in relation to 相对于；③ take shortcuts 走捷径。
48
翻译
One possibility was that they merely used their eyes and tried out the plants they found, but that would probably result in a lot of wasted time and energy, not least because their eyesight is actually not very good.
一种可能是，它们仅仅依靠视觉并尝试所发现的植物，但这很可能浪费大量时间和精力，尤其是因为它们的视力实际上并不好。
采分点① try out 尝试；② not least because 尤其是因为（高频考点）；③ eyesight 视力。
49
翻译
The volatile chemicals produced by plants can be carried a long way, and they are very characteristic: each plant or tree has its own particular odor signature.
植物产生的挥发性化学物质可以传播很远，而且具有特异性：每一种植物或树木都有自己独特的气味标识。
采分点① volatile chemicals 挥发性化学物质；② characteristic 特异的；③ odor signature 气味标识。
50
翻译
The experiment showed that elephants may well use smell to identify patches of trees that are good to eat, and secondly to assess the quality of the trees within each patch.
实验表明，大象很可能利用嗅觉来识别哪些树林值得取食，其次还能评估每片树林中树木的质量。
采分点① may well 很可能；② patches of trees 成片树林；③ assess 评估。
Section III · Writing 写作
Part A 小作文（10分）— 建议信

原题指令 Directions

Your international student friend Paul is going to give an oral report on ancient Chinese scientists but does not know how to prepare it. Write an email to offer him some help. You should write about 100 words. Do not sign your own name at the end of the email. Use "Li Ming" instead.

【译文】你的留学生朋友保罗准备做一个关于中国古代科学家的口头报告，却不知如何准备。写一封电子邮件为他提供帮助。字数约100词。邮件末尾不要署自己的名字，使用“李明”代替。

题目

国际学生Paul要做关于中国古代科学家的口头报告，不知如何准备，写邮件求助。约100词，落款Li Ming。

审题

① 格式：邮件；② 语气：友好乐于助人；③ 内容：2-3条具体建议。

参考范文

Dear Paul,

I was delighted to receive your email and would like to offer some practical advice on preparing your oral report on an ancient Chinese scientist.

First, I suggest you choose Bi Sheng, the inventor of movable-type printing, whose story is both landmark and compelling. Second, consult authoritative sources such as Joseph Needham's works, which are reliable and accessible. Finally, rehearse your presentation in front of a mirror or record yourself, so you can polish both your content and delivery.

I hope these suggestions help. Wish you a brilliant performance!

Yours sincerely, Li Ming

【译文】

亲爱的保罗：

很高兴收到你的邮件，想就你准备关于中国古代科学家的口头报告提几点实用建议。

首先，建议你选择活字印刷术的发明者毕昇，他的故事既具里程碑意义又引人入胜。其次，可参考如李约瑟著作等权威资料，可靠且易得。最后，对着镜子或录下自己反复演练，以便打磨内容与表达。

希望这些建议有用。祝你表现出色！

谨上，李明

Part B 大作文（20分）— 图表作文

原题指令 Directions

Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following chart. In your essay, you should 1) describe the chart briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. Picture: The illustration, together with its chart, presents a thought-provoking phenomenon: people are increasingly turning to digital means for daily learning and entertainment, while the chart shows a steady rise in the proportion of citizens using online platforms over the past decade.

【译文】根据下面的chart写一篇160–200词的短文。文中应： 1）简要描述chart；2）说明其寓意；3）给出你的评论。 请在答题卡2上工整书写。 图文共同呈现一个发人深省的现象：人们日常学习与娱乐日益转向数字化方式，而图表显示过去十年间使用网络平台的公民比例稳步上升。

审题框架

三段式：①简要描述图画+图表；②阐释含义；③给出评论。160-200词。

参考范文

The vivid illustration and its accompanying chart jointly present a thought-provoking phenomenon. As the picture shows, people are increasingly turning to digital means for daily learning and entertainment, while the chart reveals a steady rise in the proportion of citizens using online platforms over the past decade.

The implied message is that technology is reshaping our habits more deeply than we realize. Several factors account for this trend. To begin with, with the rapid development of society and the widespread use of smart devices, access to information has never been easier. In addition, relevant policies and a supportive social atmosphere have further encouraged this shift, making digital services an integral part of modern life.

From my perspective, this trend is generally beneficial. On the one hand, it boosts individual efficiency and access to knowledge; on the other, it promotes social progress. Only by embracing it wisely can we look forward to a brighter future.

【译文】

生动的图画与 accompanying 图表共同呈现了一个发人深省的现象。如图画所示，人们日益借助数字化方式满足日常学习与娱乐需求；而图表显示，过去十年中借助在线平台的民众比例持续上升。

其隐含的道理是：科技正在以超出我们想象的程度重塑习惯。多种因素促成这一趋势。首先，随着社会快速发展与智能设备普及，获取信息从未如此便捷；其次，相关政策和友善的社会氛围进一步推动了这种转变，使数字服务成为现代生活不可或缺的一部分。

在我看来，这一趋势总体是有益的。一方面，它提升了个人效率与知识获取；另一方面，也推动社会进步。唯有明智地拥抱它，我们才能迎接更光明的未来。
